articles.title: InnoParks veteran to lead Hung Shui Kiu Park
articles.excerpt: The Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park Company has appointed Yiu Hing-leung as its first chief executive for a three-year term…
articles.fullText:
The Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park Company has appointed Yiu Hing-leung as its first chief executive for a three-year term starting December 1.

His appointment followed an open recruitment process and received the approval of the SAR chief executive, the company said.

According to authorities, Yiu has spent more than three decades in the technology and industrial sectors.

He previously held senior roles at Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation, including chief corporate development officer and head of innofacturing.

While there, he drove the conversion of industrial estates into "InnoParks" and oversaw projects involving technology and industry clusters and incubation programmes.

Jeffrey Lam, chairman of the park company’s board of directors, said Yiu’s experience, business contacts and understanding of Hong Kong’s industrial development made him a strong fit for the role.

"I have every confidence that, leveraging his expertise and years of experience in driving new industrialisation, Dr Yiu will be able to lead the park company in attracting a high-value-added and diverse range of industries to set up operations and building a thriving industry ecosystem in the long term," he said in a statement.

Lam also said accelerating the Northern Metropolis is a key objective under Hong Kong’s first five-year plan and that the government-owned company is an important tool for advancing industry there through varied approaches.

The company is responsible for developing and operating the roughly 27.5-hectare Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park.

Its transport links and proximity to Qianhai in Shenzhen are expected to help attract high-value and smart production, including pharmaceutical manufacturing and food processing.

The company said it began operating after its board was appointed in the middle of the year and was now working actively to attract enterprises and investment.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK stocks rally as Beijing brings in 'national team'
articles.excerpt: Mainland stocks leapt to their largest gains in more than two years on Friday and the yuan rallied after Beijing…
articles.fullText:
Mainland stocks leapt to their largest gains in more than two years on Friday and the yuan rallied after Beijing vowed to strengthen the role of the state-backed "national team" in helping to stabilise a market that has struggled this year.

The rising tide up north saw the benchmark Hang Seng Index in Hong Kong surge as well, shooting up 467 points, or 2.1 percent, to close trading at 22,694 on turnover of HK$257.14 billion.

The tech index soared 220 points, or 6.5 percent, to 3,637 while the China enterprises index rose 150 points, or two percent, to 7,644.

The gains were even more pronounced on the mainland, with the Shanghai Composite Index, lately languishing around 17-month lows, surging 129 points, or 3.73 percent, to close at 3,606 on turnover of 929.77 billion yuan.

The Shenzhen Component Index skyrocketed 729 points, or 7.24 percent, to 10,814 on turnover of 1.07 trillion yuan while the ChiNext Index soared 254 points, or 11.61 percent, to 2,443 on turnover of 544.05 billion yuan.

The "national team" is markets' nickname for state-backed investors, usually led by Central Huijin, the domestic unit of sovereign wealth fund China Investment Corp, which are often buyers at times of market stress.

The Star semiconductor index jumped by a near-record 19.5 percent.

"This morning, the national team was already starting to accelerate its exercise, and the market went all out during afternoon trading," MIB Securities HK strategist Benjamin Ho said.

"What we need to see is policy and supportive measures that trickle down to the broader economy."

Winnie Wu, Bank of America Global Research, Hong Kong, said "with very depressed valuations and the consensus bearishness on China tech, it actually doesn't take too much for a relief rally.

"The State Council is essentially giving that confidence to say that we care about the market, we'll stabilise the market, and bring in long-term capital.

"We think giving this message from the very top level, ie the State Council, is an attempt to re-instill some confidence, stabilise liquidity and stabilise the trajectory of the market.

"So we think there's probably this awareness that AI is strategically, economically and financially very important, and they don't want to see a big fallout in this space."

China Everbright Securities International, Hong Kong, strategist Kenny Ng called it "a shot in the arm for markets."

"Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on," he said.

"At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south.

"It's obvious that A-shares have reached a level that's gotten the regulators' attention too – that sends the market a pretty clear signal.

"But there's a lot of news affecting the market... and so I don't think the development from here depends entirely on this one factor."

In Tokyo, the Nikkei share average rose 1,211 points, or 2.11 percent, to close at 58,711, extending its weekly gain, as investors scooped up recently battered AI-related stocks and domestic-focused shares found buyers amid market volatility.

The broader Topix ended 64 points, or 1.73 percent, at 3,815.

In Seoul, the Kospi closed up 204 points, or 4.34 percent, at 4,915 to end a week of heightened volatility with 0.9 percent gains, supported by hopes of policy measures to stabilise the market, with gains of 4.55 percent for chipmaker Samsung Electronics and 5.41 percent for SK Hynix. (With contributions from Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Abby Choi murder was carefully planned, court hears
articles.excerpt: The murder of celebrity Abby Choi had been carefully planned and the killing stemmed from a financial dispute over a…
articles.fullText:
The murder of celebrity Abby Choi had been carefully planned and the killing stemmed from a financial dispute over a luxury apartment, the High Court heard on Friday.

In her closing submissions, senior counsel Charlotte Draycott said the three defendants – Choi's ex-husband Alex Kwong, his brother Anthony Kwong and their father Kwong Kau – each had a role.

They had, she said, bought tools and other equipment a few days in advance, ready to act when the opportunity arose.

Draycott said Choi's relationship with Kwong Kau had already broken down badly before the incident and suggested Choi had planned to sell a flat on Kadoorie Hill that is believed to be linked to her death.

The senior counsel held up Choi's handbag for the jury to see.

Showing clear signs of damage, including holes and bloodstains, the bag, Draycott suggested, had been raised by Choi to protect herself during a hammer attack, during which the bag was struck.

Choi was reported missing in February 2023.

Three days later, parts of her dismembered body were found at a rented village house in Tai Po.

Her ex-husband, his father and brother deny the murder charges, but have admitted preventing the lawful burial of her body.

The defence will present its closing submissions on Monday.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Top court quashes flag desecration convictions
articles.excerpt: The Court of Final Appeal on Friday unanimously quashed the convictions of a young man with autism for desecrating the…
articles.fullText:
The Court of Final Appeal on Friday unanimously quashed the convictions of a young man with autism for desecrating the national flag and the SAR flag, ruling that the prosecution had never proved he intended to insult the flags as symbols.

Wong Chun-lok, who was 19 at the time of the offences, was convicted by a magistrate of one count of desecrating the national flag and two counts of desecrating the SAR flag, and was sentenced to detention in a rehabilitation centre.

The court heard that on National Day in 2022, Wong pulled down one national flag and four regional flags at three locations in Sham Shui Po by bending the metal flagpoles on which they were mounted.

Wong was diagnosed with autism at the age of three and also has attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and a hypersensitivity to visual stimuli.

His mother gave evidence of a similar incident in 2018 when he pulled down banners outside a shop because he was disturbed by them.

Delivering the judgement, Justice Joseph Fok held that both the national flag offence and the SAR flag offence require proof that the defendant intended to undermine the dignity of the flag as a symbol.

Recklessness is not enough, according to the judgement.

"The less egregious an act of desecration, the more cogent might the evidence need to be in order to establish an intention to desecrate the flag in question," the judgement said.

Justice Fok found the magistrate's treatment of the mental element was brief and the deputy judge who heard the appeal had given a "wholly inadequate" analysis, simply relying on the magistrate's findings and CCTV footage without explaining how an intention to desecrate could be drawn from it.

He said the deputy judge had omitted evidence that Wong had done nothing directly to the flags themselves and had said nothing showing antipathy towards them as symbols; his explanation was that the sight of rows of fluttering flags made him uncomfortable.

The deputy judge was also found to have wrongly refused to admit new evidence, comprising reports from a psychiatrist, two clinical psychologists and an occupational therapist, which set out the link between Wong's condition and his impulsive behaviour towards the flags.

Justice Fok said the reports were credible, admissible and relevant, and that had they been admitted the court could not have been satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that Wong intended to desecrate the flags.

The failure to properly assess the mental element, together with the wrongful exclusion of the new evidence, amounted to substantial and grave injustice.

"There is no question of ordering a re-trial," according to the judgement.

The court said there was no reasonable prospect of conviction, the prosecution had not sought a retrial, and Wong had already served his period of detention.

The case was heard by Chief Justice Andrew Cheung, permanent judges Roberto Ribeiro, Joseph Fok, Johnson Lam, and non-permanent judge William Young.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'Mushroom killer' asks top court to hear appeal
articles.excerpt: An Australian woman dubbed the mushroom killer for using deadly fungi to murder relatives has asked Australia's top court to…
articles.fullText:
An Australian woman dubbed the mushroom killer for using deadly fungi to murder relatives has asked Australia's top court to hear an appeal of her conviction and life sentence, local media reported on Friday.

Erin Patterson, 52, was last year found guilty of murdering her husband's parents and aunt in 2023, deliberately lacing their beef Wellington lunch with lethal death cap mushrooms.

The strange nature of the "mushroom murders" fuelled intense global interest, with Patterson's 11-week trial drawing more publicity than almost any other Australian case in recent memory.

Patterson maintained her triple murder convictions were a "miscarriage of justice", urging the Court of Appeal in Victoria State to either set her free or have the case heard again.

But that court last month not only threw out her bid to have the convictions quashed, it found her "carefully planned and deliberate" killings deserved a life sentence.

She has now launched an appeal with Australia's top court in a last-ditch push for freedom, Australia's national broadcaster ABC and daily newspaper The Age reported, citing sources.

She is appealing both her conviction and her life sentence, they said.

The High Court must now decide whether to grant her appeal, which could take months.

Patterson's lawyers have argued she suffered a "substantial" miscarriage of justice in her trial, as well as "oppressive" cross-examination and unfair decisions on the admission of evidence.

But the court last month found her "carefully planned and deliberate" killings deserved an even harsher sentence. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Police, retailers warn of data breaches and scams
articles.excerpt: Authorities and retailers have warned that weak application programming interface (API) security and AI-driven attacks are fuelling a rise in…
articles.fullText:
Authorities and retailers have warned that weak application programming interface (API) security and AI-driven attacks are fuelling a rise in data breaches and precision scams.

The warning came at a joint press conference by the police, the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD), the Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre and the Retail Management Association, which said the threats cut across industries and borders.

Superintendent Rachel Hui of the cyber security and technology crime bureau disclosed that a single breach at a chain retailer in November exposed the data of more than one million customers.

"These over one million hits were actually done within several days. It would never be done by a human. It is not a human speed," she said.

Hui said police were taking a proactive approach, including monitoring the dark web for leaked data.

"We can find that there are affected organisations that ... have never reported [these cases] to the police or the PCPD, but they have their data leaked or have something left on the dark web," she said.

"So what we are actually doing is to work with [them] to proactively alert those organisations to plug their loopholes."

The data breach of the retailer was among 11 cases linked to API vulnerabilities out of 30 cyber incidents that the police handled between October 1 and November 24.

API keys, the police said, are often written directly into app or website source code, allowing attackers to extract them and access backend databases when identity checks and rate limits are weak.

The PCPD said it had received 330 data-breach notifications by November 25, up nearly 50 percent from 223 in the same period last year.

Of these breaches, 156 involved hacking, more than double the 75 cases a year earlier.

Meanwhile, the coordination centre said it had handled more than 14,000 cybersecurity incidents in the first 10 months of the year, up more than seven percent year on year, with phishing remaining the most serious category.

Officers warned that leaked order details are increasingly being used for precision scams.

Fraudsters pose as customer service staff, cite real purchase information, claim a refund or compensation is due, and then send fake links or apps to steal banking passwords, one-time codes and credit-card data.

Police stressed that genuine refunds do not require bank passwords or verification codes, and urged residents to verify requests through official channels, use the Scameter search engine and call the anti-scam hotline if in doubt.

The agencies urged companies to adopt a “zero trust” approach, inventory their systems and APIs, separate testing and production systems, patch vulnerabilities, monitor for abnormal activity and report breaches promptly.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Central Kowloon Bypass to fully open Dec 6 at 7am
articles.excerpt: The Central Kowloon Bypass will be fully commissioned at 7am on December 6, authorities said on Friday. The final section…
articles.fullText:
The Central Kowloon Bypass will be fully commissioned at 7am on December 6, authorities said on Friday.

The final section to open will be the Kowloon Bay section, an approximately 3.4-kilometre dual two-lane trunk road that includes a 3.1-kilometre tunnel.

Its completion marks the finishing piece of Route 6.

The Yau Ma Tei section, which opened last year, is currently toll-free.

Once the bypass is fully open, however, a flat toll of HK$8 will apply to all vehicles through the HKeToll system.

Leung Sai-ho, Deputy Commissioner for Transport (Planning and Technical Services), said he hoped that once the entire route opens, it would divert traffic from existing major corridors such as the Kwun Tong Bypass.

"We have already observed a 20 percent diversion effect after the opening of the Yau Ma Tei section," he said.

"Our team will keep closely monitoring the traffic situation through our traffic surveillance system and ad-hoc deployed survey teams to see whether traffic flow is performing according to our expectations."

Authorities added the Yau Ma Tei section would be closed from midnight to 7am on the opening day for final preparations, including updating traffic signs and road markings as well as carrying out preparatory work for the HKeToll system.

Once fully commissioned, peak-hour journeys between Tseung Kwan O town centre and Yau Ma Tei are expected to be cut from 65 minutes before the project to about 12 minutes.

Route 6 links major areas including the West Kowloon Cultural District, the Kai Tak Development and Cruise Terminal, and the Kowloon East central business district.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Hackers using AI to find loopholes: HKCERT
articles.excerpt: Artificial intelligence tools have made it easier for hackers to find and exploit system vulnerabilities, contributing to a recent rise…
articles.fullText:
Artificial intelligence tools have made it easier for hackers to find and exploit system vulnerabilities, contributing to a recent rise in cyber security incidents and data leaks in Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre (HKCERT) said on Friday.

Otto Lee, head of HKCERT at the Productivity Council, told an RTHK programme that 15,877 cyber security incident reports were recorded in 2025, up more than 20 percent and a record high, while 4,404 cases were logged in the third quarter of 2026 alone, a rise of about 15 percent year on year.

Lee attributed the trend to three factors: the rapid digital transformation of businesses, which now run websites, mobile apps, cloud services and payment systems; increasingly complex links between systems through application programming interfaces and third-party platforms; and a rise in supply chain attacks, where hackers use one compromised vendor as a springboard to hit several organisations at once.

"It's like a house that now has many doors. Hackers use AI tools to scan around the clock without interruption, so as long as one of those doors isn't locked properly, they can find a loophole and get in within minutes," Lee said.

He said AI was a major factor, noting that hacking tools previously had to be bought or built but now include AI agents that can be pointed at a domain or a file and automatically hunt for weaknesses.

"Building a fake website, therefore, is absolutely very simple; in a few minutes you can build a very similar one. Everyone can do it, as long as you use AI," he said, adding that the lower cost barrier had created room for profit.

Lee also said the growth in reported cases partly reflected greater awareness among organisations of the need to disclose incidents.

He said the most common weaknesses found in cases reported to HKCERT were unpatched systems, misconfigured databases that left data exposed online, a lack of multi-factor authentication, weak API authorisation, insufficient logging, and organisations holding on to large volumes of sensitive data long after it was needed.

He urged companies to treat incident response planning as a priority, warning that some firms had no back-ups at all, while others found their back-ups had been stolen or could not be restored.

For members of the public affected by a data leak, Lee advised them to check the scope of the breach and change their passwords, monitor their accounts and statements for unusual transactions, and be on guard against phishing and fraud, warning that hackers may wait some time before using leaked data.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Manufacturing profits rise at faster pace in China
articles.excerpt: Profit growth at China's industrial firms accelerated in October, supported by improving conditions in parts of the manufacturing sector, although…
articles.fullText:
Profit growth at China's industrial firms accelerated in October, supported by improving conditions in parts of the manufacturing sector, although broader economic momentum remained subdued.

With domestic demand yet to gain meaningful traction and continuing to weigh on corporate earnings, many firms have increasingly relied on overseas markets for growth, leaving them vulnerable to trade tensions and geopolitical risks.

Profits at industrial firms rose 20.1 percent from a year earlier last month, versus a 14.4 percent gain in September, data from the National Bureau of Statistics showed on Friday.

Profits were up 16 percent in the first 10 months, accelerating from a 15.5 percent increase in the January-September period,

Industrial earnings continued to show a sharp split, with profits in computer, telecommunications and other electronic equipment manufacturing doubling in the first 10 months, while furniture manufacturing posted a decline of 52.4 percent.

The uneven performance comes as Beijing has introduced a series of policy measures in recent months aimed at supporting economic activity, including steps to lower borrowing costs, increase liquidity in the financial system and channel financing to sectors such as technology, manufacturing and infrastructure.

Still, analysts say the impact of the policy support has been mixed, with weak household demand and lingering strains in the property sector continuing to drag on the broader recovery.

The outlook for exports, a key source of support for manufacturers this year, has meanwhile become less certain.

Concerns over potential tariff increases and other trade restrictions, particularly in the United States and the European Union, have raised questions about the sustainability of export-driven growth and the earnings prospects of firms dependent on overseas demand.

Industrial profit figures cover firms with annual revenue of at least 20 million yuan from main operations. (Reuters)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: NZ leader loses majority with centrists holding key
articles.excerpt: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition lost its parliamentary majority, final results from this month's election showed on…
articles.fullText:
New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition lost its parliamentary majority, final results from this month's election showed on Friday, plunging the country into political uncertainty with an insurgent centrist party set to play kingmaker.

Preliminary results of the November 7 poll had Luxon's National Party-led coalition clinging onto power.

But margins were so tight that his party lost two seats in the final results announced — leaving his coalition with the populist NZ First and the libertarian ACT one seat short of a majority.

Luxon declared he had a mandate to form the country's next government in the wake of this month's vote, bitterly fought and dominated by spiralling costs of living in the South Pacific country.

He has run a caretaker government since the November 7 poll.

But he will now need the backing of the centrist newcomers Opportunity, led by Qiulae Wong, if he wants to govern.

And if a deal isn't struck, the country could be headed for another election.

Pledging a kinder, gentler politics as well as action on climate change, her party became the first in decades to make parliament without a former cabinet minister leader.

Wong has vowed to work with whichever party has the largest number of seats.

But she has insisted that her party's "bottom lines" on climate change action, cost of living and cleaning up politics are non-negotiable.

Both Luxon and opposition Labour Party leader Chris Hipkins have held lengthy meetings with Wong in the wake of the election.

She said following the election this month that her win represented a sea change after a decade of rising populism and extremism worldwide.

"I think we are seeing a push globally for more pragmatic politics," she told journalists.

"We've seen that populism doesn't deliver results," she said.

With the official count in, it could take weeks or even months for the shape of New Zealand's new government to be decided.

Following the 2023 poll, it took more than six weeks for Luxon to form his coalition government with NZ First and ACT. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: HK and regional markets steadier amid AI uncertainty
articles.excerpt: Asian shares were set to end a bruising month on a steadier note as a holiday lull offered some respite…
articles.fullText:
Asian shares were set to end a bruising month on a steadier note as a holiday lull offered some respite from AI jitters, while the US dollar reigned supreme, riding a wave of safe-haven demand and rate hike bets towards a third month of gains.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index opened up 36 points, or 0.2 percent, at 22,263.

The China enterprises index inched seven points, or 0.1 percent, higher to 7,501 while the tech index was 16 points, or 0.5 percent, up at 3,433.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened up five points, or 0.2 percent, at 3,482.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 37 points, or 0.37 percent, higher at 10,121 while the ChiNext Index rose 13 points, or 0.59 percent, to 2,202.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 170 points, or 0.3 percent, up at 57,669 before gaining more ground to put the 225 benchmark 538 points up at one stage before lunch as the latest data on Friday showed core inflation in Tokyo hit a 16-month high in November, bolstering the case for an interest rate hike from the Bank of Japan as soon as next month.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 17 points, or 0.37 percent, up at 4,728 and rose after a brief dip to be 94 points higher at one stage before noon, led by a rebound in chipmakers after the country's central bank raised interest rates as expected and sharply upgraded its growth forecasts.

The gains came as oil prices were headed for the first weekly rise in four on renewed concerns about supply disruptions.

Brent crude futures slipped 0.4 percent on Friday to US$96.14 a barrel, but were still up 3.9 percent for the week.

For the month, they were down 18 percent.

"Barring a big shock that severely rattles a thin market, November is practically in the books and the markets limp into December where a seasonal 'Santa Rally' currently appears elusive," said Kyle Rodda, a senior analyst at Capital.com.

"For as long as the markets remain unsure about the growth trajectory for AI and lack clarity about where US rates may peak, uncertainty and therefore volatility is liable to remain elevated."

Tech giant Nvidia remained a source of unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade.

The chipmaker told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported.

The US dollar was headed to its third monthly gain on Friday, up 1.8 percent against its major peers at 103.8.

It has been supported by expectations that the Federal Reserve is almost certain to lift interest rates in December, as well as safe-haven flows from the selloff in equities.

Futures imply a 99 percent chance the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points in December, but speculation of a half-point increase has faded. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: 'Ukraine has no intention of spreading war to Libya'
articles.excerpt: Ukraine was not attempting to spread the war with Russia to Libyan shores by attacking two Russian ships off the…
articles.fullText:
Ukraine was not attempting to spread the war with Russia to Libyan shores by attacking two Russian ships off the coast of Benghazi, Kyiv's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said on Thursday.

In a post on X, Sybiga said he had called his Libyan counterpart Al-Taher Al-Baour to explain that "none of Ukraine's actions have ever been directed against Libya or the Libyan people, only against Russian military objects directly serving Russia's war".

"We have no intention of extending Russia's war against Ukraine to Libya or any other country," he added.

On Monday, Kyiv claimed responsibility for attacks on two Russian ships – one of which was sunk – at the weekend off the coast of Libya, in what appears to be a spillover of the war between Kyiv and Moscow.

In his X post, Sybiga "reaffirmed Ukraine's full support for Libya's sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as for efforts to reunify the country".

The incident has fuelled concerns about its potential political and security repercussions in Libya, a country divided between the UN-recognised government in Tripoli and a parallel administration based in Benghazi in the east.

The eastern administration is led by Khalifa Haftar, who maintains close military and strategic ties with Russia.

Tripoli had demanded explanations from Kyiv after the attack and denied any understanding with Ukraine, as speculation circulated about a possible role of the Tripoli authorities in the operations claimed by Kyiv.

The rival executive in the east has called for an international investigation into an alleged Ukrainian military presence in Libya.

The UN mission in Libya also condemned the attacks, calling for an independent investigation and urging respect for Libyan sovereignty. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Bournemouth, AC Milan rally to wins in Europa League
articles.excerpt: Ten-man Bournemouth fought back to maintain their 100-percent record in the Europa League with a 2-1 victory at Celta Vigo…
articles.fullText:
Ten-man Bournemouth fought back to maintain their 100-percent record in the Europa League with a 2-1 victory at Celta Vigo on Thursday, while AC Milan overturned a two-goal deficit to defeat Olympiakos.

The fifth round of matches was overshadowed by clashes between Georgian police and Besiktas fans which caused the Turkish club's match against Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Batumi to be temporarily suspended.

Marco Rose's Bournemouth notched a 10th successive win in all competitions despite finding themselves a goal and a man down in Spain.

The Premier League club, playing in Europe for the first time, now sit two points clear at the top of the 36-team table from second-placed Juventus, who saw off Cypriots Omonia 4-1 in Turin.

"My team, with one player down and 1-0 down, and this kind of energy and spirit. This is quite remarkable and amazing," said Bournemouth boss Rose.

"Sometimes I have the feeling with this team (that they) don't even need a coach."

Bournemouth could secure a top-eight finish and a last-16 berth when they host Viktoria Plzen, 4-0 winners over Benfica on Thursday, in two weeks' time.

Celta struck first in the 19th minute as Bournemouth allowed 39-year-old Iago Aspas time and space in the box to score his first goal since August.

The visitors were dealt another blow just three minutes later when Bafode Diakite was sent off following a VAR review for a tackle on Couhaib Driouech.

But the Cherries pulled themselves level two minutes after half-time as Alvaro Rodriguez headed in Amine Adli's cross.

The 10 men completed a remarkable turnaround with 12 minutes to play when Rayan slotted home Marcus Tavernier's square pass to cap a quick counter-attack.

Ruben Amorim's Milan, who had lost three of their opening four matches, gave their hopes of avoiding an embarrassing early exit a boost with a 4-2 victory at Olympiakos.

Milan were facing another huge blow to their bid to reach the knock-out phase when they were trailing to a Mike Maignan own goal and Joao Silva's 49th-minute strike.

But Omari Hutchinson's brilliant solo goal gave Milan a lifeline, and the former Ipswich winger then set up Alphadjo Cisse to equalise in the 63rd minute.

Hutchinson added another assist as he crossed for Christian Pulisic to volley home 19 minutes from time, before Diego Moreira's injury-time fourth, breathing life into the seven-time European champions' campaign.

"We have a lot of work to do to be a very strong team, but the spirit is there. It's the start of something," Amorim told Sky Sport after his team edged into the knock-out playoff round places.

Ferencvaros are behind Juve on goal difference in third after losing their 100-percent record with a goalless home draw against Celje of Slovenia.

Bayer Leverkusen, who won 2-0 at Dinamo Zagreb, are fourth ahead of Benfica.

Dwight McNeil scored a late winner as Crystal Palace climbed to 12th place with a comeback 2-1 win over 10-man Real Sociedad at Selhurst Park.

Sunderland's winless run in the competition extended to three games as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Polish club Jagiellonia at the Stadium of Light. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Jordie Barrett follows brothers as All Blacks captain
articles.excerpt: Jordie Barrett will become the third member of his family to captain New Zealand when he leads an under pressure…
articles.fullText:
Jordie Barrett will become the third member of his family to captain New Zealand when he leads an under pressure and much-changed All Blacks in their Nations Championship third-place playoff against England on Saturday.

New Zealand coach Dave Rennie's side return to Twickenham just a week on from their record 37-12 defeat by England – their heaviest loss to any northern hemisphere side – at the same ground.

Inside centre Jordie Barrett, a 29-year-old veteran of 88 Tests, becomes the third Barrett brother to lead the All Blacks, after Scott and Beauden, who are also named in the match-day 23.

Jordie Barrett replaces regular captain Codie Taylor as skipper, the hooker one of several players ruled out through injury.

Rennie has made six changes to his starting side as they look to finish 2026 on a high, with the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia less than a year away.

Beauden was captain when New Zealand suffered a shock 35-28 defeat by Wales a fortnight ago – the All Blacks' first loss to the Welsh in 73 years.

"I think anyone who would have worked with Jordie would know that he's very impressive, got great game understanding," coach Rennie told reporters on Thursday.

"He's been great in our leadership group, and he's taken over the captaincy role when Codie's left the field last week and a couple of weeks ago, so it was a pretty straightforward decision for us."

Another defeat would be New Zealand's third on the trot and take Rennie's record in his first year as coach to seven wins and six losses – the All Blacks' worst set of results since 1949.

It would also be the first time that England have won three Tests in a row against New Zealand.

"Last weekend hurt," said Rennie. "We own that performance. We've been really honest with ourselves about where we fell short."

He added: "Most of our issues last week were our own undoing...

"Our line-out's got to be better, the quality of our kicking game's got to be contestable if we're doing that, so we can apply pressure. Our skill-set just weren't clinical enough.

"We made double the amount of errors that England did with half the amount of ball.

"It hasn't been a lot of time on the grass (training), but we've put a lot of time into those key things, and if we get that part of the game right, then we'll be in the hunt."

Hooker Asafo Aumua, loose forward Anton Segner, scrum-half Cortez Ratima, fly-half Richie Mo'unga, midfielder Leicester Fainga'anuku and wing Rieko Ioane, replacing the injured Will Jordan, come into the starting 15.

Damian McKenzie moves from stand-off to full-back, with scrum-half Cam Roigard and full-back Beauden Barrett dropping to the bench.

England coach Steve Borthwick named his side on Wednesday, giving a first Test start to back-row Greg Fisilau and recalling full-back Freddie Steward in two of five changes to his starting side. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Bears stun Lions in NFL Thanksgiving thriller
articles.excerpt: Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a game-winning touchdown with three seconds remaining on Thursday as the Chicago Bears beat…
articles.fullText:
Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a game-winning touchdown with three seconds remaining on Thursday as the Chicago Bears beat the Detroit Lions 39-35 in an NFL Thanksgiving holiday thriller.

Williams's six-yard pass to Odunze – who managed to get both feet down in the back corner of the end zone – gave the Bears their first lead of a pulsating game in Detroit, where victory lifted them to 9-2 and into the NFC North division lead over the 8-3 Lions.

"We knew we needed a big one," Odunze said. "Luckily the O-line held up for me. Caleb delivered the ball exactly where it needed to be, and I was able to make a play in the back of the end zone."

Williams connected on 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns, both to Odunze.

The Bears had two rushing touchdowns from Kyle Monangai and one from D'Andre Swift to help offset a monster game from Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who ran for 205 yards and three TDs.

The Bears erased an early 10-point deficit, knotting it at 10-10 on Monangai's first touchdown with 4:07 left in the first half.

Jared Goff hit Sam LaPorta with an 11-yard scoring pass to push Detroit's lead to 19-10 going into halftime, but Monangai's two-yard TD had the Bears back within two, minutes into the third quarter.

The Lions finally appeared to be in control after Gibbs motored 70 yards for a touchdown that gave Detroit a 35-24 lead with 8:20 remaining.

Chicago responded with a three-play, 71-yard drive capped by Williams's 41-yard scoring pass to Odunze.

Detroit's next possession ended with a Goff interception, the Lions coming up empty on two straight possessions before the Bears put together their game-winning drive. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Two Italians killed in drone strike in Kuwait
articles.excerpt: A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working on an air defence system on Thursday, marking the first…
articles.fullText:
A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working on an air defence system on Thursday, marking the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months.

Both Italy and Kuwait confirmed the deaths, blaming the attack on Iran. But Tehran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi insisted in calls to his Kuwaiti and Italian counterparts that it was not behind the deadly strike.

Iran has in the last week ratcheted up attacks on Kuwait and Gulf neighbour Bahrain while it continues to fight the United States for control of the contested Strait of Hormuz.

"Around 2.00 pm today, several Iranian-made drones targeted Kuwaiti military installations, including an air-defence detection station where two Italian technicians from Rheinmetall were working," Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told the Senate.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni took to social media to offer her condolences.

"My thoughts are with all those affected by the attack and their families," she wrote on X.

But Iran was quick to refute the allegations that it was behind the deadly attack.

Araghchi held phone calls with both his Kuwaiti counterpart Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah and Italian counterpart Antonio Tajani to deny Tehran's involvement, according to Iran's state TV and foreign ministry.

In his call with Tajani, "Araghchi stated that Iran had no role or involvement whatsoever in the occurrence of this event," the Iranian foreign ministry said in a statement.

Iran's top diplomat added that Tehran was prepared to cooperate with Kuwait and Italy to "determine the origin of the incident", the ministry said.

He also offered a joint probe in his call with Al-Sabah, state TV reported.

Armed forces spokesperson Abolfazl Shekarchi had earlier refuted the claims that Iran was involved and blamed false flag operations by Israel and the United States for the attack, without providing evidence.

"No military or offensive operations have been conducted by the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran in the region," he said, state TV reported.

But EU chief Ursula von der Leyen called for more pressure on Tehran after the deaths.

"We must step up pressure on Iran to put an end to these unacceptable attacks against its neighbours and our partners in the Gulf," she wrote on social media.

The Kuwaiti defence ministry had earlier said that at least four people were injured in the incident, saying several drones had targeted an unspecified, vital location in the country.

The attack comes days after Kuwait activated its air defences last week to counter drone strikes launched by Iran – the first since early September.

The conflict – which began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February – has seen the Gulf states caught in the crossfire, with US military facilities and energy installations on their soil targeted.

The United States and Iran are in a standoff over the vital Strait of Hormuz, with the US military working to escort ships transiting the waterway in defiance of Tehran's attempts to close the waterway.

Further south, the war between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis continued to rage, following a week that saw the two sides trade heavy blows.

The Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said the Iran-backed group struck a refinery in southern Saudi Arabia's Jazan, which state media said killed one person and triggered a temporary shutdown of some operations.

It marked the latest in a series of barrages targeting major energy installations in the kingdom.

The coalition also claimed to have destroyed a ballistic missile launcher in Houthi territory that was used in the attack on the refinery.

The exchanges between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen have become near-daily in the country's revived civil war, which first began more than a decade ago.

Later on Thursday, Houthi media citing their health ministry published figures saying 19 civilians had been killed in the past 48 hours by "Saudi-led aggression".

Earlier, the coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said its forces had intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital of Riyadh overnight. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Thanksgiving storm knocks out power, flights in US
articles.excerpt: A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the US East Coast on Thursday, causing coastal flooding and…
articles.fullText:
A powerful storm disrupted the Thanksgiving holiday along much of the US East Coast on Thursday, causing coastal flooding and power outages and prompting the postponement of Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

High winds and flooding hammered both coasts, snarling holiday travel. More than 800,000 homes and businesses were without electricity on Thursday afternoon, with the majority in East Coast states, according to the outage tracking website poweroutage.us.

By midday, 1,700 flights to or from US destinations were delayed and more than 400 were cancelled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.

Macy’s postponed the annual Thanksgiving parade until Saturday because of concerns about how the parade’s massive balloons would fare in the wind-swept canyons between Manhattan’s skyscrapers.

A major storm pounded sections of the East Coast with torrential rain, high winds and flooding. All of New Jersey was under a state of emergency on Wednesday night, as were parts of New York.

The weather service posted wind advisories from northern Georgia to most of the mid-Atlantic and southern New England.

Two people had to be rescued from their cars in New York City because of flooding, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said on Thursday. He cautioned people not to walk, bike or drive through flooded areas.

“There is no destination worth your safety,” Mamdani said.

The storms also flooded coastal villages and cities from North Carolina through New Jersey as high tide rolled in. Roads were closed, and emergency workers were rescuing people from cars stranded in water.

In Maryland, nearly two million water customers in Montgomery and Prince George’s counties were asked to conserve water because of intermittent power disruptions associated with the storm.

The storms also prompted several brief tornado warnings on Thursday, including a rare twister southeast of Seattle, Washington.

A winter storm dumped heavy snow on parts of Missouri and Illinois. St Louis recorded 18.5 centimetres of snowfall.

The ice arena in Wentzville, Missouri, saw its roof partially collapse early on Thursday as heavy snow pummelled the city. The arena was empty when the roof caved in at about 3 am, according to Wentzville’s Parks and Recreation Director Mike Lueck.

Meanwhile, flooding along the Pacific coast persisted on Thursday, caused by high-tide driven waves and strong winds. The conditions were expected to continue into Friday, according to the National Weather Service.

Record-breaking tides along the California coast forced residents to evacuate – from Humboldt County in the far north to the San Francisco Bay Area and down to Ventura County near Los Angeles.

King tides also continued surging along the West Coast.

Video showed a massive wave tearing down part of the Pacifica pier in California on Wednesday, sending it into the ocean. Officials had closed the L-shaped pier in the summer after finding cracks in the structure. (AP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Pablo Hernandez de Cos to succeed Lagarde as ECB chief
articles.excerpt: Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos was picked by euro zone countries on Thursday as the next European…
articles.fullText:
Spanish central banking veteran Pablo Hernández de Cos was picked by euro zone countries on Thursday as the next European Central Bank President, a move that suggests policy continuity at Europe's most powerful financial institution.

The widely telegraphed selection caps months of closed-door negotiations between top EU power over seats on the ECB's six-person board, which will also see Germany grab the powerful chief economist role and France the position overseeing market operations.

Spain's De Cos, a former central bank governor and the current General Manager of the Bank for International Settlements, will take over when current chief Christine Lagarde steps down early on February 7. He will chair his first policy meeting on March 18.

The way for De Cos to take the top ECB role was cleared on Thursday after the Netherlands decided to back him, effectively standing down its own candidate Klaas Knot.

The reshuffle comes as the ECB grapples with an Iran war-driven resurgence in inflation and worries that political turmoil in France could trigger broader financial market stress affecting other euro zone countries.

The appointment of De Cos hands the top job to a southern European policymaker and ally of former ECB President Mario Draghi, reinforcing expectations that the central bank would ultimately use its firepower to contain any new sovereign debt crisis.

EU leaders also nominated France's Laurence Boone and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier to fill the remaining two vacancies on the board.

Boone, who will be the only woman on the Governing Council once Lagarde departs, will likely oversee market operations, while Brunnermeier is expected to take over as chief economist when Philip Lane steps down on May 31.

While largely a formality, the candidates are still subject to a confirmation process, which should be completed in time for EU leaders to give their final go ahead at the December summit.

De Cos, 55, a trained monetary economist, has built a reputation for independent thinking anchored in economic theory, and pragmatism picked up over a decade served in policymaking roles.

He worked in various staff positions at the ECB and the Bank of Spain early in his career before making a rare jump to the policymaking level as governor of the national central bank, serving on the ECB's rate-setting Governing Council.

De Cos is a veteran of crises including Spain's banking sector bailout, the Covid-19 pandemic, and the post-pandemic inflation surge that forced the ECB into its fastest interest rate-hiking cycle on record.

While southern European policymakers are often considered "doves" favouring easier monetary policy, colleagues and ECB watchers say De Cos is pragmatic and a moderate who cannot be boxed into any such category.

ECB policy is decided by the 27-member Governing Council, meaning even the president has limited scope to steer interest rates single-handedly.

In any case, any dovish bias would only be relevant if inflation was slightly above target, and this year's surge in price pressures would force any ECB president to keep raising interest rates.

At 4 percent, inflation is now twice the central bank's target and policymakers speaking on and off the record appear unanimous that a rate hike in December is inevitable.

The path beyond is murky, however. Markets expect just one more upward move, given the recent retreat in oil prices and an expected decline in inflation from the spring, when statistical base effects start knocking year-earlier figures from the data set. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Man convicted of UK train knife rampage
articles.excerpt: A man who went on the rampage armed with a knife on a London-bound train was on Thursday found guilty…
articles.fullText:
A man who went on the rampage armed with a knife on a London-bound train was on Thursday found guilty of the attempted murder of 14 people.

A jury found Anthony Williams, 33, guilty of all 10 counts of attempted murder on the train involving passengers and an on-board staff member, as well as earlier incidents in London and another UK town in which four others were injured.

Rail worker Samir Zitouni, 48 – who tried to stop Williams with a frying pan and was critically injured in the November 2025 attack – has been hailed for trying to protect passengers.

Williams had denied all 14 charges but admitted having intended to harm people.

Prosecutor Christopher Paxton earlier told the jury at Cambridge Crown Court in eastern England that over Halloween weekend last year Williams had "posed a dangerous threat, marauding through towns and cities, on streets and trains alike, armed with a knife."

"He stabbed many, seeking to end their lives with deadly intention, striking out at them when they were defenceless and in fear," he said.

The mass stabbing happened on a train from Doncaster to London on the evening of November 1.

As the events unfolded, the driver made an emergency stop at Huntingdon in Cambridgeshire, where armed officers swarmed the station.

The trapped "passengers ran for their lives, hiding away in locked toilets, store cabinets, or under seats" until many simply "ran out of train" and could go no further, Paxton said.

Some showed "extraordinary bravery" in trying to fend Williams off, grabbing pans or toasters to protect themselves, he said.

Williams did not give evidence at his trial and he appeared via video-link from Rampton Hospital, a high-security psychiatric hospital in Nottinghamshire.

Detective Superintendent Sam Blackburn, of the British Transport Police's Major, Serious and Organised Crime Unit, said despite the incident, Britain's trains were very safe.

"It's incredibly rare for individuals to be involved in violence on the railway," he said.

"Millions of passengers use the railway every single day. It is a safe and secure network." (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Left-wing Democrats join Eisenkot's Israeli coalition
articles.excerpt: The centrist party of Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form the next Israeli government, and an allied left-wing party…
articles.fullText:
The centrist party of Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form the next Israeli government, and an allied left-wing party on Thursday announced they had agreed on a coalition deal.

The left-leaning Democrats are the second party to agree to a coalition deal with Eisenkot's Yashar after the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party did so on Tuesday, marking a further step towards forming a government.

Eisenkot has until December 6 – a deadline which can be extended by 14 days – to form a government to replace caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc.

"Gadi Eisenkot, chair of Yashar with Eisenkot, and Yair Golan, chair of the Democrats, have agreed to sign a coalition agreement between the two parties," a joint statement said on Thursday.

The Democrats said they would receive four ministerial portfolios as part of the coalition deal, including an expanded national security ministry which under Netanyahu's government is headed by far-right firebrand Itamar Ben Gvir.

The party will also receive the Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Communications, and Ministry of Culture and Sport, which will include a new directorate for democracy, the party said in a statement.

Eisenkot, Liberman and Golan have a combined total of 36 lawmakers – far short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority.

The bloc also includes the Beyachad party of former prime minister Naftali Bennett which has 12 seats but is yet to sign a formal coalition agreement with Yashar.

Eisenkot's wide-ranging anti-Netanyahu camp has faced divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a national unity government with Netanyahu's right-wing Likud.

The Democrats have been pushing Eisenkot for an alliance with two Arab-majority lists that achieved an unprecedented seat haul in the vote, in a bid to unseat Netanyahu.

The party disapproved of the four rounds of talks between Yashar and Likud in recent days exploring the possibility of a unity government. No breakthroughs on that front have ostensibly been reached.

Liberman, on the other hand, has refused to serve in a government that relies on Arab-majority parties and has instead advocated an alliance with the two ultra-Orthodox parties, despite his years of criticism of the community and the fact that the issue of ultra-Orthodox military conscription remains a thorny one.

On Thursday, Liberman warned that Netanyahu was trying to derail the government's formation.

"He will drag out negotiations over a 'unity' government until the last moment, look for a pretext to blow them up, and even if such a government is formed, he will try to engineer a crisis within a few months to drag Israel back to elections," added Liberman, a hawkish former aide to Netanyahu who has become a strident critic.

Bennett, meanwhile, has been pushing for a unity government between Eisenkot's bloc and Likud that would exclude the ultra-Orthodox and Arab parties.

"Even at this time, I believe that by far the best alternative for the State of Israel and the serving public is a Zionist unity government led by Eisenkot first," he wrote on X, referring to a possible rotation agreement for the premiership. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Housefishing could fool you with AI real estate photos
articles.excerpt: Housefishing scams use AI real estate photos to fool buyers. Google Lens reverse image search and live video walkthroughs can…
articles.fullText:
You find a beautiful house online. The driveway looks brand new, and the landscaping could be straight out of a home magazine. You get excited, schedule a showing and start thinking about where your furniture might go. Then you pull up to the address and wonder whether you're looking at the same house.
That's the growing concern behind housefishing, a term for real estate listings that use digitally altered or AI-generated photos to make properties look better than they actually are. A recent report highlighted complaints from homebuyers and renters who described misleading property pictures as "false advertising." With AI tools becoming more convincing, it's getting harder to know whether you're looking at a home's actual condition or a digital makeover. So how can you tell whether a listing photo shows the home you're actually getting, and what should you check before scheduling a tour?
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
HIS HOME CHANGED HANDS FOR $5. COULD IT HAPPEN TO YOUR FAMILY?
Housefishing happens when property photos create an unrealistic impression of a home. AI can make an outdated property appear freshly renovated without anyone doing the actual work. For instance, two photos can show the same two-story house, but create very different impressions. 
The original photo can show a home with a dark asphalt driveway and large shrubs covering much of the front porch. But an AI-enhanced version can show a clean concrete driveway and a newly styled entrance.
This example shows how digital alterations can make a property appear to have undergone an expensive makeover. If those improvements exist only in the edited photo, someone visiting the property could be in for an unpleasant surprise.
Virtual staging has been around for years. Adding digital furniture to an empty living room can help buyers understand how they might use the space. AI simply makes those transformations easier and more realistic. But replacing a worn-out kitchen with an AI-generated renovation is another story. Laurent Cardinal, founder of real estate technology company Planpoint at planpoint.io/, believes agents need to be upfront about what they've changed. "The line is drawn where the intent is," Cardinal explains.
He supports using AI to show what a home could look like after renovations, provided agents clearly disclose the changes. His recommendation is straightforward: Show the original photo alongside the edited version so prospective buyers can compare them. However, digitally hiding property defects or replacing an unattractive view crosses that line. "That's cheating and it's hurtful to everyone in the market," Cardinal says. A misleading listing can waste someone's time and influence important financial decisions. For renters, the consequences can be especially serious if they send a deposit based on photos that fail to reflect the property.
You might think you'd recognize an AI-generated photo immediately. Maybe the furniture looks strange or a window seems out of place. Unfortunately, today's tools can produce convincing results. Sometimes the changes are subtle enough to escape a close look. Cardinal warns that even people familiar with AI-generated content can struggle to identify it. "But there's no silver bullet here, and anyone can get caught," he says.
Unusually perfect rooms can raise questions, especially when architectural details appear inconsistent between photos. However, traditional real estate photography can also be misleading. Wide-angle lenses make rooms appear larger, while carefully chosen lighting can minimize visible imperfections. AI creates an additional concern because it can alter the features of the property itself. That makes it increasingly difficult to judge a home's condition from listing photos alone.
FAKE VACATION RENTAL SITES USE LIVE CHAT TO STEAL YOUR DATA
The rules depend on where the property is located and which listing service an agent uses. California has already taken action. Under Assembly Bill 723, which took effect Jan. 1, 2026, real estate professionals must disclose covered digital alterations in advertisements for properties for sale. They must also provide access to the original, unaltered photos. The law covers changes made using traditional editing software or AI. Routine adjustments to lighting or color generally fall outside the requirements when they don't misrepresent the property. California has also approved Assembly Bill 2025. Starting Jan. 1, 2027, the state will require disclosures for digitally altered rental advertisements, with access to original photos when existing pictures have been changed.
Meanwhile, New York has warned agents about misleading AI property pictures. In November 2025, the New York Department of State reminded real estate professionals that advertisements must accurately represent properties for sale or rent. Agents who publish deceptive advertisements can face disciplinary action. Multiple listing services have their own restrictions. Stellar MLS, for example, requires disclosure of virtually staged photos and prohibits edits that conceal property defects or alter permanent features. There is currently no single nationwide law requiring every AI-edited real estate photo to carry a disclosure. Still, existing advertising laws and professional rules can apply when pictures mislead prospective buyers.
Interestingly, the same technology creating misleading property photos may also help identify them. Cardinal's company, Planpoint, connects listing photos to interactive floor plans. That allows prospective buyers to see how rooms fit together instead of relying on individual pictures that may be difficult to interpret. Its Planpoint Visit platform also offers AI photo detection. The technology checks newly uploaded property photos for signs of AI generation and displays a warning when it finds something suspicious. Cardinal says the company achieved a 98% success rate in its internal testing.
Before scheduling a showing or putting money down on a property, there are several ways to check whether the listing photos tell the whole story.
If a home looks suspiciously polished, ask the agent whether any pictures have been digitally altered. Request the original photos so you can compare them. Pay particular attention to kitchens and bathrooms, where expensive renovations can significantly affect a home's value. If an agent cannot explain what was changed, ask more questions before moving forward.
Cardinal recommends a simple way to verify a property's appearance. "The easiest way is to request a live video call with the agent or the owner," he says. Ask to see the areas you're most interested in, including anything that looks unusually perfect in the listing. A live walkthrough can reveal details that edited photos might hide. However, it cannot prove that the person showing the home has authority to rent or sell it.
Look carefully at the room dimensions and window locations. Then compare those details with the photos. Cardinal suggests asking, "Do the rooms and angles add up?" If a small bedroom appears enormous in a listing, ask whether the pictures were digitally altered. Remember that wide-angle photography can also exaggerate the apparent size of a room.
Search the property's address in Google Maps and look at the exterior using Street View. Compare the driveway and surrounding homes with what's shown in the listing. You might notice changes that deserve a closer look. However, Street View pictures can be outdated, so differences don't automatically mean an agent used AI.
Use Google Lens or another reverse-image search tool to check whether the same property pictures appear elsewhere online. You may find older listings showing the home before it was digitally enhanced. You could also discover that someone copied photos from another property to create a fraudulent rental advertisement . For help getting started, see our guide on how to reverse search an image on your phone.
Never rely solely on listing photos when making a financial commitment. If you're renting, independently verify the identity and authority of the landlord or agent before sending a deposit. For a home purchase, arrange an in-person showing and an independent inspection before committing to buy. A polished listing photo cannot tell you whether the property has hidden problems.
Those example of the two photos of the same house really show how far AI has come. The updated version looks fantastic, and I can see why someone would want to schedule a showing. But what happens when you arrive and discover that the beautiful driveway and landscaping don't actually exist? I think AI can be a great tool for helping buyers see a home's potential, especially if they're considering renovations. The problem starts when agents present those digital upgrades as the real thing. Buying a home is a major investment, and people deserve to know exactly what they're getting before they fall in love with a property online. I'd like to see more transparency from real estate agents, with original photos available alongside any AI-enhanced versions. There's nothing wrong with showing what a house could become, but buyers should never have to guess what it looks like today.
Would you walk away from a home if you discovered the agent had used AI to make it look better than it actually was, or would you consider that acceptable marketing? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

articles.title: Bypass set to open fully on Dec 6
articles.excerpt: The Kowloon Bay Section of the Central Kowloon Bypass will open for traffic at 7am on December 6, completing the…
articles.fullText:
The Kowloon Bay Section of the Central Kowloon Bypass will open for traffic at 7am on December 6, completing the road’s commissioning.

A flat toll of $8 will be charged for all vehicle types via the HKeToll system upon commissioning.

Together with the already commissioned Yau Ma Tei Section of the bypass, and the Tseung Kwan O-Lam Tin Tunnel, the new section makes up Route 6, linking Tseung Kwan O, Kowloon East and Kowloon West.

The Civil Engineering & Development Department said that Route 6 will cut peak-hour journey times between Tseung Kwan O and Yau Ma Tei to about 12 minutes, while relieving congestion along major Kwun Tong corridors such as the Kwun Tong Bypass and Kwun Tong Road.

The Kowloon Bay Section is about 3.4 kilometres long, including 3.1km in the form of tunnels. Various innovative technologies were adopted in its construction. For example, the subsea tunnel section was constructed using two 14-metre-wide Tunnel Boring Machines, averting the need for reclamation and maintaining the operation of waterfront facilities during the works.

From midnight to 7am on December 6, the Yau Ma Tei Section will be temporarily closed to allow for updates to traffic signs and road markings as well as final preparatory work for the HKeToll system.

Following full commissioning of the bypass at 7am on December 6, new traffic, public transport and toll arrangements will be implemented.

With the addition of the Kowloon Bay Section, the number of bus routes operating via Route 6 will reach 20 by the end of this year, offering about 300 trips daily.

Highlighting that traffic may be heavier in the initial period as motorists take time to adapt to new road sections, the Transport Department urged motorists to watch the videos in its driving guide , and choose appropriate routes based on actual traffic conditions.

articles.title: LCSD probing SmartPLAY incident
articles.excerpt: The Leisure & Cultural Services Department confirmed today that, as reported by the SmartPLAY system contractor yesterday, the system was…
articles.fullText:
The Leisure & Cultural Services Department confirmed today that, as reported by the SmartPLAY system contractor yesterday, the system was illegally accessed in a hacking incident involving personal data linked to around 90,000 Leisure Link accounts.

Upon discovering the incident, the contractor said it took immediate measures to stop the hack and reviewed the system to ensure its normal operation.

SmartPLAY provides services for users to book leisure facilities and enrol in activities, and replaced the old Leisure Link system in 2023.

To allow Leisure Link users to become SmartPLAY users, Leisure Link account data was transferred to the new SmartPLAY platform when the latter launched.

To speed up the process, SmartPLAY offers a “Reactivate Leisure Link Account” function that enables Leisure Link users, when applying to become SmartPLAY users, to retrieve their personal data from the old system automatically.

Preliminary findings suggest that SmartPLAY's “Reactivate Leisure Link Account” function was hacked. The personal data involved includes dates of birth, telephone numbers, addresses, gender details and email addresses, along with the names of about 1,500 users.

The incident does not involve information on users' identity documents, and SmartPLAY does not store any payment information such as credit card details.

As most Leisure Link users have already created SmartPLAY accounts, the “Reactivate Leisure Link Account” function has been cancelled. The relevant Leisure Link data will be permanently removed from the SmartPLAY system.

SmartPLAY's “forget patron number or password” function was also used by hackers, leading to the system sending out emails containing verification codes to affected users. This breach does not involve personal data.

SmartPLAY users who did not use the function but received an emails from the system should ignore it. Users who have forgotten their password and intend to reset it may do so using their Hong Kong identity card at a leisure venue or a District Leisure Services Office with a Smart Self-Service Station.

SmartPLAY has disabled the function for detailed checks, and a separate announcement will be made when it resumes.

The department said it is highly concerned about the incident and has asked the contractor to conduct a detailed investigation and submit a report. It has also reported the matter to the Police Force, the Security Bureau, the Digital Policy Office (DPO) and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD).

Additionally, the department and the contractor are making arrangements to inform people affected, conduct a comprehensive review and strengthen protective measures on the system, with a view to preventing the recurrence of similar incidents. The department is also consulting the PCPD and the DPO in the process.

With the URBTIX and SmartPLAY systems having been illegally accessed by hackers in the past few days, the department will invite the force to determine if serious illegal activities are involved.

articles.title: FS promotes ties in the Netherlands
articles.excerpt: Leading a delegation to the Netherlands, Financial Secretary Paul Chan attended several events, including an exchange session in Amsterdam aimed…
articles.fullText:
Leading a delegation to the Netherlands, Financial Secretary Paul Chan attended several events, including an exchange session in Amsterdam aimed at boosting co-operation between Hong Kong and the Netherlands.

Yesterday morning, Mr Chan and the delegation joined an exchange session in Amsterdam co-organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC), Amsterdam Trade & Invest, StartupAmsterdam and Amsterdam Science Park.

During the session, Amsterdam representatives briefed the delegation on how the city develops its innovation and technology (I&T) ecosystem and outlined its priority areas in research and industry. They also explained how the city fosters close collaboration among universities, research institutes, investors and businesses to bring research outcomes from the laboratory to the market.

Speaking at a keynote luncheon, Mr Chan gave an update on Hong Kong’s latest economic situation. Addressing Dutch businesses and young innovators, he highlighted the city’s quality lifestyle and encouraged everyone to visit Hong Kong to experience its vibrancy and opportunities first-hand.

In the afternoon, Mr Chan and the delegation travelled to Leiden to visit the Netherlands’ largest bioscience park. Both sides explored partnership opportunities across various areas, including closer collaboration between the science parks of the two places.

The Financial Secretary then visited the Centre for Human Drug Research in Leiden, which specialises in early-stage clinical research, to learn about its facilities and work.

articles.title: Industry park CEO appointed
articles.excerpt: The Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park Company announced today the appointment of Yiu Hing-leung as its first Chief Executive Officer…
articles.fullText:
The Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park Company announced today the appointment of Yiu Hing-leung as its first Chief Executive Officer, following an open recruitment exercise and after obtaining the approval of the Chief Executive. Mr Yiu will assume duty on December 1 for a term of three years.

Mr Yiu has more than 30 years of experience in the technology and industrial sectors. He previously served at the Hong Kong Science & Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTPC), where he held several key leadership positions, including Chief Corporate Development Officer and Head of Innofacturing. He spearheaded the transformation of industrial estates to “InnoParks”, and led projects including technology and industry clusters, and incubation programmes, to drive the development of a sustainable and vibrant innovation and technology ecosystem.

Prior to joining the HKSTPC, Mr Yiu held senior executive roles at a technology startup and a multinational corporation.

The park company is wholly owned by the Government through The Financial Secretary Incorporated. It is responsible for the development and operation of the Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park, which spans approximately 27.5 hectares, and will capitalise on the park's locational advantages, including its proximity to Qianhai in Shenzhen, to drive the development of a diverse range of industries. These include high value-added and smart production such as pharmaceutical manufacturing and food processing.

Since the appointment of its board of directors in middle of this year, the park company has commenced operations and is working to attract enterprises and investment.

articles.title: Adaptation of laws completed
articles.excerpt: The Statute Law (Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance 2026 and the subsidiary legislation amending court rules were published in the Government Gazette…
articles.fullText:
The Statute Law (Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance 2026 and the subsidiary legislation amending court rules were published in the Government Gazette today, marking the completion of Hong Kong’s adaptation of laws seven months ahead of the original schedule set for the end of the current Government term.

The subsidiary legislation comprises the Rules of the High Court (Amendment) (No. 3) Rules 2026, the High Court Fees (Amendment) Rules 2026 and the Rules of the District Court (Amendment) (No. 3) Rules 2026.

The adaptation of laws involves amending legislation previously in force immediately before July 1, 1997, and adopted as laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, to align them with the Basic Law and Hong Kong’s status as a Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China. It also ensures that these laws comply with the February 23, 1997 Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress under Article 160 of the Basic Law, removing the need to rely on substitution rules in the Interpretation & General Clauses Ordinance or other interpretation principles.

According to the Government, the Law Reform Commission (LRC) Secretariat has spearheaded the systematic review of Hong Kong’s statutory laws since February 2022, prioritising the adaptation exercise. Since taking office, the current-term Government has seen the Department of Justice (DoJ) and the LRC Secretariat strengthen co-ordination with policy bureaux and the Judiciary.

After reviewing previously enacted laws and examining 185 pieces of legislation in detail, the Government streamlined its approach by tackling simpler issues first and introducing amendments in batches as soon as they were ready. Policy bureaux introduced 11 dedicated adaptation ordinances alongside the subsidiary legislation amending the court rules.

From 2024, the DoJ introduced one omnibus bill annually for three consecutive years to handle adaptation amendments collectively and on a priority basis. The Chinese and English texts of the three omnibus bills each span over 750 pages, with Bills Committees holding 13 meetings to scrutinise them thoroughly.

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam noted that completing the exercise early was made possible by the guidance and support of the Central Authorities, including the Hong Kong & Macao Affairs Office of the State Council, the Liaison Office of the Central People’s Government in the Hong Kong SAR and the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hong Kong SAR. He also credited the Chief Executive’s leadership, collaboration between policy bureaux and the Judiciary under the DoJ’s co-ordination, and the co-operation of Legislative Council Members.

“This is not only the fulfilment of the constitutional duty under Article 160, as well as other relevant articles, of the Basic Law, but also a milestone in the full and faithful implementation of the principle of ‘one country, two systems’. At the same time, the adaptation of laws exercise makes Hong Kong’s legislation clearer, more intelligible and more accessible, ensuring that the statutory laws are up to date and thereby strengthening the community's understanding and practice of the rule of law,” he said.

articles.title: Flowers moved to make room at remembrance site: govt

articles.fullText:
The government said on Thursday that it relocated some of the flowers and tribute items laid in an open space across Wang Fuk Court to make room for people who turned up after nightfall to pay their respects.

At Kwong Fuk Sitting-out Area, officers from the Civil Aid Service could be seen keeping order throughout the day by placing the bouquets on the ground in plastic containers, and moving them to a nearby lawn.

In a statement, the government said this was to create space for more people to lay bouquets, and ensure everyone's goodwill was respected while maintaining order and cleanliness at the venue.

The flowers and related items will gradually be transferred to a religious venue for storage, and to continue the public's tribute to the deceased, a spokesman added.

Media liaison officers from the police force told people at the scene that the flowers would not be disposed of, and instead moved to Fung Ying Seen Koon, a Taoist temple in Fanling.
