articles.title: Your holiday shopping data needs a cleanup before Black Friday
articles.excerpt: Data brokers may expose your name, home address and phone number to scammers sending fake USPS delivery texts ahead of…
articles.fullText:
Your phone buzzes: "USPS: Your package could not be delivered due to an incomplete address. Update your details within 12 hours." You did order something last week. Probably several things. So your thumb hovers over the link. That's the whole trick.
Black Friday lands on Nov. 27 this year, and the holiday delivery rush is already underway. That gives scammers plenty of opportunities to send fake delivery alerts that arrive when you're expecting a package.
Meanwhile, your shopping habits and personal details may be circulating through data brokers . Here's how that information can make scams more convincing and what you can do to clean it up before the holiday shopping rush gets even busier.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
A SCAMMER HAS YOUR NAME, PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS. WHAT CAN THEY ACTUALLY DO?
Every time you shop online, sign up for a discount or share your contact information, you may add to a growing collection of personal data. Some businesses use that information for their own marketing, while others share certain details with advertising partners or data brokers.
Here's where some of that information comes from:
As I've covered before, loyalty programs and store memberships can contribute to the information companies collect about you . Add the personal details available through people-search sites, and someone looking to target you may find more information than you'd expect. The FTC explains that people-search companies collect information from multiple sources and sell reports containing personal details, sometimes including relatives' names and addresses.
You can use the free exposure scanner we recommend at CyberGuy.com to check whether your personal information appears on publicly searchable websites. Keep in mind that a free scan cannot uncover every private data broker database. The results might surprise you.
WHY CAREFUL PEOPLE STILL END UP ON DATA BROKER SITES
A fake delivery text doesn't need to know exactly what you ordered. During the holidays, plenty of people are expecting packages, so a message about a delivery problem can seem believable. Scammers often send these messages to large numbers of phone numbers without knowing anything about the recipients. However, personal information obtained from public sources or data brokers can help make some scams more convincing.
Here's how that information could be misused:
The FTC reported that fake package delivery problems, often involving messages impersonating USPS, were the most commonly reported type of text scam in 2024. The problem extends beyond package deliveries. According to FTC testimony released in March 2026, Americans reported $15.9 billion in fraud losses during 2025 across all scam categories. A typical fake delivery message directs you to a convincing website and asks you to pay a small redelivery fee. That payment request is the trap. The scammer wants your credit card details and may also try to collect other sensitive information. Here's something important to remember: USPS does not charge a fee for redelivery. Its legitimate text tracking service also requires you to request tracking information first, and those tracking messages do not contain links.
Data removal takes time. Brokers process opt-out requests on different schedules, and personal information can reappear even after it has been removed. Starting now gives you a chance to identify exposed information and begin requesting removals before the busiest shopping days arrive.
There is one important distinction. Removing your information from data brokers can reduce your exposure over time, but it cannot guarantee that scam texts will stop or prevent scammers from contacting you this holiday season. That's why data cleanup should go hand in hand with safer shopping and delivery habits.
You can get started in about 15 minutes, although completing data removal requests and having companies process them can take much longer.
Look up your name on people-search websites such as Spokeo, Whitepages or BeenVerified. Check whether your home address, phone number or relatives' information appears. If you find information you want removed, look for the site's opt-out instructions.
Check the privacy settings on the websites and apps you use most frequently. Look for options to limit promotional emails, personalized advertising and sharing with marketing partners. You can also review saved shipping addresses and remove outdated entries you no longer need. Keep in mind that deleting a saved address may not erase information retained in previous order records.
If a message claims there's a delivery problem, open the retailer's or shipping company's official app or website yourself. Check the tracking number and delivery status there. Do not enter payment details through a link in an unsolicited message, even if it includes your name or address.
Instead of spending hours submitting individual opt-out forms, an automated data removal service can send removal requests to hundreds of data brokers, depending on the provider and plan you choose. Some services also submit recurring removal requests to help address information that reappears. While no service can erase every piece of information about you online, it can help reduce your exposure. Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.
Talk with your parents and other relatives about fake delivery messages. Make sure everyone knows to verify unexpected payment requests through the carrier's official website or app. For USPS specifically, explain that it does not charge redelivery fees. A message demanding immediate payment to release a package should raise suspicion.
If you receive a suspicious delivery message, don't respond or click the link. You can forward scam texts to 7726 (SPAM) and use your phone's reporting feature. For messages impersonating USPS, you can also report them to spam@uspis.gov. If you already entered your credit card information on a suspicious website, contact your card issuer immediately. Ask about blocking the card, disputing fraudulent charges and monitoring your account for unauthorized activity. You can also report the incident at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
What concerns me most about these fake delivery texts is how easily they blend into our holiday routines. When you're ordering gifts and waiting for packages, a message about a delivery problem can catch you at exactly the wrong moment. I also think we need to pay more attention to how much personal information is floating around online. Taking a few minutes to search your name, review your shopping accounts and start removing exposed information is worthwhile. But remember, even if you clean up your data, scammers can still reach you. My advice is simple: Never let an unexpected text dictate how you check on a package. Open the official app or website yourself and verify what's actually happening before you share a single detail.
Have you received a fake package delivery text that looked convincing, and how did you figure out it was a scam? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

articles.title: Nine hurt in huge explosion at Bangkok oil facility
articles.excerpt: A huge explosion rocked an oil facility in eastern Bangkok on Thursday, injuring nine people with three of them in…
articles.fullText:
A huge explosion rocked an oil facility in eastern Bangkok on Thursday, injuring nine people with three of them in a critical condition, Thai authorities said.

The blast was so strong that it rattled doors several kilometres away, according to AFP reporters, who saw a column of flames above the site in Phra Khanong followed by thick black smoke.

Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered urgent checks on the fire's possible effects on the health and safety of residents near the refinery, the government said in a statement.

Energy minister Akanat Promphan, visiting the scene, told reporters that the fire appeared to break out at a distillation tower, "which was at least 100 metres away from the oil depot", limiting the damage.

Thai energy conglomerate Bangchak Corporation, which runs the site, said it brought the situation under control within 30 minutes.

The cause of the incident was under investigation, it said in a statement.

The firm later said "air quality monitoring around the refinery shows normal levels".

Akanat said authorities tested for carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and other contaminants in a one-kilometre radius around the facility and found no irregularities.

But the government was suspending production at the plant until the energy ministry was confident operations could resume without issue, he said.

Police told AFP that students from nearby schools had been evacuated, and residents were also asked to leave.

The Erawan Emergency Medical Centre, which is operated by Bangkok city authorities, reported nine people were injured -- three classified as critical, a change from its initial assessment.

Black smoke swept across the Thai capital's skyline in the immediate aftermath of the blast.

A city-wide alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities urged people to avoid the area.

Bangchak Corporation's website describes the site as a "modern complex refinery with a maximum capacity of 120,000 barrels per day".

An explosion occurred at the refinery in July 2012, triggering a massive fire but no reported injuries. It was owned at the time by Bangchak Petroleum, which became the Bangchak Corporation.

The 2012 incident prompted questions about why such a large facility was located near a residential area. (AFP/Xinhua)

Edited by Raymond Yeung

articles.title: HK exports rise in October on AI electronics demand
articles.excerpt: Exports and imports both rose year on year in October, supported by strong shipments of artificial intelligence-related electronics, according to…
articles.fullText:
Exports and imports both rose year on year in October, supported by strong shipments of artificial intelligence-related electronics, according to data from the Census and Statistics Department on Thursday.

Total exports of goods increased 65.6 percent year on year to HK$764.5 billion, which followed a 64.9 percent rise in September.

Imports grew 56.2 percent to HK$783.8 billion, after climbing 57.8 percent the previous month.

A government spokesman attributed the strong export performance to continued robust growth in exports of AI-related electronic products.

He added that exports of other products also picked up, and that shipments to most major markets recorded notable increases.

By commodity, exports of "electrical machinery, apparatus and appliances, and electrical parts thereof" rose 57.8 percent, while office machines and automatic data processing machines jumped 146.5 percent.

By market, exports to Asia as a whole grew 66.1 percent. Exports to the mainland rose 65.4 percent while shipments to Taiwan almost tripled.

Exports to Mexico jumped 258.6 percent, and those to the United States more than doubled.

Looking ahead, the spokesman said strong global investment in AI and related demand will continue to support Hong Kong’s merchandise trade.

He warned, however, that external uncertainties remain, including developments in international trade and technology policies, risks tied to the rapid expansion of global AI investment and evolving geopolitical tensions.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Mainland flat as HK, region rise on US holiday break
articles.excerpt: Mainland stocks were flat on Thursday, giving up their opening gains as the US Trump administration's latest tariff proposal, lingering…
articles.fullText:
Mainland stocks were flat on Thursday, giving up their opening gains as the US Trump administration's latest tariff proposal, lingering AI concerns and the Thanksgiving break for Wall Street kept Asian investors on the sidelines.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 260 points, or 1.2 percent, higher at 22,226, rebounding from its lowest level since April 2025, on turnover of HK$212.45 billion.

The tech index rose 39 points, or 1.2 percent, to 3,417 while the China enterprises index was 108 points, or 1.5 percent, higher at 7,493.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index rose less than a point to close at 3,476 on turnover of 613.33 billion yuan.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell two points to close at 10,084 on turnover of 704 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index gained six points, or 0.29 percent, to close at 2,189 on turnover of 333.54 billion yuan.

The mainland markets' flat showings came after US President Donald Trump on Wednesday proposed maximum potential tariffs of 20 percent to 40 percent on 14 major trading partners including China, in a move to counter excess industrial capacity that his administration has said these countries promote.

But "market sentiment is still relatively downbeat," analysts at Nanhua Futures said in a note.

"Global concerns about AI have not subsided, and although domestic measures to stabilise the market were introduced last weekend, they have had only a limited effect on sentiment. In the short term, stock indices are expected to remain weak."

Among the biggest onshore losers, the new-energy vehicle sector fell 1.3 percent, with battery giant CATL down as much as 2.9 percent to a 26-month low. The CSI Semiconductor Index fell 2 percent.

Elsewhere around the region, markets cobbled together a rare rally as the latest salvo of US tariffs looked less damaging than first feared, while the Thanksgiving holiday offered a welcome break from the AI pain trade.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq retreated on Wednesday due to an AI selloff but finished well off the day's lows as bargain hunters stepped in.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei closed up 487 points, or 0.86 percent, at 57,499, with chipmaker Kioxia Holdings surging 12.6 percent, AI-focused startup investor SoftBank Group jumping 7.3 percent and chip-testing tool maker Advantest climbed 4.6 percent. The broader Topix inched up 0.1 percent to 3,750.

In Seoul, the Kospi inched up 13 points, or 0.29 percent, to 4,711 after the central bank raised interest rates to their highest level since November 2024, with shares of chipmaker Samsung Electronics rising 0.3 percent and its peer SK Hynix gaining 2.2 percent. (Agencies)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Commerce Ministry slams new US tariffs
articles.excerpt: China said on Thursday it reserves the right to take "necessary measures" after Washington unveiled new tariffs that could shake…
articles.fullText:
China said on Thursday it reserves the right to take "necessary measures" after Washington unveiled new tariffs that could shake the uneasy truce in the two economic giants' trade war.

Commerce Ministry spokesman He Yadong told a regular briefing that citing "overcapacity" as a reason to impose tariffs was a "pretext for protectionism".

"Such actions not only fail to address their own structural imbalances but also disrupt the security and stability of global industrial and supply chains, hinder industrial cooperation, drive up global inflation, harm the direct interests of businesses and consumers and pose long-term, systemic risks to global economic growth," He said.

"China urges the United States to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation.

"China will closely monitor developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests."

The proposed new US levies target a range of trading partners including China, the European Union and Japan and range up to 20 percent.

The Commerce Ministry spokesman also urged Washington to accelerate internal procedures so a US$60 billion tariff cut arrangement can come into effect as soon as possible.

Chinese and US officials have maintained close communication on the issue of a trade truce, He said.

Other countries have also criticised the latest round of tariffs announced by the Trump administration.

Japan's top government spokesman, Minoru Kihara, called them "regrettable", and denied that Tokyo had structural excess manufacturing capacity.

Singapore said it was "very disappointed" with proposed new US tariffs on its exports, and denied it was protecting its domestic market or subsidising manufacturing.

India's commerce ministry said trade concerns should be addressed through ongoing talks with Washington. (AFP/Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Musk says every child in US to get two SpaceX shares
articles.excerpt: Elon Musk, the world's richest person, said on Wednesday that every child in the United States will receive two shares…
articles.fullText:
Elon Musk, the world's richest person, said on Wednesday that every child in the United States will receive two shares in SpaceX, the space and AI company he runs, pledging a gift worth some US$18 billion.

Musk and rival AI company Anthropic have recently laid out sharply different blueprints for sharing some of the spoils of the AI boom, amid growing public and political scrutiny of the industry.

Children will receive one share from the company and one from him personally, Musk said in a brief post on X, without providing details.

In a separate post, Musk said the SpaceX shares will be transferred next month.

"The share directly from me will be transferred when my lockup expires in June next year," Musk added.

SpaceX said earlier on Wednesday it would contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock to every currently active Trump Account, adding that Musk will personally match the number of shares donated by the company.

A Trump Account is a programme designed to give Americans under the age of 18 a stake in the stock market and help build wealth from an early age. The White House said in October it had opened almost 70 million accounts.

SpaceX shares closed at US$127.44 on Wednesday, valuing the pledge at nearly US$18 billion.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether Musk's SpaceX share donations would be linked to Trump Accounts.

"What it does is build a massive, long-term retail shareholder base," said Christopher Brankin, global markets advisor at brokerage Mitrade Group.

"It builds immediate market engagement and creates a massive, financially literate client pipeline for trading platforms as that generation comes of age."

Musk, whose net worth is around US$824 billion, said last month he would give one of his SpaceX shares to every child in America. He held about 6.42 billion shares in the company as of June.

"Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Musk said in a post on X at the time.

"Giving shares, which are stakes in the future economy, directly to the people is the way," Musk added.

Most of Musk's philanthropic efforts have been through the Musk Foundation, which reportedly holds more than US$14 billion in assets.

In October, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband pledged a share of their SpaceX stock to each of more than 2 million children under the Trump initiative.

Anthropic, which recently went public, said last month it was committing 5 percent of its shares to a new fund for the "public good".

Anthropic said its initiative, worth around US$54 billion at current prices, will give it more flexibility and scale to make donations for the benefit of humanity.

Other executives have also set up major, long-running philanthropy ventures.

Berkshire Hathaway Chairman Emeritus Warren Buffett, one of the most prominent figures in philanthropy, is reported to have given away US$60 billion so far, with most of the rest of his roughly US$150 billion fortune slated for philanthropy too.

The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has distributed more than US$100 billion since its founding in 2000, with some of that fueled by donations from Buffett. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Home prices edge lower but rents scale new highs
articles.excerpt: Private home prices have eased, ending two months of gains. Latest data from the Rating and Valuation Department showed prices…
articles.fullText:
Private home prices have eased, ending two months of gains.

Latest data from the Rating and Valuation Department showed prices fell 0.6 percent in October from the month before.

The private home price index had gone up by 0.2 percent in September and 0.1 percent in August.

Still, the index last month were 8.2 percent higher than a year ago.

For the first 10 months of the year, prices were up 6.5 percent year on year.

The index had fallen in July, the first monthly decline in more than a year.

By unit size, prices of small and medium flats dropped 0.6 percent in October from the month earlier, whereas luxury homes recorded a 0.3 percent drop.

On the other hand, rents hit new highs.

Rental levels rose 0.5 percent in October from the month before and 6.7 percent from a year ago for the 12 straight month of gains.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: HK, regional equities rally as Wall St fights off lows
articles.excerpt: Asian shares eked out a rare rally on Thursday after Wall Street fought back from deep lows, though concerns over…
articles.fullText:
Asian shares eked out a rare rally on Thursday after Wall Street fought back from deep lows, though concerns over the circular financing of AI and a new round of US tariffs made for a muted mood in a holiday-thinned session.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index started the day up 268 points, or 1.2 percent, at 22,234.

The tech index surged 77 points, or 2.3 percent, up to 3,455 while the China enterprises index rose 100 points, or 1.4 percent, to 7,485.

Up north, the Shanghai Composite Index opened up 13 points, or 0.39 percent, at 3,490.

The Shenzhen Component Index was 98 points, or 0.98 percent, higher at 10,184 while the ChiNext Index rose 29 points, or 1.35 percent, to 2,213.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei opened 417 points, or 0.73 percent, up at 57,429 before doubling its gains to be 818 points higher at one stage before lunch.

In Seoul, the Kospi opened 47 points, or 1.01 percent, at 4,745 and, unlike the Nikkei, its gains were a little more sedate, nudging the benchmark up to 53 points higher at one stage before noon.

The gains came after tech giant Nvidia was again at the centre of the unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade citing weaknesses in the chipmaker's management and board oversight.

Nvidia stock ended down 3.9 percent at US$149.30 on Wednesday, US$2.3 trillion short of its October peak of US$243.37.

Wall Street did recoup most of its initial losses overnight as money moved into other, more defensive, sectors. S&P 500 futures added 0.5 percent early on Thursday, while Nasdaq futures firmed 0.4 percent.

Bond investors are wondering if the broad losses in stocks coupled with doubts on the durability of AI-driven business investment might temper the hawkishness of central banks.

It was notable that Treasury yields hit multi-week lows on Wednesday even as US economic growth for the third quarter was revised up sharply to 4.3 percent, while the Federal Reserve's favoured measure of core inflation hit an uncomfortably high 3.3 percent.

While futures still imply a 98 percent chance the Fed will raise rates by 25 basis points in December, speculation of a half-point increase has faded.

Yields on 10-year paper were off at 4.848 percent, having touched an 11-week trough overnight.

Still, the outlook for inflation was not helped by White House proposals for new tariffs on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, though crucially the new duties will not stack on top of those imposed in July.

"The latest US tariff announcement is not as alarming as it looks, and the increase in the effective tariff rate looks set to be a touch lower than we've been assuming," said Stephen Brown, chief North America economist at Capital Economics.

"The additional tariff burden is likely to be small, but will still provide a marginal boost to prices and keep core goods inflation firm into next year." (Agencies)

Edited by Wendy Wong

articles.title: James sets NBA record as oldest to score triple-double
articles.excerpt: LeBron James became the oldest player in NBA history to produce a triple-double, leading Philadelphia to a 114-104 victory over…
articles.fullText:
LeBron James became the oldest player in NBA history to produce a triple-double, leading Philadelphia to a 114-104 victory over Miami in the NBA Cup on Wednesday.

Four-time NBA Most Valuable Player James, who turns 42 on December 30, scored a season-high 25 points, passed off a season-high 12 assists and pulled down 10 rebounds for the 76ers.

Miami grabbed a 32-29 lead after the first quarter, but James scored 14 consecutive Sixers points in a second-quarter run for a 62-53 halftime lead, and the hosts never lost the lead in the second half.

"We wanted to get back to our defensive identity," James said. "We didn't do that in the first quarter but for the next 36 minutes I thought we got back to that."

The 76ers improved the best record in the Eastern Conference to 15-4 while snapping a seven-game win streak for Miami (10-7).

Both clubs are 2-1 in East Group B Cup play, but with a win Miami would have clinched the group and advanced to the knockout stage of the in-season tournament.

With Joel Embiid out because of illness and Jaylen Brown out after early left hamstring tightness, it fell to James to score and set up his teammates with NFL-ish passing.

"That's my favorite aspect of my game besides my IQ," James said.

"So to be able to go out there and just play like a quarterback role and watch these guys run the right routes and it's my job to put it on time and on target, it was fun."

Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 30 points while fellow guard VJ Edgecombe added 18.

"In this league you have to have some depth for sure," James said. "It's a fast-paced game. It feels good for us. These are my young bulls right here. They keep me going. They keep me energised."

Greek star Giannis Antetokounmpo led Miami with 32 points and 14 rebounds.

A late rebound gave James his first triple double with the 76ers, drawing a standing ovation from the Philadelphia crowd.

James left the Los Angeles Lakers in the off-season and selected the 76ers from several clubs in hopes of capturing a fifth NBA crown. (AFP)

Edited by Nazvi Careem

articles.title: Lukoil reaches deal to sell international assets
articles.excerpt: An investment consortium that includes US firm Eldridge announced a deal on Wednesday to acquire Lukoil's international assets, a transaction…
articles.fullText:
An investment consortium that includes US firm Eldridge announced a deal on Wednesday to acquire Lukoil's international assets, a transaction spurred by US sanctions on the Russian oil company.

The deal involves a swap of shares of Lukoil and other Russian equities for the equity of Lukoil International GmbH (LIG), Eldridge said in a press release.

The overall value of the deal is US$10 billion, a person close to the matter told AFP.

Besides Eldridge, which is led by US billionaire Todd Boehly, the consortium includes the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), an international investment arm of the US government that will receive an ownership interest in the assets.

The move drew condemnation from Democrats, with congressman Gregory Meeks -- who sits on the House Foreign Affairs Committee -- calling on the Trump administration to halt the deal.

"Congress banned the DFC from investing in Russia less than a year ago, yet this Administration is circumventing that restriction by buying US$10 billion in energy assets from Russia's largest oil company, a corporation the US sanctioned precisely to pressure Moscow to end its war in Ukraine," Meeks said in a statement.

The other consortium members are investment group Xtellus Partners and Catena Investment Holding, which is based in the United Arab Emirates.

LIG produces about 350,000 barrels a day of oil equivalent, owns three refineries and operates more than 2,000 gasoline stations in 16 countries, including the United States.

In October 2025, the United States added Lukoil and fellow Russian producer Rosneft to its blacklist of sanctioned entities.

Lukoil said in January that it reached an agreement to sell its foreign assets to the US investment firm The Carlyle Group, but the private equity company dropped out of the deal in October.

Another group of prospective buyers, the brothers Moutaz and Ramez Al-Khayyat, also fell by the wayside.

A potential deal involving the Qatar-based brothers sparked criticism over their business ties to Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner, the US president's daughter and son-in-law, according to the New York Times.

Boehly and his investment firm have given US$2 million to Donald Trump's political causes, the Times reported. (AFP)

Edited by Altis Wong

articles.title: Steelers cut Rodgers after fiery coach criticism
articles.excerpt: Four-time NFL Most Valuable Player Aaron Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday after ripping head coach Mike…
articles.fullText:
Four-time NFL Most Valuable Player Aaron Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday after ripping head coach Mike McCarthy in a television interview.

Rodgers, a Super Bowl champion quarterback who turns 43 next Wednesday, rejected any idea he could return to the Steelers, saying, "That ship has sailed."

Rodgers, who had already said this was his final NFL campaign, had been benched by the Steelers for Friday's game against Denver, with backup Mason Rudolph elevated to the starting role and Rodgers deactivated for the contest.

The shocking call came hours after McCarthy had said Rodgers would be the starter despite struggling in a loss to Philadelphia last Sunday.

Rodgers went on "The Pat McAfee Show" on ESPN on Wednesday and said he only found out about his benching when told by Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth in a phone call.

"This has been months of conversation leading up to the last couple days when things went to a different place," Rodgers said.

Rodgers also accused McCarthy of falling asleep and snoring in team meetings – calling it "not an abnormal week" – and missing team events.

Rodgers said his benching came after he spoke to McCarthy about his complaints in a tense conversation where he sought McCarthy to have someone else call offensive plays.

"If you try and bench me or don't change the play calling then you should just release me, because I feel like at this point I'm doing what's right for the organisation," Rodgers said he told McCarthy.

"He responded with, 'I'm going to do what's right by the organisation,' which in his mind was getting rid of me."

McCarthy spoke briefly just before the Steelers confirmed reports of releasing Rodgers, saying he saw Rodgers's remarks as an "ultimatum" for McCarthy to give up play calling or release him.

"We got to a point, we had talked about some things, communication, things like that, and there was an ultimatum made that was clearly outside his job description," McCarthy said.

"It was my decision to bench him," McCarthy said, adding it also was his call to release Rodgers with the support of Steelers management.

"It was my decision, clearly, and they have fully supported me," he said.

Rodgers also said McCarthy, who was the long-time Green Bay Packers coach during Rodgers' time there, broke a halftime huddle last Sunday by saying, "1-2-3, Packers."

McCarthy, 63, admitted to the moment, saying it was "embarrassing" but an honest mistake after coaching the Packers from 2006-2018.

Asked why he should be considered the right man to lead the Steelers, McCarthy replied, "Because I know how to win and that's the facts."

McCarthy attended a player council meeting that he said could lead to change.

"Very direct. Very honest, I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind," he said.

Rodgers said McCarthy "had already lost a lot of" the defensive unit by not paying enough attention to defensive schemes and skipped or was late to watch films of opponents, adding it was "not what I signed up for."

McCarthy coached Dallas for five seasons before sitting out the 2025 campaign and taking over the Steelers in January to replace Mike Tomlin.

Rodgers signed a one-year deal to play for the Steelers in 2025 and inked another one-year contract this past May, reuniting with McCarthy but saying four days later that 2026 would be his last NFL season.

He will be available to be claimed by any other team and if he clears waivers would be a free agent.

Rodgers has completed 220 of 361 passes for 2,241 yards and 16 touchdowns this season.

In 22 NFL seasons he has thrown for 68,515 yards and 543 touchdowns – third most in league history. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: PSG held in Champions League as Barca win big
articles.excerpt: Paris Saint-Germain lost their perfect record in the Champions League as Roma held them to a 2-2 draw on Wednesday…
articles.fullText:
Paris Saint-Germain lost their perfect record in the Champions League as Roma held them to a 2-2 draw on Wednesday, while Anthony Gordon got a brace in Baku as Barcelona eased to victory over Sabah.

Bayern Munich slipped to a 2-1 loss at Lille, further denting their hopes of an automatic last-16 berth via a top-eight finish in the league phase.

Liverpool, meanwhile, cruised to a 3-0 win at Club Brugge thanks to an Alexander Isak brace either side of a fine Florian Wirtz strike.

On a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, Donyell Malen's 17th goal in 16 matches this season denied Luis Enrique's twice defending champions as they failed to keep pace with Real Madrid, who are now the only remaining team with a 100 percent record in the competition.

The Dutch forward's 78th-minute penalty ensured the sides finished level after Illia Zabarnyi's header and Ousmane Dembele's spot-kick had flipped the script for the hosts following Mario Hermoso's early opener for Roma.

"It was the hardest match we have had this season and I am happy with the result," said PSG coach Luis Enrique. "I hope we don't have to play them later on over two legs."

The result brought an end to a run of 12 consecutive wins for PSG, who have lost key attackers Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to injury recently, but they nonetheless look highly likely to secure a top-eight finish and avoid the play-off round, unlike in their last two campaigns.

A point further back than PSG lie Barcelona after Hansi Flick's charges showed no signs of missing Lamine Yamal as they beat Sabah 4-1.

With the teenage star out with an ankle knock, England winger Gordon continued his love affair with the Azerbaijani capital.

He scored twice either side of half-time to put Barca firmly in control, taking his tally in the city to six after he scored four goals in his previous appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for previous club Newcastle last season.

"I've been very successful here," Gordon said. "Two goals, I'm happy with that.

"A good performance, all in all, very good."

Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions before Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah.

Bayern added a first defeat to their two wins and two draws so far in the competition as Vincent Kompany's injury-plagued side languish in 15th spot on eight points.

"There are no excuses. It's simply the reality we face, and we have to stand together," Kompany said as Bayern tasted defeat for the first time this season.

With men's Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane set for a stretch on the sidelines and Michael Olise also missing, centre-half Dayot Upamecano stepped into his illustrious colleagues' goalscoring boots to put Bayern ahead early on.

However, Japanese forward Ayase Ueda levelled for Lille just after the hour before calamity struck three minutes later as Aleksandar Pavlovic horribly misjudged his attempted clearance from Ethan Mbappe's shot off the post and scuffed the ball into his own net.

Liverpool's £125 million signing Isak said he was "in a good place" after netting twice in Belgium to bring his tally for the season to 10 in all competitions after struggling last season to justify the hefty price tag.

Two crisp finishes by the Swede in both halves, with Wirtz continuing his own fine form of late after a difficult first season at Anfield with a fizzling 79th-minute strike, got Liverpool back to winning ways in the Champions League as they climbed to fifth.

Elsewhere, Inter Milan and Atletico Madrid both enjoyed 2-0 home wins over Stuttgart and Viking, respectively. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Sporting deny Pochettino first win with Man United
articles.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach after a wild 2-2 Champions League draw at…
articles.fullText:
Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach after a wild 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, with the hosts equalising thanks to a goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens.

The Belgian stopper's poor handling allowed Luis Suarez to complete a brace for the hosts, cancelling out United playmaker Bruno Fernandes's double against his former side.

United gave away two penalties in the first half, the second converted by Suarez, before Fernandes equalised from the spot early in the second half.

Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez's acrobatic effort levelled the game.

United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match.

A crushing 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick.

Pochettino brought Harry Maguire into the three-man defence as he shuffled his pack, as well as starting Joshua Zirkzee in place of the suspended Matheus Cunha.

Neither side took many risks in the opening stages, with few chances of note until the game burst into life midway through the first half as United lost control.

Lisandro Martinez brought down Geny Catamo in the area and Sporting were awarded a penalty.

The hosts blew their chance from the spot, with Suarez's scuffed effort easily saved by Lammens, but the Red Devils gave away another spot kick just a couple of minutes later.

Goalkeeper Lammens came flying off his line and clattered Maxi Araujo, and this time Colombian striker Suarez made no mistake from the spot.

United thought they had equalised when Amad Diallo hit the crossbar and then nodded home the rebound, but the goal was disallowed to their dismay.

Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio, although he seemed to win the ball, upsetting United further after Leny Yoro's controversial red card against Liverpool on Sunday that was later rescinded.

Fernandes pulled United level early in the second half from the spot after Eduardo Quaresma brought down Martinez.

The former Sporting playmaker calmly stroked his penalty beyond the dive of Kaique Pereira into the bottom left corner.

Fernandes said on the eve of the game he had stopped contract talks because he wanted to focus on helping United improve their form after a dire start to the season.

The midfielder soon had his second goal, with the help of a bizarre bounce off a divot on the pitch.

Fernandes's low effort from distance seemed bound for Pereira's hands, but suddenly bounced up off a patch of uneven turf and fortuitously over the goalkeeper's head.

The Portugal international bent a free-kick narrowly off target as he looked to complete his hat-trick.

Lammens saved well from Sergi Altimira to protect United's lead as Sporting battled to find an equaliser.

It eventually came from a howler from Lammens, who failed to claim a cross dropping out of the sky, spilling the ball in front of Suarez, who produced a hooked acrobatic effort to score.

Moments later United had the ball in the net at the other end after another goalkeeping error by Pereira, who mishandled Fernandes's corner, pushing the ball into his own net.

However what would have been the winner was disallowed for an elbow by Patrick Dorgu on the goalkeeper, a decision the visitors were also unhappy about. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies at 65
articles.excerpt: Andy Taylor, the guitarist and songwriter for pop-rock band Duran Duran and a Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee…
articles.fullText:
Andy Taylor, the guitarist and songwriter for pop-rock band Duran Duran and a Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee, died at age 65 on Monday, according to a joint statement from his family and former bandmates released on Wednesday.

Taylor, who co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits, including “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “Rio,” and “Girls on Film,” died from metastatic prostate cancer. He was diagnosed in 2018.

The first section of the statement came from his family, while the second was from Duran Duran members Simon Le Bon, Nick Rhodes, John Taylor and Roger Taylor.

"To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," Taylor's wife, Tracy Wilson-Taylor, said on behalf of his family.

The members of the Grammy-winning band noted that Taylor brought a unique style to their sound.

"Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music," they said, adding that he faced his illness with courage, honesty and grace.

Taylor's rock- and funk-inspired riffs drove the British band's dance floor hits such as "Girls on Film" and "Rio".

The band enjoyed huge success in the 1980s, with their popularity in the United States compared to Beatlemania.

They have sold more than 100 million records, had 30 top 40 singles in their native UK and 21 top 40 hits in the US charts.

The band were also one of the first to harness the advent of the music video, to burnish a sophisticated and seductive image.

Taylor joined Duran Duran in 1980, travelling from Tyneside to the band's base in Birmingham, central England, in response to an advert in a music magazine.

The group released its debut album a year later, with first single "Planet Earth" peaking at number 12.

But it was their third single, "Girls on Film", accompanied by a raunchy video featuring topless women mud wrestling, that catapulted Duran Duran to global fame.

Their second album "Rio" (1982) spawned global hits such as "Save a Prayer" and saw Princess Diana claim Duran Duran as her favourite band.

Nile Rodgers produced "The Reflex" which became the band's first US number one in 1985, the same year they recorded James Bond theme "View to a Kill" and played in front of 90,000 people during the Philadelphia "Live Aid" event.

It appeared they were at the peak of their powers, but internal divisions were beginning to take their toll, and Taylor left the band in 1986 to pursue other projects.

He was due to reunite with the band for their induction ceremony into The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022.

But he was unable to attend, and the band instead revealed his illness during their onstage speech.

In accepting the honour, Le Bon read an open letter from Taylor, who said that just over four years previously he was diagnosed with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.

"Many families have experienced the slow burn of this disease and of course, we are no different," Taylor wrote.

Speaking to journalists backstage at the ceremony, Le Bon called the news "absolutely devastating".

"We love Andy dearly," he said. "I'm not going to stand here and cry, I think that would be inappropriate, but that's what it feels like."

Taylor told UK television's Channel 5 News that he was determined to "live life" despite the terminal prognosis.

"I often say to people, every minute's like an hour, every day's like a week. You really want to get the most out of life," he said.

"I've been very fortunate, I've had so much, in terms of living the dream, but because I do music, I think that's probably really helped me to live with pessimism of an incurable disease."

Taylor was married to his wife Tracey for over 40 years and had four children, living together in Ibiza, Spain. (Agencies)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Brazil, EU slam proposed US tariffs
articles.excerpt: Brazil's government on Wednesday slammed "unacceptable" US proposals to impose tariffs on Brazilian aircraft and sugar, as part of a…
articles.fullText:
Brazil's government on Wednesday slammed "unacceptable" US proposals to impose tariffs on Brazilian aircraft and sugar, as part of a battery of new levies on major trading partners.

"The unilateral decision by the USTR [Office of the United States Trade Representative] is an unacceptable action within the ongoing bilateral negotiation process," President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's office said in a statement.

"Brazil will not yield to this type of threat," the presidency added, also saying that it was not ruling out "reciprocal measures."

Washington has proposed adding a 10-percent tariff on aircraft from Brazil, home of aerospace manufacturer Embraer.

The Brazilian government stressed that it had been negotiating "in good faith" with Washington for over a year and that the two sides had agreed in August to establish a working group on trade issues.

Brazil will continue to seek "a negotiated solution" without renouncing the right to bring challenges before the World Trade Organization, the presidency said.

The EU said on Wednesday that it rejected the premise of the proposed new tariffs and expected Washington to stick by a deal struck with Brussels last year.

"We will study the findings," European Commission spokesman Olof Gill said.

"At the same time we strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity. To the contrary, Europe is among those most exposed to overcapacity," he said.

The Commission would continue engaging with Washington on implementing a tariff deal struck in 2025 to cap Trump's duties on the bloc at 15 percent, he added.

"We expect any measure from this investigation to respect it in full, including when combined with existing duties," Gill said. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Jailed Kenyan cult leader convicted of child assault
articles.excerpt: A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher was on Wednesday convicted of assault and cruelty against children, barely a month after being sentenced…
articles.fullText:
A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher was on Wednesday convicted of assault and cruelty against children, barely a month after being sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of children in an infamous starvation cult.

Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the sect's base near the coastal resort of Malindi, in what became known as the "Shakahola Forest Massacre."

Paul Mackenzie has faced multiple charges linked to the cult in different courts. On Wednesday, a children's court in Mombasa convicted him and 11 others of several offences against children in a case that heard evidence from 13 minors who survived the cult.

The magistrate said Mackenzie was convicted on one count of "assault causing actual bodily harm" and five counts of "cruelty to a child."

Others convicted alongside Mackenzie were also found guilty of violating children's right to education.

The court acquitted 24 other defendants in the case, which has been ongoing for more than two years.

Mackenzie also faces charges of radicalisation and manslaughter, with rulings expected this week, according to local media.

Mackenzie was arrested in April 2023 after a rights group alerted authorities and some followers were rescued from the 325-hectare ranch in the Shakahola forest on Kenya's coast.

The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights put the death toll at 429 in 2024. Some victims remain unidentified.

The case has fuelled calls for tighter regulation of religious organisations, after it emerged that Mackenzie had previously been arrested twice but released.

He established the Good News International Church in 2003 and set up branches in Nairobi and along Kenya's coast that attracted thousands of devotees, though he claimed it closed in 2019.

He was arrested in 2017 over charges of "radicalisation" but was acquitted. He was arrested again in 2019 in relation to two child deaths at Shakahola but released on bail. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US Q3 GDP revised upwards but inflation surges
articles.excerpt: US GDP growth in the third quarter was revised strongly upwards on Wednesday, with the US Commerce Department citing strong…
articles.fullText:
US GDP growth in the third quarter was revised strongly upwards on Wednesday, with the US Commerce Department citing strong investment and consumer spending, as the Fed's preferred inflation gauge hit a three-year high in October.

US GDP growth in the third quarter this year was estimated at 4.3 percent, the department's Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) said, a rise of 0.9 percentage points from the previous estimate and much higher than market expectations.

"Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports," the BEA said in a statement.

The US economy has shown resilient growth in recent months despite facing significant headwinds, including from US President Donald Trump's chaotic tariff policies and his war on Iran, which has driven up energy prices.

Also on Wednesday, the US Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge came in at a three-year high in October, according to BEA data, with a rise in energy prices accompanied by an increase in non-durable goods inflation.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index rose by 3.8 percent year-on-year in October, the data showed, matching a three-year high set in May.

The US Federal Reserve has a long-term two-percent target for PCE inflation, one that it has missed for almost six years.

In September, the Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years in order to combat the persistent price increases, which have battered US households and businesses.

The Fed's Open Market Committee (FOMC) held rates steady at its last meeting in October, but with inflation continuing to run hot it is likely to raise rates at its next confab in December.

The years of above-target inflation since the pandemic have hit US households hard, with current price levels more than 30 percent higher than in 2020, as per the official Consumer Price Index.

Affordability was a key issue in this month's midterm elections, which saw Trump's Republican Party swept out of power in both houses of Congress by their rival Democrats.

The price increases have been driven by Trump's tariffs, energy price increases due to the war on Iran and a massive investment boom in AI technology driving up demand for some goods.

Trump has defended his economic performance by pointing to data like GDP growth, which has been robust despite the headwinds, mainly on the back of the AI boom.

Economists warn that while consumer spending has remained strong, despite the high prices, there is a growing divide between lower- and higher-income households in the United States. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Wall Street mixed as slide saved by bargain hunters
articles.excerpt: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq retreated on Wednesday amid an AI-related selloff, but finished well off the day's lows…
articles.fullText:
The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq retreated on Wednesday amid an AI-related selloff, but finished well off the day's lows as bargain hunters stepped in ahead of the US Thanksgiving holiday.

The Dow finished higher.

The Nasdaq fell more than 4 percent early in the session as the selloff in AI-related stocks and new US tariff proposals hit sentiment.

"There are all these potential headwinds, but then there's also a certain amount of conditioning of buying on the dip, and that's part of what we're seeing," said Oliver Pursche, senior vice president and adviser for Wealthspire Advisors in Westport, Connecticut.

"The broad selloffs tend to kind of throw the baby out with the bathwater. Investors are taking advantage of some of those discrepancies," he said.

Wall Street has been roiled this month, partly because of worries about AI leader Nvidia. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month, but the company's board reinstated him on Monday. The Nasdaq Composite is down 7.3 percent for the month.

"This has broadly been a more sentiment-driven type of selloff," said Charlie Ripley, senior investment strategist at Allianz Investment Management.

At the same time, for some companies from a price-to-earnings perspective, "things are starting to look more attractive," he said.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 164.25 points, or 0.3 percent, to 50,182.95, the S&P 500 lost 18.31 points, or 0.3 percent, to 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 147.73 points, or 0.6 percent, to 23,585.80.

The US market will be closed on Thursday and will close early on Friday.

Nvidia shares fell 3.9 percent and an index of semiconductors was off 0.7 percent, while shares of Amazon fell 3.1 percent. On the plus side, PC maker HP gained 11.5 percent after it reported fourth-quarter revenue and profit above analysts' estimates.

Fears of increased regulatory scrutiny of the AI sector following the Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections have added to worries about AI stocks. Early in the day, the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20 percent from its record closing high, flirting with bear-market territory.

New tariffs could cloud the outlook for investors grappling with the prospect of interest rates staying higher for longer, as inflation has accelerated and oil prices have risen steadily due to the Iran war.

The US proposed tariffs on goods from 14 trading partners to combat what it calls structural excess industrial capacity, reviving global trade tensions.

In addition, investors digested data showing the US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation increased further in October, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise rates next month and again in early 2027.

"Tariffs are somewhat responsible for inflation... so that's actually being counterproductive to what the Fed is trying to do," said Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities in New York. (Reuters)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: US proposes tariffs on trade partners, including China
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and…
articles.fullText:
US President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in US midterm elections.

His administration proposed new maximum potential rates of 20 percent to 40 percent to counter excess industrial capacity that it says these countries are promoting. But the US Trade Representative's office said it intends to cap new tariffs at lower levels agreed under trade deals that are completed or still under negotiation.

In unveiling the results of an eight-month unfair trade practices investigation into excess industrial capacity, USTR aims to more fully rebuild Trump's tariff leverage after the Supreme Court in February struck down his broad global duties under a national emergencies law.

Under the excess factory capacity probe, USTR said China would face the highest capped rate of 20 percent, which would be added to duties of roughly 25 percent imposed during Trump's first term.

That rate would comply with a US-China trade truce that expires on January 10. But if the truce unravels, China's rate would rise to 40 percent, the USTR said.

Vietnam would face a capped tariff rate of 20 percent if it reaches a trade agreement with Washington, rising to 35 percent if negotiations fail.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the tariffs, which would not take effect until after a January 25 public hearing, were intended to counteract "industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labour suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market-distorting practices" that undermine the US manufacturing base.

The duties would not stack on top of prior tariffs of 10 percent or 12.5 percent imposed under a separate US probe into allegedly lax enforcement of anti-forced labour laws in 60 economies, nor would they add to sectoral national security duties on steel, aluminium, autos and other goods.

Greer said the proposed tariffs also would not apply to about US$30 billion of Chinese imports under consideration for tariff reductions through a bilateral mechanism known as the Board of Trade.

Washington has long accused China of subsidising industry and flooding global markets with low-cost exports ranging from steel to electric vehicles and solar products.

A spokesperson for China's embassy in Washington rejected allegations that China is a source of excess capacity.

"The so-called issue of 'industrial overcapacity' does not really exist and should not be used as a pretext for political manipulation," the spokesperson said, urging the two sides to jointly deliver on agreements between President Xi Jinping and Trump.

Speaking before the new tariffs were announced, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said tariff wars and trade wars serve no one's interests, adding that both sides should resolve economic and trade issues through consultation on the basis of equality, respect and mutual benefit.

The USTR also proposed capped tariff rates of 18 percent for imported goods from Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Bangladesh, and 15 percent, including existing "Most Favoured Nation" duties, for Japan, South Korea, the EU and Switzerland.

India, which has yet to reach a trade deal with the Trump administration, would face a 17 percent tariff rate if an agreement is finalised and a 25 percent rate if talks fail, the USTR said. Singapore would receive a capped tariff rate of 10 percent.

Mexico and Norway were excluded from the proposals because investigations into their trade practices remain under way, Greer said.

Separately, USTR proposed a new 10 percent tariff on imports of Brazil's finished Embraer commercial aircraft, and an increase in duties on imports of Brazilian sugar that exceed quotas as part of an effort to push Brasilia to rectify alleged unfair trade practices.

The products were previously exempted from Trump's 25 percent tariffs on Brazilian goods that were imposed in July under a separate Section 301 investigation. Greer said he decided to propose the tariff increases after months of talks between the US and Brazil made "no meaningful progress." (Reuters/Xinhua)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Can hackers still read Gmail after a password change?
articles.excerpt: Remus Stealer malware developers claim Gmail access survives a password change, but Google says the attack targets infected devices, not…
articles.fullText:
You change your Gmail password after noticing something suspicious. You sign out of unfamiliar devices and figure your account should be safe again. But what if someone could still read your Gmail after a password change? That's the unsettling claim behind Remus Stealer, a malware service being marketed to cybercriminals. Its developers claim they can keep accessing Gmail messages even after someone resets their password and revokes existing sessions.
However, security researchers have not independently verified those claims, and Google disputes the suggestion that the malware exploits a Gmail security flaw. The company says this type of attack targets infected devices rather than Gmail itself. Google also warns that changing your password may not solve the problem if malware remains active on your computer. Here's what the investigation uncovered and how to protect your inbox.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
CHEAP ANDROID PHONES FOUND WITH MALWARE ALREADY INSTALLED
Security researchers at Hudson Rock examined promotional materials for Remus Stealer, a type of malware designed to collect sensitive information from infected computers. In a November 9 report, the company described a new feature advertised in version 1.3.9 of the malware. The developers claim it allows criminals to open a compromised Gmail inbox directly from their control dashboard. The promotional screenshots show lists of emails and individual messages. There's also a "Mail" option connected to records of infected devices. According to the developers, criminals can retrieve email verification codes without collecting browser cookie files.
The developers make an even more concerning claim. They say changing a Google password or revoking existing sessions won't necessarily stop someone from accessing the mailbox. They also advertise a way to share mailbox access with other criminals through links. Think about what that could mean if the claims prove true. Someone with access to your Gmail could potentially read private conversations or collect password reset messages for other accounts. However, these claims come from the people selling the malware. Independent researchers have yet to demonstrate that the feature works as advertised.
Hudson Rock contacted the malware developer and spoke with someone who claimed to have used the Gmail feature. That person said they could still access an inbox after closing the browser, resetting a session and changing the Google account password. The developer also described a technique involving browser memory but didn't provide enough technical information to verify it. There are important limits to the investigation.
Hudson Rock did not reverse engineer the feature or conduct controlled testing after a complete account recovery. Researchers also couldn't independently verify the customer's claims. Most importantly, the investigation never established that criminals could retrieve newly arriving emails after someone had properly secured their Google account. The screenshots demonstrate that the service advertises a Gmail-reading interface. They don't prove that Remus can defeat Google's protections after a full recovery. There's also no evidence in the report of a previously unknown Gmail security vulnerability.
Researchers also could not rule out other explanations, including incomplete session revocation, previously collected messages or unauthorized access that remained active through another route. Without controlled testing, there's no way to confirm exactly how the advertised feature operates.
NEW AI MALWARE RANKS VICTIMS BY HOW MUCH THEY'RE WORTH
We reached out to Google about the research, and the company rejected the suggestion that the reported activity involved a vulnerability in Gmail. A Google spokesperson said: "Attacks involving infostealer malware that target session tokens on personal devices are not new, and there is no Gmail or Google vulnerability at play here. We routinely upgrade our built-in defenses to protect users against session theft and automatically secure accounts when we detect suspicious activity. Users can invalidate stolen sessions by removing malware from the affected device and revoking active sessions via g.co/mydevices."
Google explained that this kind of attack targets infected personal devices rather than exploiting Gmail itself. The company also highlighted something especially important for anyone recovering from malware. If the infection remains on a computer when someone resets their password, the malware could capture the new login session. That means a fresh password alone may not solve the problem. Google recommends removing the malware before signing back in on the affected device. From a separate, trusted device, you should also change your password, revoke suspicious sessions through Google's device activity page at myaccount.google.com/device-activity and review your account using Security Checkup at myaccount.google.com/security-checkup. The infected computer should remain disconnected until the threat has been removed.
The company says it regularly strengthens its defenses against stolen sessions. Those protections include frequent cookie rotation and additional authentication checks when someone attempts sensitive account changes. Google also highlighted Device Bound Session Credentials, a Chrome security technology designed to make stolen session cookies harder to reuse on another device. This protection applies to supported Chrome sessions, with availability depending on the platform and service. These protections help reduce the risk of account theft, although they don't eliminate every possible malware attack.
You probably open Gmail every day without typing your password. That's because your browser remembers that you've already signed in. Behind the scenes, browsers and applications use session cookies or authentication tokens to maintain access to accounts. These digital credentials help keep you signed in without repeatedly entering your password. Unfortunately, criminals know how valuable that information can be. Infostealer malware can target stored authentication data on an infected computer. If an attacker obtains a valid session, they may be able to access an account without entering the password again. That can also undermine the protection you'd normally expect from two-step verification because the legitimate account holder has already completed the sign-in process.
However, a stolen session doesn't automatically give someone unlimited access. Google can invalidate sessions, and some sensitive actions require additional verification. Google's documentation explains that changing a password generally revokes OAuth access and refresh tokens used by applications with Gmail permissions, although certain exceptions apply. Google also notes that password changes sign people out of most devices, but some trusted devices and third-party connections may remain signed in. Those exceptions do not prove that Remus uses any of these methods. The concern with an infected computer is that malware may capture fresh authentication information when you sign in again. That's why securing the computer and reviewing account access are essential parts of recovery.
An unfamiliar Google security alert deserves attention, especially if you haven't signed in from a new device. You should also investigate password reset messages you never requested. These can indicate that someone is attempting to access another account connected to your email address, although an unexpected reset message alone doesn't prove an account has been compromised.
Other warning signs include missing messages or people telling you they received strange emails from your address. Check your Sent folder for messages you didn't write. You might also discover forwarding rules or account recovery settings you don't remember changing. If something looks suspicious, open your Google account directly rather than following a link in an unexpected message.
If you suspect that someone has accessed your Gmail, take action promptly. The goal is to secure your account while preventing malware from stealing fresh login information. Google emphasizes that removing the infection and revoking compromised sessions are both essential. You can begin securing your account from a trusted device while keeping the suspected infected computer offline.
If you believe your computer has been infected, disconnect it from the internet. Use a separate, trusted device to begin securing your important accounts.
Strong antivirus protection with real-time scanning can help prevent infostealers from gaining access in the first place. However, no antivirus program can guarantee that every threat will be detected. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at CyberGuy.com
Use a trusted device to secure your Google account. If you suspect that malware stole your login information, change your password promptly and make sure the infected computer cannot capture another session. Do not sign back into Google on the suspected infected computer until you have removed the malware.
Google notes that several sessions can appear under the same device name. Review each one and sign out of any you cannot confidently identify. If you've already changed your password while malware was still running, make sure the infected device has been cleaned or remains offline, then change your password again from a trusted device and review active sessions once more.
A criminal who gains access to your Gmail may change settings so incoming messages get forwarded to another email address. That could allow someone to receive copies of new messages even after you change your password. Google requires verification when someone adds a new forwarding address, but you should still check for forwarding that may have been configured without your knowledge.
To check your Gmail settings on a computer:
Some third-party applications can access parts of your Google account after you grant permission. If an unfamiliar app has access to your Gmail, it deserves a closer look.
You can also read my CyberGuy guide on apps accessing your Google account for additional instructions.
Google recommends several protections that can make account takeovers harder.
Passkeys offer stronger sign-in security, but they cannot remove an existing infection or automatically prevent theft of an already authenticated session. Google's Advanced Protection Program adds stricter account safeguards, including tighter restrictions on third-party access.
Remember how many online services use your email address for account recovery. If criminals accessed your mailbox, they may have seen verification messages from other services. Review important accounts for unfamiliar activity. Pay particular attention to unexpected password changes or security alerts.
If you reused your Google password anywhere else, change those passwords too. Use unique credentials for every important account, and consider a password manager to keep track of them. For additional protection, my CyberGuy article on identity thieves who don't need your password explains other ways criminals try to get around traditional account security.
For years, changing your password has been one of the first things I've recommended when an online account gets compromised. I still believe that's essential. But this investigation highlights something many people overlook. If malware is running on your computer, it may be able to steal fresh login information after you've changed your password. What concerns me is how much of our digital lives depend on a single Gmail account. Think about the personal messages sitting in your inbox and the accounts that rely on your email for password recovery.
Someone who gains access could potentially create problems well beyond your inbox. Google's response makes an important distinction. This is a threat involving malware on infected devices, not a newly demonstrated vulnerability in Gmail. We should also remember that the most alarming claims about this malware have yet to be independently verified. There's a big difference between what criminals advertise and what security researchers can actually demonstrate.
My advice is to take account security seriously without panicking over an unproven claim. Keep strong antivirus protection running on your devices and pay attention to suspicious account activity. If you suspect an infection, make sure the malware has been removed before trusting a fresh login. Then change your password from a trusted device and revoke any suspicious sessions. Those extra steps can help prevent someone from regaining access to your account.
If you discovered that a hacker had been reading your Gmail, would changing your password restore your confidence, or would you feel compelled to abandon that email address entirely? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com
