articles.title: North Korea’s naval buildup poses new security challenges for US, South Korea: expert
articles.excerpt: Questions remain over Pyongyang’s ability to sustain its warships amid vulnerabilities and rising costs.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean .
North Korea’s push to build increasingly large warships could pose new security challenges for South Korea and the United States, but questions remain over whether Pyongyang has the military capabilities and financial resources to operate the ships effectively, security experts told Radio Free Asia.
North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un has made naval modernization a priority, commissioning two 5,000-ton destroyers this year while pursuing even larger surface combatants.
The first destroyer, the Choe Hyon, entered service in June, followed by the Kang Kon in September. During a Nov. 2 visit to the Nampo shipyard, southwest of the capital Pyongyang, Kim inspected what state media described as an enormous new warship, with photographs revealing part of its lower hull.
The destroyers mark a significant departure from North Korea’s traditionally coastal-focused navy, which has relied heavily on smaller vessels. The new larger ships are designed to carry a wider range of weapons, including missiles capable of striking targets at greater distances.
North Korea also conducted tests of new torpedoes in October and November, underscoring Pyongyang’s efforts to expand its naval capabilities.
This picture taken on July 3, 2026 and released by North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) via KNS on July 5, 2026 shows North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un (C) observing performance tests of the main weapons systems of the destroyer Kang Kon at an undisclosed location in North Korea.
(STR/KCNA via KNS/AFP) Unlike land-based missile launchers, warships can move across large maritime areas, potentially giving North Korea more options for launching strikes and complicating efforts to track nuclear weapons within the isolated country.
Bruce Bennett, a former senior researcher at the California-based RAND Corporation, told RFA Korean that the destroyers could add another dimension to North Korea’s nuclear threat.
“North Korea is diversifying its means for delivering nuclear weapons. … Its destroyers are designed to carry nuclear weapons, and they will likely do so as part of this diversification process,” said Bennett. “By doing so, it hopes to make it very difficult for the United States to carry out a disarming attack on its nuclear forces. It will have too many targets of too many different types.”
A senior officer in Japan’s Maritime Self-Defense Force, who spoke to RFA Korean on condition of anonymity, also said the destroyers could carry tactical nuclear weapons, increasing the threat posed by Pyongyang’s expanding fleet.
The officer noted that North Korea had likely relied on Chinese and Russian technology to build the destroyers, which appear to be beyond its existing capabilities.
The destroyers’ hulls resemble China’s Type 052D Luyang III-class destroyers, while their radar systems resemble those of Russia’s Admiral Gorshkov-class frigates, suggesting Pyongyang may have drawn on Chinese shipbuilding expertise and Russian weapons technology, according to the officer.
Despite their potential threat, however, the vessels face significant operational limitations, particularly against aircraft and submarines, the officer said.
“Large surface vessels are exposed to threats from the air and underwater. Surface warships cannot operate independently,” the officer said.
Modern naval operations require multiple layers of protection, including onboard air defense systems, early warning aircraft and fighter jets capable of intercepting incoming threats.
North Korea tested an airborne early warning aircraft in March 2025, but South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said at the time that its operational threat remained limited despite potential improvements in surveillance capabilities.
Pyongyang’s fighter fleet also faces disadvantages. In December 2024, U.S. Indo-Pacific Command chief Adm. Samuel Paparo raised the possibility that North Korea could acquire MiG-29 and Su-27 fighter jets.
However, both are fourth-generation aircraft that would face significant challenges against the more advanced fifth-generation F-35 fighters operated by South Korea and the United States, potentially limiting Pyongyang’s ability to protect its warships.
The Japanese officer also questioned the destroyers’ ability to counter submarines, particularly in the complex waters east of the Korean Peninsula.
“The Sea of Japan is an extremely difficult area in which to detect submarines because of its complex currents and salinity distribution,” said the officer, referring to the body of water east of the Korean Peninsula, also known as the East Sea.
“Without combining patrol aircraft such as the P-3C or P-8, it is impossible to locate submarines. North Korean destroyers would not be able to defend themselves against submarine attacks.”
The officer added that even stealth-designed warships could be quickly detected by satellites or high-altitude reconnaissance drones.
This picture taken on Sept. 6, 2026 and released by North Korea's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) on Sept. 7, 2026 shows North Korean leader Kim Jong Un (C on platform) seeing off the destroyer "Kang Kon" duing a commissioning ceremony was held at Wonsan Port in Kangwon Province.
(KCNA via KNS/AFP) Political ambitions and mounting costs
Despite those challenges, Kim appears determined to build vessels even larger than Choe Hyon and Kang Kon, reflecting a longstanding North Korean ambition to develop a powerful navy.
That ambition dates back to the reign of Kim’s late grandfather, national founder Kim Il Sung. Pyongyang has long viewed its naval inferiority as a strategic disadvantage, believing it left the country unable to challenge the Northern Limit Line, a disputed maritime boundary established by the U.N. Command after the 1953 Korean War armistice, that places several islands near North Korea’s shore under South Korean control.
But a Japanese government official, who spoke to RFA Korean on condition of anonymity, suggested the younger Kim’s pursuit of increasingly large vessels may reflect personal ambition rather than purely military requirements.
“This may reflect Chairman Kim’s personal desire to possess enormous warships,” the official said.
The official argued that North Korea’s centralized political system could encourage military planners to prioritize the leader’s preferences over operational considerations.
“I believe Kim – who aspires to match countries such as South Korea and the United States – has become fixated on building impressive-looking large warships, so he has issued orders that disregard military rationality,” the official said.
The official added that North Korean military officers and engineers faced pressure to satisfy the leadership, with those opposing Kim’s views risking punishment.
Lee Hyun-ju, who was once Seoul’s consul general in Osaka and who previously headed the South Korean office of the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization, or KEDO, told RFA that military officers in North Korea know that the wisest course of action is to demonstrate loyalty and respect toward Kim Jong Un.
“They also know that displaying intense hatred and aggression toward anyone who insults the supreme leader is the safest approach,” he added.
Beyond their operational limitations, the warships could impose substantial financial costs on North Korea’s economy.
The expense comes as North Korea continues to face international sanctions imposed over its nuclear and missile programs, restricting its access to foreign markets and technology.
According to Japan Self-Defense Forces officials, building a 5,000-ton destroyer would cost at least 50 billion yen (US$314.2 million), even after accounting for the country’s relatively low labor costs.
That would be roughly equivalent to North Korea’s total exports in 2024, according to the officials’ estimate.
“Building a destroyer also requires spending on maintenance, repairs and other operating costs,” a Self-Defense Forces official told RFA Korean. “This would represent a considerable burden for North Korea.”
Edited by Taejun Kang and Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Apple tightens Mac security as AI agents seek your files
articles.excerpt: Apple's macOS 27.3 beta 2 adds new Mac security controls for AI agents, letting you pick specific protected folders instead…
articles.fullText:
Ever download an app on your Mac and click through the permission requests without giving them much thought? You're certainly not alone. But what if one of those approvals gave an AI assistant access to your private messages, financial documents or even files you thought were protected?
That's the concern behind Apple's latest Mac security controls . As AI agents become more capable of performing tasks on your computer, they're also requesting access to more personal information. And once you grant certain permissions, an app could potentially see far more than you intended.
Now, Apple is introducing new protections in macOS 27.3 that give you greater control over what these apps can access . The changes arrived in macOS 27.3 beta 2 on Nov. 16, with the broader software release still to come. Here's what Apple is changing and why you may want to check your Mac's privacy settings now.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
MALICIOUS BROWSER EXTENSIONS CAN HIJACK AI ASSISTANTS
AI assistants have become increasingly useful, especially when you want help getting through a long list of tasks. An AI agent can go further by interacting with apps and taking actions on your behalf. For example, you might ask an AI agent to organize your Downloads folder or find a receipt buried in your email. To complete those tasks, the software may request permission to access information stored on your Mac. That's where things can get uncomfortable. Some apps request a powerful macOS permission called Full Disk Access , which can give them access to nearly everything stored on your computer, including information from other apps.
Apple warns that an app with this permission can read or modify sensitive files. It may also be able to delete or export information without asking you again. And the potential exposure goes beyond documents . Another powerful permission, called System & App Protection Override , can allow an app to control your Mac and monitor activity, including keystrokes, when you grant unrestricted access. That's a lot of trust to place in software, especially when an AI agent can take actions without asking you to approve every step.
Apple's upcoming update introduces several changes designed to make powerful permissions easier to understand. It also gives Mac owners more opportunities to limit access before an app starts working.
Apple is separating its existing Device Control and Data Access permission system into two settings: System & App Protection Override and Accessibility . The change helps clarify when an app is requesting permission to bypass built-in protections. Apple is also introducing more detailed warnings about the information an app could access if you approve its request. Instead of clicking through a vague permission prompt, you'll have more information about what you're allowing.
One of the biggest changes involves Full Disk Access . Starting with macOS 27.3, some apps requesting this permission will let you choose specific protected folders instead of granting access to everything. Other apps may continue using the existing approval process, depending on their purpose.
For example, an AI tool helping you organize work documents may only need access to one folder. You could grant that limited permission while keeping other protected information off-limits. Apple is also introducing a more consistent process for granting these permissions. You'll select the requesting app from a list rather than navigating different approval methods.
Another important addition gives you more control over how AI agents interact with other apps . When configuring System & App Protection Override , you can choose which apps an AI tool may control. For each approved app, you can select Ask First or At Any Time . Choosing Ask First means the AI agent must request permission before controlling that app. That extra confirmation may slow down some automated tasks, but it also gives you an opportunity to catch unwanted actions.
Apple is adding a transparency indicator that appears when an app controls another app through this permission system. That could make it easier to recognize when software is acting on your behalf.
MAC MALWARE CAN HIDE COMMANDS IN YOUR ICLOUD CALENDAR
Apple's announcement follows growing scrutiny over how much information AI-powered software can access. In September, a journalist claimed that Meta's Muse AI app had read his private messages without his permission. Meta disputed that account, saying the Messages integration requires explicit permission. Separately, a security vulnerability in OpenAI's ChatGPT Mac app could have allowed attackers to access sensitive information. OpenAI patched the flaw before it was publicly reported.
These incidents highlight the security concerns surrounding increasingly capable AI software. Even legitimate applications can create privacy risks when they receive broad access to personal information. Apple's response focuses on making those permissions more visible and giving people greater control over what they approve. Importantly, the changes won't prevent you from installing AI agents or using apps that genuinely need broader permissions.
There's something worth knowing before assuming the update will automatically protect everything on your Mac. Apple says permissions you've already granted will remain in effect after the update. The new approval experience primarily applies when apps request permissions going forward.
That means an AI app you installed months ago could still have access to information you previously approved. You'll need to review those permissions yourself if you want to change them. Apple is also allowing developers of certain backup and accessibility applications to request special permissions that preserve their existing functionality. This should help prevent legitimate tools from losing features they need to operate.
You can review your Mac's privacy permissions now, even before macOS 27.3 becomes widely available.
Steps may vary slightly depending on your version of macOS.
If you find an app with permissions it no longer needs, you can revoke its access. Depending on your macOS version, you may see a toggle or an option to remove the app from the permission list. For macOS 27.3: Select an app and click the Remove (−) button to revoke access. To replace broad access with a more limited permission, remove the app and add it again. When prompted, choose the specific protected folders or apps it needs.
Keep in mind that some legitimate applications, including backup software and security tools, require extensive access to function properly. Removing their permissions could prevent certain features from working.
AI CHATBOT PRIVACY: WHAT YOUR AI MAY KNOW ABOUT YOU
You don't have to stop using AI assistants to protect your information. A few precautions can help you take advantage of these tools while reducing unnecessary exposure.
When an app requests access to your files, consider whether it needs permission to browse your entire Mac. If the new macOS controls offer a Choose Folder or Choose Apps option, use it to limit the information the software can reach. You can adjust those permissions later if the app needs additional access.
If you're using macOS 27.3, look for the Ask First setting when granting an AI agent permission to control another application. This gives you another opportunity to review what the software wants to do. It's especially useful when an AI tool interacts with apps containing sensitive personal information.
Be careful when installing new AI agents, particularly from unfamiliar websites. We've previously reported how AI-related scams target Mac owners through convincing fake download pages. Stick with official developer websites or the Mac App Store whenever possible. Keep your installed apps updated to receive security fixes.
Your Mac includes built-in malware protection, but reputable antivirus software can add another layer of security. It can help detect malicious downloads and other threats, including malware disguised as legitimate AI tools. However, antivirus software can't reliably prevent an app from accessing information you've already given it permission to use. That's why reviewing your Mac's privacy settings remains important. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.
Even when an app has limited access to your files, you should understand how it handles information you choose to share. Check whether the developer stores your data or sends it to cloud servers. Apple's permission controls can restrict access to protected information on your Mac, but they don't replace an app's privacy policy.
An AI tool may have needed access to a particular folder when you first installed it. That doesn't mean it needs the same permission indefinitely. Periodically check Privacy & Security and remove access that no longer serves a purpose. This is particularly important for AI apps you rarely use.
If you're allowing an AI agent to organize or modify files, make sure you have a recent backup. An automated task could accidentally delete something important or change a document you wanted to keep. Apple's built-in Time Machine can automatically back up your Mac and help you recover files if something goes wrong. For step-by-step instructions, check out our guide on how to back up your computer.
I'm glad Apple is taking a closer look at how much access AI agents can have on our computers. These tools are becoming more capable, and I can see why people would want an assistant that handles repetitive work. But giving an app permission to see everything on your Mac seems like a steep price to pay for convenience. I particularly like the option to make an AI agent ask before controlling another app. That's a level of oversight I would want, especially when personal information is involved. My biggest concern is that previously granted permissions will remain active. Apple can introduce better warnings, but those warnings won't change the decisions you've already made. I'd encourage Mac owners to spend a few minutes reviewing their settings rather than waiting for the next update.
Would you trust an AI assistant with unrestricted access to your Mac if it could save you hours of work, or does the thought of software reading your private information cross a line? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

articles.title: CE visits Wang Fuk Court residents
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee recently visited residents affected by the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po who are temporarily…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee recently visited residents affected by the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po who are temporarily staying in Aberdeen to check on their well-being and the progress of their new housing arrangements. He was joined on last Saturday’s visit by Secretary for Home & Youth Affairs Alice Mak and Secretary for Labour & Welfare Chris Sun.

Residents from two households who expect to move into their new units next month told Mr Lee the properties suited their needs. They added that moving in earlier had greatly eased their minds.

They thanked the Government for its help, including support from the “one social worker per household” scheme and the District Services & Community Care Teams with financial assistance, document replacement and medical arrangements. They also backed the Government’s push for systemic reforms and its fight against bid-rigging.

Mr Lee said the Government is deeply saddened by the suffering caused by the fire and will continue to do everything possible to support Wang Fuk Court residents.

“Through the ‘one social worker per household’ mechanism and the Care Teams, we will continue to follow up comprehensively on residents’ needs in relation to supplies, medical care, emotional support and assistance in choosing new accommodation. We will continue to stand by the residents and provide them with appropriate support to help them start a new life,” he said.

Mr Lee reiterated that the Government is speeding up long-term housing plans to help residents rebuild their lives quickly. At the same time, it is amending six laws to close loopholes in building maintenance and renovation works so similar incidents do not happen again.

He stressed that these legal changes will stop criminals and syndicates from exploiting building maintenance and renovation projects for unlawful gain. This will address public concerns about fraud in building repairs.

The Chief Executive has instructed officials to put residents first, review every stage of building maintenance and renovation and swiftly finish drafting the legislative amendments for the Legislative Council’s scrutiny to strengthen regulation.

The Government also thanked the Tung Wah Group of Hospitals for offering free legal services to help with property purchase matters.

articles.title: GBA legal conference held in Macao
articles.excerpt: Deputy Secretary for Justice Cheung Kwok-kwan today led a delegation to Macao to attend the eighth Greater Bay Area (GBA)…
articles.fullText:
Deputy Secretary for Justice Cheung Kwok-kwan today led a delegation to Macao to attend the eighth Greater Bay Area (GBA) Legal Departments Joint Conference.

Mr Cheung had an in-depth exchange with Guangdong Department of Justice Director-General Chen Xudong and Macao Special Administrative Region Government Secretary for Administration & Justice Wong Sio Chak.

The conference aims to advance the development of the rule of law in the GBA through the collaborative efforts of the three sides.

During the conference, representatives from the legal departments of Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao held in-depth discussions on key areas including mediation, arbitration, legislative collaboration and nurturing legal talent.

They have achieved interim progress in formulating and promoting GBA standards, further strengthening their work on aligning mechanisms and rules.

The three jurisdictions have officially launched the “Platform for Promotion of the GBA Standards on Arbitration & Mediation”.

The first batch of more than 10 arbitration and mediation institutions has joined the platform. They will work closely with the joint conference to promote the relevant GBA standards and gather feedback from the sectors and users.

The initiative aims to facilitate the alignment of arbitration and mediation mechanisms among the three jurisdictions and continuously improve the relevant standards.

Mr Cheung said the mechanisms for the GBA standards on arbitration and mediation will become more comprehensive upon the platform’s establishment, covering the formulation, promotion and refinement of standards. As a result, he added, these benchmarks are not only created, but also put into practice and continuously refined.

In addition, Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao have agreed to advance with research on legislative collaboration.

Mr Cheung said the “Task Force on Expediting the Alignment of Rules & Mechanisms in Guangdong, Hong Kong & Macao”, which he leads, is currently being formed. It will co-ordinate with relevant bureaus and support the joint conference’s work.

The conference also endorsed the GBA Mediator Panel 2026, and the three parties took the opportunity to exchange views on the use of the GBA Arbitrator Panel.

articles.title: LCSD follows up on URBTIX incident
articles.excerpt: The Leisure & Cultural Services Department confirmed today that, as reported by the URBTIX system contractor yesterday, the system was…
articles.fullText:
The Leisure & Cultural Services Department confirmed today that, as reported by the URBTIX system contractor yesterday, the system was illegally accessed in a hacking incident.

Upon discovering the incident, the contractor said it took immediate measures to stop the hack and reviewed the system to ensure its normal operation.

The URBTIX system was developed and is owned by the contractor at its own cost. It mainly provides ticketing services for the department's performance venues.

Preliminary findings suggest that the incident involves the personal data of around 1,300,000 users, including usernames or names, telephone numbers and email addresses. The system does not collect information on users' identity documents and masks credit card information.

The department said it is highly concerned about the incident and has asked the contractor to conduct a detailed investigation and submit a report. It has also reported the matter to the Police Force, the Security Bureau, the Digital Policy Office (DPO) and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD).

Additionally, the department and the contractor are making arrangements to inform people affected. The department is also consulting the PCPD and the DPO in conducting a comprehensive review of the incident with the contractor, with a view to strengthening protection measures for the system and preventing the recurrence of similar incidents.

articles.title: Bill passed for half-rate trading tax
articles.excerpt: The Government has welcomed the Legislative Council’s passage today of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Tax Concessions for Shipping-related Activities &…
articles.fullText:
The Government has welcomed the Legislative Council’s passage today of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Tax Concessions for Shipping-related Activities & Physical Commodity Trading) Bill 2026, which introduces a new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity trading and enhances existing tax concessions for shipping-related activities.

The amendment ordinance will be published in the Government Gazette on December 4. The relevant tax concessions will apply to qualifying profits from years of assessment beginning on or after April 1, 2025.

The new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity trading is designed to attract commodity traders to establish a presence in Hong Kong. Where a qualifying trader has incurred expenditure on “specified maritime services”, a certain proportion of such expenditure is required to be spent on Hong Kong service providers, thereby promoting the development of the local maritime services ecosystem.

In response to the evolving international tax landscape under the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting 2.0 framework formulated by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation & Development, the Government’s amendment ordinance introduces an additional 15% concessionary rate under existing preferential tax regimes for shipping-related activities, to ease compliance costs for eligible multinational enterprises.

The bill also introduces tax deduction arrangements aligned with international tax standards, thereby preserving the competitiveness of Hong Kong’s tax regimes. Commodity traders under the new regime are also offered the abovementioned additional 15% concessionary tax rate option.

The Government highlighted that it is pressing ahead with the “volume to value” transformation of the Hong Kong Port, as set out in the National 15th Five-Year Plan and Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan.

It added that it is developing the city into a global maritime capital in all respects, anchored by the dual-core strategy of “enhancing port competitiveness” and “optimising the high value-added maritime services ecosystem”. It considers a favourable tax regime a core pillar and key source of competitiveness, and essential for sustaining the growth momentum of the city’s high value-added maritime services industry.

The Government said it will actively promote the new tax concession locally and overseas. To help the industry understand the new requirements, the Inland Revenue Department will issue guidance and maintain close communication with stakeholders to provide technical support and address enquiries.

articles.title: FM calls on UK to uphold principle of free trade
articles.excerpt: China hopes that Britain will uphold the principle of free trade and adopt an open approach, providing Chinese enterprises with…
articles.fullText:
China hopes that Britain will uphold the principle of free trade and adopt an open approach, providing Chinese enterprises with stable policy expectations and a favourable business environment for cooperation in Britain, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Tuesday.

Wang made the remarks during a phone conversation with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband.

China stands ready to work with Britain to promote the mature, steady and sustainable development of bilateral relations, Wang added.

The foreign minister also said he hopes that London will earnestly abide by the one-China principle and uphold the political foundation of bilateral relations. (Reporting by Xinhua)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Shanghai Party chief Chen Jining under investigation
articles.excerpt: Shanghai's Communist Party chief Chen Jining, who's also a Politburo member, is under disciplinary and supervisory investigation, an official statement…
articles.fullText:
Shanghai's Communist Party chief Chen Jining, who's also a Politburo member, is under disciplinary and supervisory investigation, an official statement said on Tuesday.

Chen is being investigated by the Communist Party of China Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Commission of Supervision for suspected severe violations of discipline and laws, the statement said.

Chen, 62, was previously president of Tsinghua University.

He became environmental protection minister in 2015 and then served as mayor of Beijing.

He joined the Politburo in 2022 and was named Party boss of Shanghai. (Xinhua and agencies)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Huawei passes 100m mark in HarmonyOS takeup
articles.excerpt: Huawei on Tuesday announced that the number of smartphones, tablets and computers running its self-developed HarmonyOS operating system has exceeded…
articles.fullText:
Huawei on Tuesday announced that the number of smartphones, tablets and computers running its self-developed HarmonyOS operating system has exceeded 100 million, marking a major milestone in the company's efforts to build an independent software ecosystem.

The figure covers devices running HarmonyOS 5, 6 and 7.

The HarmonyOS operating system now offers more than 460,000 applications and services, with over 12 million registered developers, it said.

Huawei introduced a new HarmonyOS architecture in October 2024, with the launch of HarmonyOS 5, followed by subsequent updates, versions 6 and 7.

The architecture is independent of Google's Android and Apple's iOS, featuring its own operating kernel, programming language and AI framework, all developed without using the Linux kernel or Android open-source code.

Operating systems are the foundation of the digital ecosystem, while the number of devices running them is a key factor determining whether an ecosystem can achieve sufficient scale to take root and sustain itself.

It took about 25 months for the self-developed HarmonyOS to grow from commercial launch to surpassing the 100-million-devices milestone.

Huawei said HarmonyOS applications now cover a wide range of areas, including local services, e-commerce retail, office work, travel and video games.

New applications combining innovative technology with real-world use cases have emerged, from high-definition livestreaming with telephoto macro photography to accessibility tools for people with language barriers.

More than 14,000 contributors are developing industry-specific innovations on the open-source OpenHarmony operating system, producing over 120 customised versions for sectors such as power, water management and manufacturing.

Xia Yubin, director of the OpenHarmony technology club at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, said operating systems have long been dominated by a few foreign companies, and HarmonyOS' surpassing of the 100-million mark means China's foundational software has blazed a path for independent development that can be replicated.

More devices and more diverse scenarios lead to a more mature ecosystem, which in turn encourages more companies to invest in underlying technological innovation.

Huawei has continued to prioritise research and development.

In the first half of 2026, its R&D spending reached a same-period record high of 121.38 billion yuan, up 25.2 percent year on year, according to its semi-annual report, with R&D accounting for 25.94 percent of total revenue. (Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Hong Kong SAR's first astronaut set to return home
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong SAR’s first astronaut, Lai Ka-ying, will return to Earth after completing an in-orbit crew rotation, the China…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong SAR’s first astronaut, Lai Ka-ying, will return to Earth after completing an in-orbit crew rotation, the China Manned Space Agency on Tuesday said, as it announced that the Shenzhou-24 would launch on Wednesday morning to the Tiangong Space Station.

The mission will carry the station’s first foreign astronaut, Pakistani payload specialist Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who will fly alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi.

Ali will conduct a short mission and return with Lai and Zhang Zhiyuan, another Shenzhou-23 astronaut who will command the return flight.

Zhang Jingbo, who is a spokesman for the agency, said Lai had completed a range of tasks as payload specialist.

"She did a great job with space science research, tech tests, and science outreach," he said.

"Working closely with her crewmates and ground teams, she ran experiments like studying the molecular mechanisms behind multigeneration genetic stability and environmental adaptability of space-grown rice."

He added that Lai also operated a robotic arm inside the cabin during an extravehicular activity, supporting her two teammates and helping them smoothly complete tasks including solar-wing repair and the installation of space debris protection devices.

Zhang noted that Lai also made a virtual return to her alma mater in September for a live educational lecture that captivated students in Hong Kong and Macao.

"She and her crewmates were the space teachers that made microgravity experiments live for young people and explaining how astronauts do research on the station, giving Hong Kong and Macao folks a direct look at the nation's space achievements and deepening their love for the country. It got a great response," he said.

Zhang said Lai approached every task with vigour and a down-to-earth scientific attitude, and that her experience had given young people — especially Hong Kong and Macao youth — a sense of the strength of the nation’s science and technological capabilities.

He expressed hope that her experience would encourage young people to boldly pursue the nation’s space dreams.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: China to launch Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship on Weds
articles.excerpt: The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship will launch at 8.18am on Wednesday morning from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre, the China Manned…
articles.fullText:
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship will launch at 8.18am on Wednesday morning from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced on Tuesday.

A Long March-2F carrier rocket, which will be used for the launch, will soon be filled with propellant, said Zhang Jingbo, the CMSA spokesperson, at a press conference.

Zhang also said 90 scientific experiments and technology tests were being planned for the Shenzhou-24 mission.

These will cover space life sciences, space material science, microgravity fluid physics and combustion science, fundamental physics, space medicine, and new space technologies.

In a first for the country's space programme, the Shenzhou-24 crew will include Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station, as well as Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi.

As a payload specialist, Ali will join in the crew's routine work and focus on joint China-Pakistan space science experiments, primarily installing experiment samples and units and carrying out in-orbit experiments.

The Shenzhou-24 is the eighth crewed mission during the development stage of China's space station, and the 41st flight mission overall of China's manned space programme. (Xinhua)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: USA to co-host 2031 Women's World Cup, UK to host 2035
articles.excerpt: A US-led joint bid was confirmed by Fifa on Monday as the host of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while…
articles.fullText:
A US-led joint bid was confirmed by Fifa on Monday as the host of the 2031 Women's World Cup, while the 2035 tournament will be hosted in the United Kingdom.

The winning bids were voted by acclamation after Fifa president Gianni Infantino confirmed the United States in partnership with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica was the "sole candidacy" to host in 2031, when the tournament will feature 48 teams for the first time.

The joint English, Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh bid was also the only candidacy for 2035.

Infantino had already revealed last year that the respective bids for 2031 and 2035 were unchallenged and therefore set to be awarded the tournaments, with both being officially rubber-stamped at Monday's meeting of Fifa's member associations.

"As of 2031 there will be 48 teams and four hosts," said Infantino. "This is an incredible growth in just a few years."

The next Women's World Cup will take place next year in Brazil, running from June 24 to July 25. It will feature 32 teams, with the final at the Maracana Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

Spain go into that tournament as the holders after winning the last Women's World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand in 2023, when they defeated current European champions England in the final.

The US co-hosted this year's men's World Cup, with the majority of matches being played on American soil, including the final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey which was won by Spain. That was the first men's edition featuring 48 teams.

The USA has hosted the Women's World Cup twice before, in 1999 and 2003, and is also the most successful nation in the tournament's history, having lifted the trophy four times.

No senior men's or women's World Cup has been played in the UK since England hosted and won the men's edition in 1966. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Brentford sink Everton to climb in Premier League
articles.excerpt: Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday…
articles.fullText:
Keane Lewis-Potter struck twice as Brentford battered 10-man Everton 4-0 to climb into the Premier League's top six on Monday.

Lewis-Potter's luck was in as twice he saw deflected efforts leave Jordan Pickford stranded before a wild challenge by captain James Tarkowski left Everton a man down for over half the match.

Vitaly Janelt's stunning strike from long range and Fabio Carvalho rounded off a comfortable victory for the Bees, who will fancy their chances when they travel to struggling Manchester United on Saturday.

David Moyes's record 593rd game as Everton boss was not one the Scot will want to remember as his side were swatted aside in west London despite having the chance to go fifth in the table.

A defensive mix-up allowed Jaidon Anthony too much time to pick out Lewis-Potter for the opening goal and his shot deflected off Jarrad Branthwaite to wrong-foot Pickford.

Two minutes later, Everton failed to deal with a free-kick into the box and Lewis-Potter was given two opportunities to double his tally.

The winger's first effort was blocked by Tarkowski before Thierno Barry this time deflected into his own net as the Frenchman threw himself towards the ball.

Worse was to come for the visitors when their skipper was shown red after a VAR review for catching Yehor Yarmoliuk on the shin.

Tarkowski will now be banned for Sunday's Merseyside derby at home to Liverpool.

Moyes turned to Jack Grealish off the bench at half-time in his first appearance since being dropped for breaching club discipline a month ago.

Grealish could do little to inspire the 10 men as Janelt's strike lit up an otherwise uneventful second half.

The German midfielder blasted into the top corner from well outside the box 23 minutes from time.

Carvalho rounded off the scoring from point-blank range when a corner fell to the former Liverpool winger in the 90th minute.

Brentford will head to Old Trafford for Mauricio Pochettino's first home match in charge of United full of confidence and eager to inflict more woe on the Red Devils.

United sit second bottom of the table after a nine-game winless league run, plunging the English giants into danger of being relegated for the first time in 52 years. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Bougainville independence from PNG could change geopolitical landscape: experts
articles.excerpt: Papua New Guinea faces a crucial vote in parliament that would create another sovereign state in the Pacific.
articles.fullText:
Updated on Nov. 25, 2026 at 10:30 a.m. ET
PORT MORESBY, Papua New Guinea – As Papua New Guinea’s Parliament prepares to deliberate on granting independence to the autonomous region of Bougainville, experts told Radio Free Asia that the decision could alter the geopolitical landscape, where China and Western powers compete for diplomatic influence.
Bougainville gained autonomous status in 2005, giving it its own constitution, elected president and parliament, as well as broad powers over local governance, natural resources and public services.
In a landmark referendum held in 2019, voters in the autonomous region overwhelmingly backed independence from Papua New Guinea, or PNG. The vote was part of a peace agreement that ended a decade-long separatist conflict, but its outcome was nonbinding and requires a final decision by PNG’s Parliament.
PNG’s Parliament is expected to resume deliberations during its November budget session on whether to ratify the referendum result, a decision that could pave the way for Bougainville to become one of the world’s newest sovereign states, but Wally Hiambhon, a journalist-turned-media consultant in PNG, told RFA that the emergence of more small Pacific states could create new vulnerabilities amid growing competition between major powers.
A map showing the location of Bougainville within Papua New Guinea.
(RFA) “A fragmented Pacific with too many small states presents the potential for instability and conflict in an environment where there exists super-power rivalry and influence,” said Hiambhon. “We should tread with caution and responsibility on this one.”
Port Moresby’s recent warming relationship with Beijing is concerning, James Tanis, a former Bougainville president who participated in the peace negotiations, told RFA.
He took particular issue with the shutdown of Taiwan’s representative office in Port Moresby in November, and said that under its current status, Bougainville has no control over its own foreign relations.
“Only independence will help Bougainville to choose its own international friends,” he said.
An independent Bougainville would be able to pursue its own diplomatic relationships, although international recognition and admission to the United Nations would present additional challenges.
The people have spoken
For Margaret Edoni, a self-employed mother in PNG, the question of whether Bougainville should become an independent country has a straightforward answer: the people have already made their choice.
“Yes, I think PNG should give independence to Bougainville,” she told RFA. “In the 2019 referendum, 97.7% of Bougainvilleans voted for independence. And as a democratic state, PNG must respect the Bougainville people’s choice.”
Others in PNG have also voiced support for independence, arguing that the overwhelming vote leaves the national government with little justification for rejecting it. Some have criticized Port Moresby’s handling of the process, accusing it of poor planning and indecisiveness.
Bougainville Referendum Commission staff count votes prior to the referendum announcement in Bougainville on Dec. 11, 2019. Voters backing Bougainville's independence from Papua New Guinea have won a landslide referendum victory, according to results released on Dec. 11.
(Llane Munau/AFP) The current debate began in October after the government formally presented the referendum result and two supporting documents to Parliament in August. Prime Minister James Marape said lawmakers would return to the matter in November before a vote.
Under a parliamentary procedure adopted in June, ratification requires an absolute three-quarters majority, or 89 votes in the 118-member Parliament.
A troubled history
Bougainville, an island region east of mainland PNG and geographically close to the Solomon Islands, has a long history of separatist aspirations.
The dispute intensified in the late 1980s over the Panguna copper and gold mine, once among the world’s largest, as grievances over environmental destruction and the distribution of mining revenues fueled an armed rebellion.
The conflict between separatists and PNG security forces, compounded by internal fighting, killed thousands of people and devastated infrastructure before a peace process brought the fighting to an end.
The 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement provided for regional autonomy, weapons disposal and an eventual referendum on independence.
A voter from Selau is seen at Buka market, Bougainville, Papua New Guinea, Nov. 30, 2019.
(Bougainville Referendum Commission/Jeremy Miller/Handout via Reuters) Nearly 25 years later, the region is approaching a decisive stage in implementing that agreement.
Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama said on Nov. 13 that his government had fulfilled its obligations under the peace process and expected PNG to demonstrate the same commitment.
Bougainville’s leadership has proposed a transition to self-government by September 2027, followed by full independence in 2030.
Both sides have agreed that the start date of self-government would be Sept. 1, 2027 if the parliament approves, but that approval remains uncertain.
Marape has emphasized that Parliament must consider both Bougainville’s aspirations and the implications for PNG’s national unity. His government has proposed a negotiated transition of up to 15 years if lawmakers endorse independence, potentially subject to economic and security conditions.
What if Parliament says no?
Tanis warned that rejecting independence could jeopardize decades of efforts to establish lasting peace.
“It is better to simply endorse and complete the process rather than not endorse and throw the process into the unknown,” he told RFA.
Tanis argued that the responsibility for securing the necessary parliamentary majority rested with Marape’s ruling Pangu Party and its coalition partners.
He also questioned what would follow a rejection, saying the agreements governing the peace process did not establish a clear pathway for implementing a negative vote.
Bougainville's President Ishmael Toroama speaks during the Papua New Guinea Investment Week conference in Sydney on Dec. 11, 2024.
(David Gray/AFP) Under the parliamentary procedure, a failed ratification vote would leave Bougainville’s existing autonomy arrangements in place, although the two governments could continue consultations.
Marape has suggested that a negative vote need not permanently settle the issue, leaving open the possibility of further negotiations.
But for supporters of independence, another delay could deepen frustration after years of waiting.
Mary Soondrawu, chairperson of PNG Trust Inc., an educational and advocacy organization, said the national government should respect the referendum outcome.
“The people have spoken and let their voice be heard,” she told RFA.
Can Bougainville survive alone?
Even if Parliament endorses independence, the region faces substantial economic challenges.
Bougainville relies heavily on financial transfers from PNG’s national government, raising questions about its ability to fund public services and maintain essential infrastructure as a sovereign country.
According to the Autonomous Bougainville Government, Bougainville’s internal annual revenue is 46.74 million kina (US$10.2 million), or just 5.5% of its budget for 2026 .
Delegations led by Chinese President Xi Jinping and Papua New Guinea’s Prime Minister James Marape attend a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China Nov. 17, 2026.
(Maxim Shemetov/Reuters) Marape has proposed that Bougainville demonstrate sufficient internal revenue to support at least 70% of its budget as part of a negotiated transition.
Mining could provide a potential source of revenue, although the legacy of Panguna remains contentious.
On Nov. 16, global mining group Rio Tinto announced a commitment of US$250 million over several years to a fund addressing environmental and human rights impacts associated with the former mine.
PNG Trust Inc.’s Soondrawu said independence should allow Bougainville to pursue accountability for environmental damage and make its own economic decisions.
Hiambhon warned that the economic realities of independence could prove more difficult than its supporters anticipate.
“My view is that whilst the majority of Bougainvilleans want independence, the reality of self-rule might be tougher than they reckon, particularly economic wellbeing,” he told RFA.
Edited by Taejun Kang and Eugene Whong.
Update adds that the start date of self-government would be Sept. 1, 2027 if parliament approves.

articles.title: Google AI smartwatch could flag high blood pressure
articles.excerpt: Google's AI used smartwatch sensors to spot hypertension without a blood pressure cuff, but the Nature study found it missed…
articles.fullText:
When was the last time you checked your blood pressure? If you're like a lot of people, it probably happened during your last doctor's appointment. And if you feel perfectly healthy , you may not give it another thought. That's what makes high blood pressure so concerning. You can have it for years without noticing anything wrong.
Now, Google researchers are exploring a way to uncover that hidden danger using something many of us already wear on our wrists. In a new study recently published in Nature, researchers demonstrated an artificial intelligence system that can identify signs of hypertension using standard smartwatch sensors. It works in the background without requiring calibration with a traditional blood pressure cuff.
The technology uses sensors that already exist in consumer smartwatches. That could make early detection much more accessible. However, the research also reveals a limitation that anyone relying on a smartwatch for health information should understand.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
SMARTWATCH AFIB ALERT SENDS DAD TO ER BEFORE HEART SURGERY
Your smartwatch already knows quite a bit about your body. It can track your heart rate throughout the day. Depending on the model, it may also detect irregular heart rhythms.
Google's new AI takes the information collected by those sensors and looks for signs of something harder to detect: ongoing high blood pressure. According to Google Research , the system analyzes two types of sensor data.
The first sensor uses light to detect changes in blood volume beneath your skin. It's the same basic technology many watches use to monitor your pulse. The second sensor measures movement. Researchers found that it can also capture incredibly small vibrations caused by your heart pumping blood. You wouldn't notice those vibrations. However, the AI can analyze them alongside your pulse patterns to look for signs associated with hypertension.
The system collects information over multiple days. It then combines those patterns with your height to estimate the likelihood of sustained high blood pressure. Unlike a traditional monitor, the smartwatch doesn't produce a reading such as 120 over 80. Instead, it looks for signs that your blood pressure may be consistently elevated. What's interesting is that you wouldn't have to do anything differently. You could go about your day while your smartwatch quietly looks for potential warning signs.
Google worked with researchers from Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and Harvard Medical School to develop and test the system. First, researchers trained the underlying AI using nearly 500,000 hours of smartwatch sensor data collected from 2,109 consenting participants. They then evaluated the hypertension detection system in a clinical study involving 196 participants across five U.S. locations. None of those participants had known cardiovascular disease or were taking blood pressure medication.
During the study, participants wore a consumer smartwatch for seven days. Researchers compared the AI's findings with results from 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring. That medical test uses a cuff to measure blood pressure repeatedly throughout the day and night. Doctors use it to help confirm hypertension.
During initial screening, the results showed:
For comparison, initial blood pressure screenings performed in medical offices identified 55.3% of participants with hypertension in the study. That's an encouraging result. However, the difference between the smartwatch and office screening was not statistically significant, according to a Nature Portfolio summary of the findings. There's another number worth paying attention to.
That's a number worth paying attention to. After all, we're talking about a condition that can lead to a heart attack or stroke , often without any warning signs.
Researchers also looked at a smaller group of 48 people who had elevated blood pressure readings during their initial doctor's visit. In that group, the AI correctly identified 78.4% of those with ongoing hypertension. It also correctly ruled out the condition in 90.9% of those who didn't have it. Those results are encouraging, but there's still work to do. Google needs to test the technology on more people before we can know how reliably it can detect high blood pressure.
MICROSOFT AI BEATS DOCTORS IN SIMULATED DIAGNOSIS TEST
Here's where things get interesting for people who already own a Google smartwatch. Google introduced its Health Guardian features in September 2026. Among them is a blood pressure trends feature available through the Google Health app.
According to Google's September announcement, blood pressure trends are available at no additional subscription cost on eligible Pixel Watch 3, Pixel Watch 4 and Pixel Watch 5 devices . Availability depends on your region.
The feature analyzes pulse and movement patterns over time. Then, it provides a monthly assessment of whether your blood pressure trend appears high. Google says these existing Health Guardian capabilities are informed by clinical research, including work connected to its newly published findings. However, there's an important difference between the experimental system described in Nature and the feature available on your watch today.
The existing Pixel Watch feature is intended for general wellness. Google specifically says it cannot diagnose hypertension or serve as a medical screening tool. It also cannot tell you your actual systolic or diastolic blood pressure numbers. According to Google's support documentation, the feature provides a monthly trend assessment such as "High" or "Not high."
And a "Not high" result doesn't guarantee your blood pressure is normal. Google also warns users against relying on these estimates to change medications or treatment plans. Meanwhile, the newly published research remains exploratory. Google has not announced that the experimental hypertension screening system will become a commercial diagnostic feature.
Google has some competition in this area. Apple has already introduced FDA-cleared hypertension notifications for compatible Apple Watch models. As we previously reported in Apple Watch gets FDA-approved hypertension alerts , the feature looks for patterns associated with chronic high blood pressure. It uses information gathered by the watch's optical heart sensor over 30-day periods.
The feature supports Apple Watch Series 9 and later models, along with Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models, subject to software and regional availability. If the watch detects concerning patterns, it can notify you. However, Apple also makes clear that the feature cannot diagnose hypertension. And it may miss cases. Apple recommends checking your blood pressure with a traditional cuff and discussing the results with a healthcare professional if you receive an alert.
So, while Apple and Google are approaching this technology differently, the current guidance remains clear. A smartwatch alert can give you useful information, but you still need an accurate blood pressure measurement.
High blood pressure has earned the nickname "silent killer" for a reason. According to the World Health Organization, more than one billion adults worldwide live with hypertension. Many have no idea they have it.
Meanwhile, untreated high blood pressure can damage blood vessels and increase the risk of a heart attack or stroke. Younger adults can be particularly vulnerable to missed diagnoses because they may feel healthy and see little reason to get checked. Now, consider what could happen if a smartwatch noticed concerning patterns before someone developed symptoms.
That person might decide to schedule an appointment and have their blood pressure checked. If doctors confirm hypertension, earlier treatment could help reduce the risk of complications. Of course, researchers still need to determine whether smartwatch-based screening actually improves diagnosis rates and long-term health outcomes.
COULD A PAINT-ON ELECTRONIC TATTOO SPOT HEART ATTACKS?
If your smartwatch warns you about possible high blood pressure, don't ignore it. But don't assume the watch has diagnosed you, either. The next step is to check your blood pressure using a validated upper-arm cuff.
The American Heart Association recommends automatic upper-arm monitors for home measurements because they provide more reliable readings than typical wrist or finger monitors. If you're using Google's blood pressure trends feature and receive a "High" result, Google recommends checking your blood pressure twice a day for seven days and sharing those readings with your doctor.
Make sure you follow your monitor's instructions and use the correct cuff size. Also, keep an eye on how you're feeling. If you experience emergency warning signs such as chest pain or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention rather than waiting for another smartwatch assessment.
And remember, even if your watch never sends an alert, you should continue getting your blood pressure checked. For another way to track your readings, see our article on how to monitor blood pressure with your Apple Watch using a compatible blood pressure monitor.
One of my biggest questions about this technology comes down to how much confidence people will place in the results. Let's say your smartwatch tells you everything looks normal. Would you still bother checking your blood pressure? That's where the research raises an important concern.
In Google's initial screening study, the AI missed a meaningful number of people who actually had hypertension. And while the results compared favorably with initial office screening, the study was relatively small. Researchers will need more evidence before the technology can become a dependable part of routine medical screening.
Google's findings suggest that everyday wearables could eventually help identify people who might otherwise go undiagnosed. For now, though, a reliable blood pressure cuff and a conversation with your doctor remain essential.
I like where Google is going with this. Most of us probably don't think about our blood pressure until we're sitting in a doctor's office with a cuff around our arm. So the idea that a smartwatch could spot a potential problem before we even know something's wrong is pretty exciting. But there's one number in this study that concerns me. The AI missed roughly one in three people who actually had high blood pressure. That's a lot, especially when you consider the serious health risks involved. I think this technology has tremendous potential, and I'm looking forward to seeing how Google improves it. But for now, I wouldn't rely on my smartwatch to tell me whether my blood pressure is normal. I'd still want to check it with a traditional cuff.
Would you trust your smartwatch to warn you about high blood pressure? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.

articles.title: FBI warns AI hackers can breach systems in under 3 hours
articles.excerpt: The FBI warns the ARTEX AI hacking tool can give criminals privileged access in under three hours, targeting Microsoft 365…
articles.fullText:
Your bank could spend millions protecting its computer systems. Your employer might have an entire cybersecurity team watching for suspicious activity . Yet hackers now have an AI-powered tool that can help them break into some organizations in less than three hours.
The FBI is warning that criminals are using the ARTEX AI hacking tool to automate cyberattacks against businesses around the world. Some attacks have moved from initial targeting to powerful administrator-level access in under three hours. That leaves companies very little time to recognize an attack and stop it.
If hackers reach a business that stores your personal information, you could end up dealing with the consequences. Here's how ARTEX works, why the FBI is concerned and what you can do to protect yourself.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
AI-POWERED CYBERATTACKS FUEL 'BLACK OCTOBER' FEARS
ARTEX started as a legitimate penetration testing framework. Cybersecurity professionals use these tools to find weaknesses in computer systems before criminals discover them. However, hackers have found ways to turn ARTEX against organizations without permission. The framework uses artificial intelligence to handle tasks that previously required significant hacking expertise. It can search for security weaknesses and attempt to exploit them. Once inside a system, ARTEX can work toward gaining higher levels of access and extracting sensitive information. What makes ARTEX particularly concerning is its ability to operate with limited human involvement. Attackers can give the software instructions, then let AI agents carry out much of the work automatically.
ARTEX also connects to external AI models , including OpenAI's GPT and Anthropic's Claude. It supports DeepSeek and several other models. These integrations allow the framework to process instructions and automate complicated hacking operations. Their availability does not mean the AI companies are directing the attacks. According to the FBI, the technology allows criminals with relatively little technical knowledge to launch sophisticated attacks against multiple organizations simultaneously.
In a November 13, 2026, security advisory, the FBI warned that criminals have used ARTEX in cyberattacks since at least August 2026. The agency identified campaigns targeting financial institutions and healthcare organizations. Government agencies and technology companies have also appeared among the targets. The speed of these attacks is especially troubling. According to the FBI, some intrusions progressed from initial targeting to privileged access in less than three hours. That means hackers obtained powerful permissions that could allow them to make changes inside compromised systems.
ARTEX can also identify weaknesses in systems that companies sometimes overlook. These include employee portals and older business applications. Criminals may exploit vulnerable third-party connections to reach organizations with stronger security. Although automated attacks can trigger security alerts, their speed creates another challenge. A company's security team might detect suspicious activity only after criminals have already gained access.
One of the clearest examples involves Microsoft 365, the service millions of employees rely on for work email and company files. In October 2026, hackers exploited compromised application credentials associated with ConnectWise Cloud Backup. The service, formerly known as SkyKick Cloud Backup, helps businesses back up Microsoft 365 information. Here's why that attack is so concerning. The compromised applications already had permission to access customer environments. Hackers took advantage of those existing permissions to authenticate without needing an employee to sign in. In an October 21 investigation, Microsoft attributed the campaign to a China-state-aligned hacking group it tracks as Storm-0940.
The group used ARTEX to speed up its operations and attempt access to more than 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 customer environments. Cybersecurity company Huntress reported unauthorized sign-ins across at least 162 customer environments during its initial investigation. However, the number of environments targeted does not represent the number where criminals stole information. Microsoft specifically warned that successful authentication does not automatically mean customer data was accessed or taken. The attack also did not result from a vulnerability in Microsoft's own systems or services. Hackers exploited permissions associated with a trusted third-party application. For businesses, that's a serious concern. Employees could have strong passwords and multifactor authentication enabled, yet criminals might still gain access through a compromised application the company already trusts.
The Microsoft 365 incident represents only part of the FBI's warning. In South Korea, hackers used ARTEX in attacks against financial institutions. Those attacks exposed personal information belonging to approximately 67,000 people, according to the FBI.
In a separate investigation, South Korean authorities arrested seven suspects connected to attacks against more than 90 organizations. Police said the group stole approximately 8.2 million data records, with ARTEX reportedly used in many of the attacks. Researchers have also identified a separate international cyberespionage campaign.
Cybersecurity company CrowdStrike reported that a China-linked hacking group known as Vapor Panda used ARTEX in attacks targeting more than 200 organizations across 14 countries. The campaign compromised at least nine organizations. The AI agents helped criminals identify vulnerabilities and obtain credentials. When one attack method failed, the software could attempt another approach. These incidents show how quickly AI-assisted hacking has expanded from individual targets to coordinated attacks against organizations around the world.
You probably have never heard of ARTEX before now. But the businesses you depend on could become targets. Think about the information your employer keeps on file. It may include your Social Security number and banking details for direct deposit. Your healthcare provider holds sensitive medical information, while financial institutions maintain records connected to your identity. If criminals steal information from those organizations, they could use it to attempt identity theft or target you with convincing scams. A hacker who obtains your email address and details about your employer could create a phishing message that looks legitimate. A message mentioning a company you actually do business with may be harder to recognize as fraudulent.
There's another concern. Your personal information could be exposed through a company you barely remember giving it to. The FBI has not warned that ARTEX automatically compromises personal phones or home computers. Its advisory focuses on attacks against organizations and the systems they operate. Still, you don't have to be the direct target of a cyberattack to feel its effects.
NEW AI MALWARE RANKS VICTIMS BY HOW MUCH THEY'RE WORTH
The original ARTEX developer released the framework publicly in July 2026. After reports emerged that criminals were abusing it, the developer removed the original GitHub repository on October 8. However, the software remains available through archived copies and modified versions. The FBI also identified a commercial version called ARTEX PRO. As of early November, researchers had identified more than 1,600 publicly exposed ARTEX consoles. That figure refers to accessible framework interfaces, rather than 1,600 confirmed criminal operations. Removing the original project did little to eliminate copies already circulating online.
While companies are responsible for securing their systems, you can still take steps to protect your personal information and limit the damage if a business you trust gets hacked.
If criminals steal login credentials from one organization, they may test those credentials against other accounts. Reusing passwords makes that easier. Use a strong, unique password for every important account. A reputable password manager can generate secure passwords and store them for you. Start with your primary email account because criminals who gain access to it may be able to reset passwords for other services.
Multifactor authentication adds another security check when someone tries to sign in to your account. Enable it for your email and financial services whenever available. Choose a passkey or authenticator app when supported. Passkeys can provide stronger protection against phishing than traditional passwords. Keep in mind that these protections cannot prevent every attack. The ConnectWise incident involved compromised application credentials rather than someone entering an employee's password.
You may have granted third-party applications permission to access your Google or Microsoft account without thinking much about it. Review those connections periodically. Remove permissions for unfamiliar services or applications you no longer need. For personal Microsoft accounts, visit account.microsoft.com. For Google accounts, review your connected apps through myaccount.google.com. Look for unfamiliar sign-ins while you're there. If something seems suspicious, secure the account and revoke any sessions you don't recognize. For work accounts, contact your IT department before changing business application permissions.
Cybercriminals often use major security incidents to create convincing phishing messages. You might receive an email claiming your bank was hacked and asking you to verify your password. Another message could direct you to a fake account recovery page. Avoid clicking unexpected links or opening unfamiliar attachments. Instead, visit the company's official website or open its app directly to check for alerts. Never share verification codes with someone who contacts you unexpectedly, even if the person claims to work for your bank.
Install security updates on your computer and phone. These updates frequently address vulnerabilities criminals could exploit. Strong antivirus software with real-time protection can also help identify malicious downloads and suspicious programs. Some security tools offer additional protection against phishing websites. However, antivirus software on your personal computer cannot prevent criminals from compromising a company's cloud systems. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android & iOS devices at Cyberguy.com.
Check your financial accounts regularly and enable transaction alerts. These notifications can help you spot unauthorized activity quickly. Review your credit reports for unfamiliar accounts or credit inquiries. You can request free reports through AnnualCreditReport.com. If your Social Security number has been exposed, consider freezing your credit with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. A credit freeze is free and can make it harder for criminals to open new credit accounts using your identity. A freeze will not prevent fraud involving accounts that are already open, so continue monitoring those accounts.
VISA, MASTERCARD AND JPMORGAN CUSTOMER DATA LEAKED
If a company notifies you about a breach, find out exactly what information was compromised. Then take action based on the type of data involved.
You can also report suspected internet crime to the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center at ic3.gov/.
A backup service is supposed to help protect a company's information. In the ConnectWise attack, hackers abused that trusted connection to gain access to customer systems. That's especially concerning because employees could have followed every security recommendation and still been exposed through a service their company depended on. The speed of these AI-powered attacks also worries me. Three hours gives security teams very little time to stop criminals who know exactly where they're going. I think companies need to take a much harder look at the outside applications they trust and how quickly they can detect unauthorized access. For you, the best approach is to secure your own accounts and pay attention when a company reports a breach. You shouldn't have to become a cybersecurity expert to feel confident that businesses are protecting your information.
If AI-powered hackers can gain privileged access to company systems in less than three hours, do you still trust businesses to protect your personal information, or should companies face tougher consequences when that information gets exposed? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com.
