articles.title: China says global green transition is 'irreversible'
articles.excerpt: China on Monday said the failure of a United Nations climate conference to produce a deal following a row over…
articles.fullText:
China on Monday said the failure of a United Nations climate conference to produce a deal following a row over fossil fuels was disappointing but that the green transition is "irreversible".

"We express our disappointment over this, while maintaining that confidence in the multilateral process should not be lost as a result," Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular news briefing.

"China wishes to emphasise that tackling climate change is a shared endeavour for all humanity. The trend of global transition to green energy low carbon is irreversible.

"China has been committed to safeguarding multilateralism, advancing international cooperation, and promoting green transition.

"China will continue to act responsibly and work with all parties to cope with challenges, overcome difficulties and promote the green and low-carbon transition and sustainable development worldwide."

For the first time since the 2009 meeting in Copenhagen, the COP climate conference in Türkiye could not reach a final agreement from its talks after the European Union and others rejected a final deal that did not include any mention of fossil fuels' role in global warming because of pressure from Saudi Arabia and other oil-producing nations. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Domestically-built cruise ship in Kai Tak maiden call
articles.excerpt: The second China-built large cruise ship, the Adora Flora City, arrived at Kai Tak Cruise Terminal on Monday morning on…
articles.fullText:
The second China-built large cruise ship, the Adora Flora City, arrived at Kai Tak Cruise Terminal on Monday morning on its maiden commercial voyage carrying more than 3,800 passengers.

The ship set sail from the Nansha International Cruise Home Port in Guangzhou for a six-day, five-night journey that will also take it to Hue in Vietnam.

The vessel is 341 metres long and has 2,130 cabins, with capacity for up to 5,232 passengers.

Compared with the first China-built large cruise ship, the Adora Magic City, the new vessel's hull has been lengthened by 17.4 metres, with more than 3,000 square metres of additional public space.

It also features a larger atrium, an upgraded water park and more passenger-friendly services.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Hong Kong to help build world-class bay area: CE
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong would actively leverage its advantages of being connected to the mainland and the world under "One Country, Two…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong would actively leverage its advantages of being connected to the mainland and the world under "One Country, Two Systems" to contribute to the national effort to promote bay area economies and build a world-class bay area with other Greater Bay Area cities, Chief Executive John Lee said on Monday.

In a video address to the 16th Hong Kong International Financial Forum and the seventh Pilot "9+2" Navigation GBA Forum, Lee noted that President Xi Jinping proposed establishing a global association for bay areas economic cooperation to deepen exchanges among bay areas around the world and explore new paths for Asia-Pacific cooperation during a keynote speech at the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen last week.

He said this year marks China's year as Apec host, and that the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting and CEO Summit in Shenzhen last week, together with the Apec Finance Ministers' Meeting held in Hong Kong for the first time in October, showed the Greater Bay Area cities' collective role in serving the country's efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community.

Lee said the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, bringing together the two special administrative regions and nine Guangdong cities, had a combined economic output of over US$2.1 trillion, showing strong economic resilience and enormous development potential.

He said the government would deepen coordination with bay area cities on technology and innovation cooperation, "hard connectivity" of infrastructure, "soft connectivity" of rules and mechanisms, and "heart connectivity" among residents, as well as on major cooperation platforms, to promote the efficient flow of people, goods, capital and information.

"Hong Kong will actively leverage its advantages under 'One Country, Two Systems' of connecting the mainland with the world, contribute to our country's development of the bay area economy, and work together with fellow Greater Bay Area cities to build a world-class bay area," he said.

The chief executive said the Northern Metropolis university town would bring together education, technology, industry, talent and urban development, and that the Northern Metropolis would be developed into a "highland" for international talent and an important platform for deeper participation in Greater Bay Area development.

The government, he added, would encourage more top mainland universities and research institutions to set up there.

"We will drive more first-class mainland universities and research institutions to settle in the Northern Metropolis, pool top academic and research capabilities with local colleges and universities to complement each other’s strengths, and serve the country’s high-level scientific and technological self-reliance and self-strengthening," he said.

He also said Hong Kong's common law system, free flow of capital and internationalised business environment allow it to provide bay area enterprises with all-round professional services through a task force on mainland enterprises going global, helping them expand into new markets.

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Marquez makes history with eighth MotoGP world title
articles.excerpt: Spaniard Marc Marquez was crowned MotoGP world champion for a record-equalling eighth time on Sunday, with an eighth-place finish at…
articles.fullText:
Spaniard Marc Marquez was crowned MotoGP world champion for a record-equalling eighth time on Sunday, with an eighth-place finish at the Portuguese Grand Prix enough to establish an unassailable lead in the standings to cap a remarkable comeback this season.

Italian Marco Bezzecchi rode to victory in southern Portugal but the result was enough to seal a second consecutive world title for the Ducati rider.

On crossing the line, the 33-year-old Marquez leapt from his bike and was hoisted up by his team before he ran towards his fans screaming with his arms aloft.

"Last year was for me, this one is for you," he told his fans through a microphone before again throwing back his head and screaming out his emotions.

His eighth success in the premier class of motorcycling pulled Marquez level with Italian great Giacomo Agostini who won his titles between 1966 and 1975.

The latest triumph is even more remarkable given the Spaniard's injury and crash-blighted campaign where he had to wait until the eighth race in Hungary on June 7 before claiming his first win.

Marquez suffered a flat tyre in the season-opener in Thailand in March, fell at the Spanish GP in Jerez and again at the French GP where he picked up a foot fracture which ruled him out of the following race, the Catalan GP.

Making his comeback at the Italian GP in Mugello he trailed Bezzecchi by a massive 102 points early June just weeks after undergoing foot surgery on top of a previous operation on his injured shoulder.

But the Spaniard managed to bounce back once again, defying those who had already written him off.

Once he got rolling he roared into a regular winning run with seven Grand Prix and ten sprint race victories in all this season.

While not as obviously dominant as having won 11 GP in the 2025 season, where an unexpected return to form since his 2024 switch to Ducati gave him a new lease of life, this latest win is as impressive.

Marquez had been the youngest-ever premier class champion in his debut season in 2013 for Honda and then went on to win the title in five of the next six seasons.

He also overtakes his great rival Valentino Rossi, who won seven MotoGP titles, although the swashbuckling Italian has 89 individual race wins in the top category to Marquez's 80.

Having crashed during Saturday's sprint race Marquez rode out Sunday's GP safely, needing only to finish in the top nine to secure his tenth title across all categories combined.

Aprilia's Bezzecchi won Sunday's race to complete the double in Portugal having also won the sprint, with his stablemate Jorge Martin of Spain crossing in second.

With a total of 439 points and seven victories this year, this was enough for Marquez to keep his rivals at bay.

Martin is second with 396 points but only one win and Bezzecchi, who has 394 points and seven first-place finishes, in third ahead of the season-finale in Valencia, Spain next weekend.

"Thank you for this bike," Marquez told his team Ducati during his victory lap. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Skubal to join Mets in record-breaking deal: reports
articles.excerpt: Tarik Skubal, a two-time Cy Young Award winner as Major League Baseball's top pitcher, has agreed to terms on a…
articles.fullText:
Tarik Skubal, a two-time Cy Young Award winner as Major League Baseball's top pitcher, has agreed to terms on a record nine-year deal worth US$450 million with the New York Mets, according to multiple reports on Sunday.

The 30-year-old American left-hander spent his first six seasons with the Detroit Tigers before joining the Los Angeles Dodgers in a trade last August, but he was unable to help the club lift a third consecutive World Series trophy.

The US$50 million average annual value would make the deal a record for pitchers, surpassing the US$43.3 million annual value of contracts for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander.

Skubal's deal also would be the richest contract for any pitcher in MLB history, surpassing the mark of US$325 million set when the Dodgers signed Japan's Yoshinobu Yamamoto to a 12-year deal in 2024.

Skubal became only the 12th pitcher in MLB history to win back-to-back Cy Youngs when he captured the award in the American League in 2024 and 2025.

He completed the AL triple crown in 2024, leading the league in wins with 18 and in earned-run average at 2.39 plus topping MLB in strikeouts with 228.

Skubal, a unanimous Cy Young choice in 2024, also had the AL's lowest earned-run average in 2025 at 2.21 and struck out 241 batters over 195 1/3 innings to repeat.

In 2026, he won an arbitration hearing and was awarded US$32 million for the 2026 season, but the campaign was cut short in May when he had to undergo surgery for loose bodies in his elbow.

He returned in July and after joining the Dodgers, Skubal went 5-2 with a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts over 62 innings, then went 1-1 in the playoffs, where the Dodgers were eliminated by eventual champion Milwaukee.

Skubal, considered the top free agent player available, made the agreement as MLB owners and the MLB Players Association stand deadlocked over how to divide profits with the December 1 deadline for a new deal fast approaching.

If the sides cannot agree on terms for a new collective bargaining agreement, a lockout is expected next month.

Owners demand a salary cap system while the union has been against such a format for decades. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Alcaraz downs Zverev to win ATP Finals for first time
articles.excerpt: Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the…
articles.fullText:
Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals with a 6-2, 7-6 (9/7) victory over world number one Alexander Zverev in the title match in Turin on Sunday.

After becoming the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam at the start of the season with victory in the Australian Open, the 23-year-old has bookended an up-and-down year with a first title at the season-ending showpiece tournament.

Alongside Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic, Alcaraz now forms part of an exclusive list of men to have won all four majors and the ATP Finals.

With his compatriot Rafael Nadal never managing to win the season-ending tournament, Alcaraz became the first Spanish champion since Alex Corretja in 1998.

"It's been an amazing week. I couldn't finish the week in a better way, so I'm really proud," Alcaraz said after capturing his sixth title of the year.

"I've been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything. I'm playing great tennis, so for me, lifting this trophy is something that I've been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me," he added of the hamstring issue he suffered earlier in the tournament.

A wrist injury had caused Alcaraz to miss a good chunk of the middle of the season and following that victory in Melbourne he failed to add to his seven major titles.

But since returning in August, he has enjoyed a blistering end to the year, winning his last 14 matches to capture trophies at the Vienna Open, the Paris Masters for the first time and now the elusive ATP Finals.

He lost in the season-ender's final to Jannik Sinner last year, but with the injured Italian having curtailed his season, Alcaraz found himself again in the Turin title match against a world number one.

Zverev, a two-time ATP Finals champion, broke his Grand Slam duck this season by claiming the French and US Opens, catapulting him above Alcaraz and Sinner to the top of the rankings.

The top two seeds in Italy, Alcaraz and Zverev were a cut above the rest all throughout the tournament, both topping their respective pools with three wins from three.

The first set of Alcaraz's semi-final win over Ben Shelton was the only frame either player had dropped all week.

Indeed Zverev had marched into the final without dropping a service game, but he was mightily tested straight out of the traps by Alcaraz as the world number three forced three break points in the very first game before the German dug in to hold.

Alcaraz was not so wasteful two games later, however, as he broke Zverev to love when the 29-year-old overcooked a mid-court forehand.

Zverev forced break-back points in the next game but, after failing to convert, he was left to rue his luck even further as the Spaniard broke to 30 to grow his lead to 4-1.

Zverev wiped out one break but Alcaraz was nonetheless firmly in the ascendancy and pounced for a third time on the Hamburg native's serve in an entertaining seventh game which saw Zverev dejectedly chuck his racquet to the floor after netting a smash from an Alcaraz tweener lob.

A netted backhand by Zverev – his 19th unforced error of the match – on Alcaraz's first set point then brought an end to a surprisingly sloppy opening frame.

Both players exchanged breaks in the second set as it went the distance.

The Murcian took a 3-0 lead in the tie-break before Zverev won the next six points to bring up three set points.

But the Spaniard struck back to wipe them out before getting a mini-break to bring up championship point on his own serve.

The first went begging when he whipped a forehand into the tramlines but he brought up a second with a drop-shot and sealed the title with a backhand. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: Man Utd drubbed 4-0 in nightmare Pochettino debut
articles.excerpt: Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager with a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool that left the Red…
articles.fullText:
Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager with a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool that left the Red Devils still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone.

United never recovered from Leny Yoro's controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool's man advantage count.

Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool's third before Victor Munoz completed the rout.

The defeat leaves United second bottom of the table and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories.

"We feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game," said Pochettino, who was furious at the decision to dismiss Yoro.

"I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card."

Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title.

"We could have scored more," said Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola.

"In other games you will remember those chances, but today we've controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box."

Pochettino answered United's call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils' first 10 league games in charge.

The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans.

Pochettino's bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game's decisive moment.

De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal.

The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card.

Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box.

Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar.

Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding.

Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time.

But Bradley Barcola’s blistering speed created Liverpool's third just after the hour mark.

The French international destroyed Lisandro Martinez for pace before picking out Ngumoha to slot home.

Wirtz rounded off one of his best Liverpool displays since a £100 million move from Bayer Leverkusen last year with the assist for Munoz to crash home the fourth goal eight minutes from time.

Liverpool fans rejoiced in their rivals' pain with chants of "you are going down".

United have not been relegated since 1974 but find themselves in a battle for survival despite still enjoying one of the biggest revenues in world football.

The 34 goals they have conceded in all competitions is the worst defensive record of any team in Europe's top five leagues this season. (AFP)

Edited by Cecil Wong

articles.title: FDA clears tiny surgical robot to remove bladder tumors
articles.excerpt: The FDA-authorized Virtuoso Endoscopy System uses needle-sized robotic arms to remove bladder tumors intact, helping pathologists assess detrusor muscle.
articles.fullText:
If a doctor finds a tumor in your bladder, you want to know what you're dealing with. Is it cancer? Has it reached the bladder muscle? The tissue removed during surgery helps answer those questions. Now, a tiny surgical robot could give doctors a clearer view of what's happening inside the bladder.
The FDA has authorized the Virtuoso Endoscopy System, developed by Nashville-based Virtuoso Surgical. It uses two needle-sized robotic arms to remove bladder lesions through the urethra, without cutting through the skin. The technology allows surgeons to remove many tumors in one piece, potentially giving pathologists better tissue samples to examine. This new approach to robotic bladder tumor removal could help doctors make more informed treatment decisions.

WOULD YOU TRUST A TINY DENTAL ROBOT?
The Virtuoso Endoscopy System uses a narrow medical instrument called a rigid endoscope, which enters the bladder through the urethra. At the tip are two miniature robotic arms made from a flexible metal alloy called nitinol. A surgeon controls both arms from a console. One arm lifts and holds the tumor while the other carefully separates it from the tissue underneath. This gives the surgeon two-handed control inside a very small space.
The technique is called en bloc resection, which means removing a tumor in one piece. Surgeons can already perform this procedure using conventional instruments, but it can be technically demanding. Virtuoso designed its system to make that approach easier to perform. The robot also relies entirely on the surgeon's movements. Unlike some autonomous surgical robots being tested in research settings , Virtuoso does not make surgical decisions or operate independently.
Bladder cancer affects thousands of Americans every year. The American Cancer Society estimates that approximately 84,530 people in the United States will receive a bladder cancer diagnosis in 2026. One of the most common procedures for evaluating and removing bladder tumors is called transurethral resection of bladder tumor, or TURBT. During conventional TURBT, surgeons often remove tumors in smaller fragments. While effective for many patients, that approach can disrupt the tissue's original structure. As a result, pathologists may have a harder time determining how deeply cancer has grown. That's particularly important when it comes to the bladder's muscle layer, called the detrusor muscle. Doctors need to know whether cancer has reached this muscle because that can change the recommended treatment.
Removing a lesion intact may preserve more of the information pathologists need. It can also allow them to examine the tissue around the tumor more clearly. Dr. Duke Herrell, a urologic surgeon and CEO of Virtuoso Surgical, explained the potential benefit in the company's FDA announcement. "Removing a tumor intact can provide a better tissue specimen, which supports clearer diagnosis and staging," Herrell said. For patients, a more complete tissue sample could help their medical team determine the next steps with greater confidence.
Virtuoso has already tested the system in human patients, and the early clinical findings are encouraging. In the first 20 patients enrolled in the company-sponsored VIABLE study at The Chinese University of Hong Kong, 94% of removed lesions contained detrusor muscle. That exceeded the study's predefined performance goal of 60%. Researchers also reported that surgical margins could be evaluated in 93% of malignant lesions. Surgical margins are the edges of the removed tissue. Examining them can help doctors assess whether cancer cells extend to the edge of the sample. However, being able to evaluate a margin does not necessarily mean it is free of cancer. The company reported no adverse events during the operations.
There are important limitations to these findings. The study involved a small number of patients at one medical center. The previously published first phase of the same VIABLE study involved six patients and recorded two postoperative adverse events. One patient experienced temporary urinary retention, while another developed a chest infection later linked to a separate esophageal tumor. The company also compared its results with previously published research on conventional bladder tumor removal.
However, the Virtuoso study did not directly compare the robot against traditional instruments in a randomized trial. Researchers still need larger studies to determine whether the system improves long-term outcomes or reduces the need for additional procedures.
BRAIN TUMOR FOUND DURING PREVENTIVE SCAN PUTS FULL-BODY MRIS BACK IN THE SPOTLIGHT
The FDA granted De Novo authorization for the Virtuoso Endoscopy System on Oct. 30, 2026. The company publicly announced the decision on Nov. 10. The authorization establishes a new FDA classification for robotic surgical instruments that operate through an endoscope inside the body. Specifically, the system is authorized to remove bladder lesions in adult patients and obtain tissue samples, including bladder muscle, to assist in diagnosing bladder cancer .
The decision follows the FDA's September 2025 Breakthrough Device Designation for the system. That earlier designation recognized the technology's potential and allowed the company to receive additional regulatory guidance during development. However, the new authorization does not establish that the robot improves survival rates or prevents cancer from returning. The system must also be operated by trained surgeons in an operating room.
Virtuoso Surgical plans a limited U.S. launch in 2027, starting with leading urology centers. The company has not announced which hospitals will receive the system first. That means patients may have to wait before the technology becomes available at their local hospital. Questions also remain about pricing and insurance coverage.
Virtuoso is exploring other potential applications for its miniature robotic instruments, including procedures involving the lungs. However, those uses remain experimental and have not received FDA authorization. For now, the company's focus is bladder surgery, where better tissue samples could help doctors evaluate cancer more accurately.
If you or someone you love is facing bladder cancer, this technology could eventually provide another surgical option. Its miniature robotic arms may help doctors obtain more complete tissue samples during the initial procedure. However, availability will be limited at first, and the early results still need confirmation in larger studies. The robot's FDA authorization also does not guarantee better results for every patient.
If you're discussing bladder tumor surgery with a urologist, ask whether en bloc resection might be appropriate for your situation. You should also ask how the surgeon plans to obtain enough tissue to determine whether cancer has reached the bladder muscle. Those answers can help you understand your options before surgery.
When you're facing a possible cancer diagnosis, getting accurate answers as early as possible can make a real difference. That's what I like about this technology. Virtuoso's tiny robotic arms could help surgeons collect better tissue samples without taking control away from the medical professional performing the operation. It's also encouraging to see the FDA authorize a system designed for such a specific surgical challenge. Still, 20 patients represent a very small study, and I want to see how this robot performs in larger trials before getting too excited about its potential. If the results hold up, this could become a valuable addition to the tools doctors use to diagnose bladder cancer.
Would you trust a surgeon using this new robotic system to remove a tumor, or would you prefer a conventional procedure until there's more evidence of its benefits? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

articles.title: CE meets WorldSkills HK team
articles.excerpt: Chief Executive John Lee today officiated at a reception for Team Hong Kong from the 2026 Shanghai WorldSkills Competition, reception…
articles.fullText:
Chief Executive John Lee today officiated at a reception for Team Hong Kong from the 2026 Shanghai WorldSkills Competition, reception co-organised by the Government and the Vocational Training Council (VTC). He congratulated all contestants on their dedication and tireless efforts in preparing for and competing in the event.

Held in Shanghai from September 22 to 27, the 48th WorldSkills Competition saw the Hong Kong, China delegation send 41 competitors across 37 trades – setting new records for both team size and trade participation.

The delegation secured 15 awards in total, comprising a silver medal in Rail Vehicle Technology and 14 medallions for excellence across other trades.

In his remarks, Mr Lee noted that the event is hailed as the “Skills Olympics”, where Hong Kong’s representatives faced fierce competition from more than 1,400 contestants representing nearly 70 countries and regions.

He applauded the team for their superb craftsmanship and fighting spirit in achieving Hong Kong’s best-ever results, showcasing the outstanding talent of the city’s younger generation to the world and telling Hong Kong’s story through their actions.

The Chief Executive also pointed out that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan explicitly calls for promoting the high-quality development of vocational and professional education and training, calling it a vital pillar of the local education system.

He added that the Government is implementing the strategy of “fostering industry-institution collaboration and diversified development” to offer young people of varying aspirations and abilities flexible, high-quality pathways for learning and career advancement.

The Government will continue working closely with the VTC and all sectors of society to expand career opportunities for young people, enabling them to apply their skills and realise their potential, Mr Lee said.

During the reception, the award-winning competitors shared their competition experiences and insights.

Among them was Tang Kwong-tai, who won silver in Rail Vehicle Technology and was named Team Hong Kong’s top scorer. He said he felt deeply proud to stand on the podium and bring honour to Hong Kong, adding that the training and competition had been immensely beneficial to his railway engineering career.

articles.title: What really happens when you need help restoring your identity
articles.excerpt: Identity theft restoration involves credit freezes, fraud alerts and disputing fraudulent records. Here's how the recovery process works, step by…
articles.fullText:
Identity theft restoration takes more than one phone call. It often means securing accounts, documenting fraudulent activity and working with several companies to correct inaccurate records.
The term "identity restoration" can sound complicated until you suddenly need it. Maybe someone opened a credit card in your name, took over your bank account or used your personal information to get medical care. Now you're dealing with unfamiliar charges, paperwork and companies that all seem to have different requirements.
Fortunately, knowing what happens during recovery can make the process easier to manage. Here's how identity restoration typically works, what you may need to do yourself and where professional help can make a difference.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT
Identity restoration usually starts with understanding the problem. A specialist may ask when you first noticed suspicious activity, which accounts someone accessed and whether you lost money or personal information. These details help identify the type of identity theft involved. Someone opening a credit card in your name requires a different response than a criminal taking over your phone number or using your medical information. A restoration specialist can help you separate confirmed fraud from suspicious activity that still needs investigation. As a result, you can focus on the companies and accounts that need attention first.
Before tackling paperwork, focus on preventing additional damage. Depending on what happened, you may need to contact your bank, lock a credit card, change passwords or secure your mobile phone account. If someone accessed your email, make securing that account an early priority. Criminals can use compromised email accounts to reset passwords and gain access to other services. You may also want to place a fraud alert or freeze your credit.
Neither option fixes fraud that has already occurred. However, both can help reduce the risk of additional new-account fraud.
One of the most frustrating parts of identity theft recovery is having to explain the same problem repeatedly. A case file helps you keep track of important information and avoid starting over with every phone call. Include dates of suspicious activity, copies of statements, confirmation numbers, correspondence and the names of representatives you've contacted. Also, record what each company promised to do and when you should expect a response. This becomes especially helpful when several organizations are involved. For example, your bank might close an account while a fraudulent balance still appears on your credit report. Having documentation gives you a clear record of the steps you've already completed. Keep those records somewhere secure. Additionally, avoid sending sensitive documents through unverified email addresses or links.
Depending on the type of fraud, identity restoration may involve banks, creditors, credit bureaus, mobile carriers, medical providers or government agencies. Each organization follows its own procedures. A bank may ask you to complete a fraud affidavit, while a credit bureau may request an identity theft report before blocking fraudulent information. A restoration specialist can explain those requirements and help you navigate the process. In some situations, the specialist may also coordinate communications or work with institutions on your behalf. However, you may still need to verify your identity, provide documents or authorize certain actions. Restoration assistance helps you work through the process, but the affected institutions remain responsible for reviewing claims and correcting their records.
Once you secure your accounts and identify the affected organizations, the next step involves correcting the damage. If someone opened a fraudulent credit account, you may need to dispute the information with the creditor and the credit bureaus. The Federal Trade Commission recommends reporting identity theft through IdentityTheft.gov, where you can create an FTC Identity Theft Report and receive a personalized recovery plan. An FTC Identity Theft Report can also help you exercise important rights, including requesting that credit bureaus block information resulting from identity theft. Medical identity theft may require contacting healthcare providers and insurers to correct inaccurate records. Meanwhile, tax identity theft generally involves working directly with the IRS. Keep copies of every document you submit. Whenever possible, request written confirmation after an organization resolves an issue.
Identity theft recovery rarely happens all at once. Your bank might reverse a fraudulent transaction before a credit bureau finishes investigating a related account. Similarly, a phone carrier may restore your number, but you may still need to strengthen account security to prevent another takeover. That's why follow-ups are so important. Set reminders for promised responses and continue checking your statements, accounts and credit reports after the initial incident. You can review your credit reports for free each week at AnnualCreditReport.com. Even after you resolve a case, additional suspicious activity can surface if criminals continue trying to use your stolen information.
WAS YOUR IDENTITY STOLEN? WHAT TO DO IN THE FIRST 24 HOURS
Not every identity theft case follows the same path. The type of fraud determines which organizations need to get involved and what steps you should take. For example, new-account fraud often involves creditors and credit bureaus. An existing bank-account takeover requires immediate attention from the financial institution, while medical identity theft may involve correcting treatment and billing records. Tax or government benefits fraud can require separate reporting procedures. And if a scammer convinced you to authorize a payment, your options may differ from those available for unauthorized account transactions. That's why identifying the problem early is important. A credit freeze may help protect against new credit accounts, but it cannot correct a medical record or recover money sent to a scammer.
Identity theft recovery can feel slow, especially when you're waiting for several companies to respond. However, you can track progress by focusing on specific actions rather than expecting everything to happen immediately. Have you secured the compromised account? Did you report the fraudulent charge? Has the credit bureau acknowledged your dispute? Each completed step helps move the case forward. If a company misses a deadline or provides conflicting information, your case file will help you explain the situation without starting the conversation from scratch.
Before speaking with a restoration specialist or fraud department, gather any suspicious statements, letters, alerts or emails connected to the incident. The company may also ask you to provide identification, an FTC Identity Theft Report or written authorization allowing someone to assist with your case. Always verify that you're communicating with the legitimate organization before sharing sensitive information. Also, ask why a document is necessary and how the company plans to handle it. Ultimately, you should understand what information you're providing and what actions someone may take on your behalf.
If you've experienced identity theft, handling multiple disputes and follow-up calls yourself can become overwhelming. That's where an identity protection service may help. Some services provide access to identity restoration specialists who can guide you through the recovery process. Depending on the provider and your plan, specialists may help organize documentation, explain next steps and assist with communications involving affected institutions.
Identity protection services may also monitor certain personal information, credit reports and financial accounts. Alerts can help you discover suspicious activity before it leads to additional problems. However, identity monitoring cannot detect every form of fraud, and restoration assistance cannot guarantee that every dispute will end in your favor. The benefit comes from having experienced support when you're trying to work through a complicated situation.
Beyond restoration assistance, some identity protection services offer tools that help you identify suspicious activity, reduce the exposure of personal information and respond when something looks wrong. Features vary by provider and plan, so it's worth checking what's included before signing up.
Some services offer tools that help you identify merchants and websites that may have your payment card information on file. Reviewing these connections can help you decide where to remove stored payment details, especially if you no longer use certain accounts. However, these tools cannot automatically confirm whether someone has stolen your card information.
Certain identity protection services can monitor eligible financial accounts and flag transactions that appear unusual or potentially fraudulent. These might include unfamiliar purchases or unexpected charges. An alert gives you an opportunity to review the transaction and contact your financial institution if necessary. Keep in mind that these services may not detect every suspicious transaction.
Some identity protection services include tools that search covered data broker websites for your personal information and submit removal requests on your behalf. Reducing publicly available information may help limit your exposure to identity theft and scams. However, no removal service can erase your information from every website or guarantee that it will never reappear.
Some providers offer access to support specialists or online tools that can help you evaluate suspicious messages, websites and financial activity. Depending on the service, you may receive guidance on reporting scams, securing accounts and taking steps to recover from identity theft.
Certain plans may also include reimbursement benefits for eligible losses or expenses, subject to coverage limits and exclusions. However, these services cannot guarantee that you'll recover money you sent to a scammer. Always review the terms before relying on a particular benefit.
See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com
When someone steals your identity, discovering the fraud is often only the beginning. The real work comes afterward, when you're trying to secure accounts, correct records and get answers from companies handling different parts of the problem. I've always believed that knowing what to do next can make a stressful situation much easier to handle. Start by protecting the accounts you still control, document everything and use the free recovery tools available through the FTC. If you want additional help, an identity protection service with restoration specialists may help you navigate the recovery process and stay organized. No service can promise an instant fix, but having experienced support can make a difference when you're dealing with identity theft.

articles.title: Cruise industry sails into new era with vessel's debut
articles.excerpt: China's second domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, embarked on its maiden voyage on Sunday, marking a new…
articles.fullText:
China's second domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, embarked on its maiden voyage on Sunday, marking a new step in the country's efforts to expand cruise tourism and boost consumption.

Carrying more than 3,800 passengers, the ship departed from Guangzhou on a six-day, five-night journey to Hong Kong and Hue, Vietnam.

Measuring 341 metres in length and with a gross tonnage of 141,900, the vessel has 2,130 cabins and can accommodate up to 5,232 passengers.

Construction of Adora Flora City began in August 2022. Operated by Adora Cruises under China Tourism Group, it was delivered in Shanghai on November 6 and embarked on its first trial voyage on November 9.

Shi Dai, chairperson of China Tourism Group, said the company is using cruise operations to drive the development of integrated cultural tourism products and travel experiences, aiming to set a new benchmark for vacations at sea.

Adora Flora City is larger and features a more streamlined design than its sister ship, Adora Magic City, China's first domestically built large cruise ship.

Adora Magic City began commercial operations in January 2024 and has since completed about 250 voyages.

Hu Zhenyu, deputy director of the Qianhai branch of the China Development Institute, said the entry into service of two domestically built large cruise ships marks a new phase for China's cruise industry.

The development will not only expand the range of high-quality marine tourism products but also create new drivers of consumption in coastal areas, Hu said.

In 2027, Adora Flora City is scheduled to undertake over 50 international voyages from its home port in Guangzhou, offering both short getaways and longer itineraries to destinations including Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.

The ship will also offer voyages with no scheduled port calls, allowing passengers to enjoy the cruise ship as a destination in itself.

On Sunday, the vessel departed from the Guangzhou Nansha International Cruise Home Port, one of China's largest integrated cruise port complexes.

A duty-free store at the terminal also opened, adding a fresh shopping option for cruise passengers.

The maiden voyage comes as China seeks to expand tourism consumption.

A 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for cultural and tourism development calls for boosting spending on cruise and yacht tours, among other specialised tourism offerings. (Reporting by Xinhua)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: China slams US curbs on phone numbers access
articles.excerpt: China on Sunday called on the United States to revoke proposed restrictions on Chinese telecom operators' direct access to US…
articles.fullText:
China on Sunday called on the United States to revoke proposed restrictions on Chinese telecom operators' direct access to US phone numbers, saying the move violates the principles of non-discrimination and fair competition.

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) abused its regulatory powers and overstretched the concept of national security, while making arbitrary accusations against Chinese telecom companies without factual basis and maliciously undermining their operations in the United States, a Commerce Ministry spokesperson noted in response to a media query.

Affected entities include China's three biggest telecom firms: China Unicom, China Telecom and China Mobile.

The FCC has recently continued to push to decouple and sever supply chains between China and the United States in telecommunications, communications, testing and certification, the spokesperson added.

Such moves run counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and undermine the stability of China-US economic and trade relations, the spokesperson said.

China urges the United States to immediately rescind the measures and return to the right way of resolving issues through consultations, the spokesperson said, noting that China will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own interests.

The criticism by Beijing comes after President Xi Jinping hosted his US counterpart Donald Trump at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, where Xi hailed "stable and improved" ties with Washington. (Xinhua, with additional reporting by AFP)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Messi furore after Columbus thrash Miami in MLS Cup
articles.excerpt: Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent…
articles.fullText:
Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after hurling a throw-in at an opponent as Inter Miami crashed to a 3-0 defeat in the MLS Cup playoffs on Saturday.

Messi's frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he aimed a forceful throw-in into the face of Columbus Crew forward Gonzalo Tapia with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.

Messi and Tapia both were shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.

"Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card," Courtois said in a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. "It's just really sad."

Referee Chapman later defended the decision to only show Messi a yellow.

"The force used was negligible and the offence did not reach the level of violent conduct," Chapman told a pool reporter.

Inter Miami had already been reduced to 10 men when the incident occurred and were 1-0 down after Chile international Tapia's early penalty.

Reigning MLS champions Miami went on to suffer a 3-0 defeat, with Tapia grabbing a second after a Taha Habroune strike just after half-time at Miami's Nu Stadium.

The result means seventh seeds Columbus, the 2023 champions, can eliminate Messi and Miami from the playoffs with a victory in game two of the best-of-three series in Ohio next Friday.

"It was a game where nothing went right for us, and we effectively created their chances for them," Miami coach Kily Gonzalez said afterwards.

"We didn't produce the great performance we had hoped for. Everything went wrong, but we have to learn from it because next time, if we don't win, we're out," he added.

"There's no better challenge for us as a team than this. It's a test of character, and I know my team has that character."

In other MLS playoff action on Saturday, Joaquin Valiente scored two goals as host Dallas beat Portland 3-0 in their Western Conference series opener.

The 25-year-old Uruguayan midfielder scored in the 53rd and 55th minutes and Samuel Sarver added an insurance goal in the fourth minute of stoppage time for Dallas, who can advance by winning at Portland next Saturday.

US teen Peyton Miller scored one goal and set up another in New England's 2-0 victory over visiting Philadelphia.

Miller's 10th-minute shot deflected in off Philadelphia defender Nathan Harriel to make it 1-0 and the 19-year-old scored in the 73rd minute off a Jack Harrison cross to complete the scoring.

New England can advance to the MLS Eastern Conference semi-finals with a road victory next Saturday. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Itoje hails England after big win over All Blacks
articles.excerpt: Northern hemisphere sides are continuing to lay down a marker ahead of next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia, with…
articles.fullText:
Northern hemisphere sides are continuing to lay down a marker ahead of next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia, with both New Zealand and South Africa falling to defeat for a second week in a row.

England captain Maro Itoje said he was delighted by the team's growth after a record 37-12 win over New Zealand in a Nations Championship clash at Twickenham on Saturday.

Itoje's team ran in five tries, three in the first half alone, as Henry Slade, Jack van Poortvliet and player-of-the-match Ben Earl all went over before Ollie Chessum and Seb Atkinson crossed in the second half.

England's 25-point winning margin surpassed their previous best against the All Blacks of 17 points achieved in a 38-21 success at Twickenham in 2012.

This win — just England's 10th in 48 Tests against New Zealand — was also the first time in more than 20 years they had enjoyed successive victories over the All Blacks following last year's 33-19 triumph at Twickenham.

England have now won all three of their November Nations Championship clashes following dominant defeats of Australia and Japan.

"We had a fast start again and the guys coming off the bench, all those guys, the impact they made was unbelievable," Itoje said.

The All Blacks were back to full-strength following last week's stunning 35-28 defeat by Wales — their first loss to the Welsh in 73 years.

But the All Blacks managed just two tries on Saturday, with recalled captain Codie Taylor telling Sky Sport: "We were just really inaccurate tonight."

The hooker added: "We put ourselves under pressure, England put us under pressure, and when we had our opportunities, we either gave the ball away or made errors."

New Zealand great Beauden Barrett marked becoming just the fourth man to appear in 150 Tests with a second-half try but the full-back admitted he did not know what to say after a thumping loss.

"Deflated's one word, disappointed. They were simply too good, and it's a tough one," he said.

"I don't know where to start."

Meanwhile, in Dublin, two first-half tries from Rob Baloucoune helped a rejuvenated Ireland beat South Africa 20-17, but a losing bonus point was enough to book the world champions a place in next weekend's Nations Championship final.

With Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus watching on from his hotel serving the first of a six-match ban, Ireland dominated the first period and led the subdued Springboks 17-10 at halftime thanks to Baloucoune's tries and one from Ronan Kelleher.

A Sam Prendergast penalty stretched the lead to 10 points and while a Malcolm Marx try cut it to three just before the hour, the Springboks could not breach the brilliant Irish defence and fell to back-to-back defeats.

In Edinburgh, Darcy Graham and Liam McConnell each bagged a hat-trick of tries as Scotland thrashed Japan 67-5 in the Nations Championship in Edinburgh.

After beating Australia last weekend, the Scots totally outclassed Eddie Jones' Japan team.

Graham scored the hosts' first of 11 tries after five minutes in a one-sided contest.

Kyle Rowe, Ollie Smith (2), Jamie Dobie and Rory Hutchinson also crossed the whitewash, Tom Jordan and George Horne shared six conversions between them.

Japan's sole points came from a try by Takuro Matsunaga after Rowe let a long punt bounce. (Agencies)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: China ready to speed up Singapore FTA talks: Premier
articles.excerpt: Premier Li Qiang said China stands ready to work with Singapore to accelerate negotiations on the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement…
articles.fullText:
Premier Li Qiang said China stands ready to work with Singapore to accelerate negotiations on the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (FTA) 4.0 and promote a higher level of two-way opening-up.

Li made the remarks on Saturday during talks with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Beijing.

China and Singapore signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Shenzhen on Friday to launch negotiations on upgrading the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement.

Key focus areas include the digital economy, greater cooperation and market access in public procurement, as well as emerging sectors like artificial intelligence.

Li said China is willing to strengthen strategic communication with Singapore, consolidate political mutual trust, support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns, and expand practical cooperation.

Noting that China and Singapore share similar approaches to social governance and face many common challenges, Li called for greater exchanges and mutual learning to address an aging population, promote balanced development and improve public services.

Wong, for his part, said Singapore looks forward to maintaining closer high-level exchanges with China, strengthening the alignment of development strategies, deepening cooperation in areas such as AI, the digital economy, green energy and connectivity, and enhancing people-to-people and cultural exchanges.

The Singaporean leader also congratulated China on successfully hosting the Apec summit. (Xinhua/Agencies)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: $500M investment could bring AI robots to your workplace
articles.excerpt: Genesis AI raised $500 million to expand its general-purpose robot Eno, which learns physical skills from workers wearing special electronic…
articles.fullText:
What if a robot could learn how to do your job simply by watching you work? That's what Genesis AI is working toward, and some of the biggest names in tech are betting big on it. The robotics company has raised $500 million to bring its general-purpose robot, Eno, into more workplaces. The investment values Genesis at $3.5 billion and puts some serious financial muscle behind its plans.
But what really caught my attention is how these robots learn. Genesis is developing technology that allows people to teach robots physical skills without having to program every movement. Workers wear special electronic gloves while doing their regular jobs. The gloves capture their hand movements and turn that information into training data that helps robots learn to perform similar tasks.
Eventually, Genesis wants these robots to handle complex work without someone constantly supervising them. The company plans to bring Eno to customer sites in 2027, starting with industrial workplaces. So, how close are we to robots that can actually do our jobs, and what happens to the people teaching them? Let's take a closer look.
AI BUILDS VIRTUAL HOMES WHERE ROBOTS LEARN FROM THEIR MISTAKES

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
Genesis AI announced a $500 million Series A funding round at a $3.5 billion post-money valuation. Premji Invest, Khosla Ventures and Eclipse co-led the investment. Other backers include Nvidia, AMD Ventures, Samsung Next and Zoom. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, Zoom CEO Eric Yuan and Yahoo co-founder Jerry Yang are also among the investors. T. Rowe Price-advised accounts and several other major financial and technology firms participated. That's a significant vote of confidence in a company developing robots that can perform physical work across different environments.
Genesis plans to use the funding to expand robot training and improve its artificial intelligence . The company is also increasing production of Eno while hiring additional researchers and robotics engineers. 
"Our mission is to remove the physical limits on human ambition," said Zhou Xian, co-founder and CEO of Genesis AI. The company wants to move beyond robots programmed to repeat a single task. Its larger goal is to build machines that can adapt to changing conditions and eventually handle entire workflows.
Eno takes a different approach from humanoid robots designed to closely resemble people. Genesis has focused on giving the machine useful physical capabilities rather than recreating every aspect of human appearance. The robot combines dexterous hands with a body designed for practical work. Its hands can handle tools and objects that require careful control, while its AI helps it respond to different physical tasks.
At the center of the technology is GENE, the company's AI foundation model, which acts as the robotic brain. The system helps robots interpret their surroundings and control precise physical movements. We previously covered Genesis AI's robotic brain and its ability to perform complex hand movements.
Now, the company is working to bring that intelligence into Eno for commercial use. For now, Genesis has demonstrated several advanced skills using a test robot powered by GENE. Those capabilities are expected to move to Eno as development continues.
How does a robot learn to handle delicate objects or perform tasks that require precise finger movements? We asked Genesis AI co-founder and President Théophile Gervet to explain how its electronic gloves make that possible.
"The electronic gloves are worn while people are performing their regular work so we can collect massive amounts of real-world data about how humans perform physical tasks in order to train GENE, our robotic brain," Gervet explained. 
"The gloves capture detailed finger movements and the pressure applied when handling different materials. Genesis designed its robotic hands to closely match human hands, creating what the company calls a 1:1:1 mapping between the human hand, glove and robotic hand. This process enables Eno to learn complex physical skills without having to manually program every movement.
Genesis also uses small cameras worn on workers' heads to record tasks from their point of view. 
"This lets GENE see exactly what someone sees as they perform a task, including how they use their hands and interact with their surroundings," Gervet said. The company also trains GENE using existing videos of people performing physical work. Together, these sources help the AI develop more complex physical skills.
Genesis has another training advantage. Its robots can practice inside Genesis World, a simulation platform that recreates physical environments. For example, a robot learning to play the piano can study movements collected from someone wearing the electronic gloves. It can then repeatedly practice those movements inside a virtual environment.
Gervet explained how the training process can speed up learning. 
"Also, instead of practicing at the piano for an hour or so a day like you and I might, the robot can train in our hyperrealistic simulation, Genesis World, helping it master its task, like playing the piano, much quicker than it would in the real world." 
That approach allows developers to test movements without relying entirely on expensive physical training sessions.
AUTONOMOUS EXCAVATORS ARE DIGGING WITH EMPTY CABS
Genesis has demonstrated its GENE robotic brain performing several complex activities. These include preparing meals, handling laboratory equipment and assembling wire harnesses. Gervet also cited manipulating a Rubik's Cube as an example of a skill learned through human demonstrations. These activities require precise control of robotic hands.
However, there's an important detail here. These demonstrations currently use a test robot rather than Eno itself. 
"Today, GENE allows robots to tackle a wide variety of tasks, including preparing a meal, lab pipetting, wire harnessing, packaging and more. These tasks are currently being demonstrated in a test robot and will be exported over to Eno very soon," Gervet told us.
That means Genesis still needs to show how well Eno performs these skills during extended operation in actual workplaces. One investor says the technology has already shown encouraging progress. 
"What stood out to us was watching Genesis robots complete long, multi-step tasks on their own at the same speed a person would, with smooth and natural movement," said Vedant Agrawal, partner at Premji Invest.
Genesis began proof-of-concept projects and customer pilots in 2026. Now, the company is preparing to bring what it learned into its next phase of commercial deployment. 
"We started proof of concepts and pilots with customers in 2026 and received valuable insight by working with the customers. Now we are taking these lessons learned and heading to customer sites in 2027," Gervet told us.
 The first deployments will focus on manufacturing facilities, logistics operations and laboratories. Genesis has also announced a strategic partnership with LG CNS , LG's consulting and AI transformation business.
The companies plan to evaluate Genesis robots for manufacturing and logistics work at LG operations in the United States. Their partnership could eventually expand to additional industrial customers. 
Gervet confirmed the relationship and said, "We will share more on our work with them in the coming months." 
After industrial deployments, Genesis plans to expand into hospitality and healthcare. Home robots and outdoor applications are further down its development roadmap. However, the company has not announced a firm timeline for bringing Eno into people's homes.
As Genesis works toward robots that can handle entire workflows independently, there's an important question about the employees helping train them. Could those same robots eventually take over some of their jobs? We asked Genesis how employees participate in its training program and who owns the data collected through the electronic gloves and cameras. The company says participation is voluntary and that people involved specifically agree to the work. 
"All employees who participate in data collection have chosen to opt in and have agreed and consented," Genesis told CyberGuy.
The company added that participants understand how the information is collected and that Genesis does not capture personally identifying information. It also says people receive clear information before providing consent. As for ownership, Genesis was direct: "We own the training data that we capture with our gloves and cameras."
That answers an important question about the program. However, the larger issue remains how this technology could eventually affect employment. Workers may voluntarily help train robots today, but those same machines could eventually perform some of their responsibilities without constant human supervision.
Teaching a robot to perform an impressive task under controlled conditions is one thing. Making that same robot work reliably every day inside a busy workplace is another. Industrial environments change constantly. Equipment moves, objects may end up in unexpected locations and people work nearby.
For general-purpose robots to become practical, they need to respond safely when something goes wrong. Genesis believes developing its hardware and AI together will help address those challenges. The company also controls its training systems and simulation technology, allowing engineers to improve different components together. But the biggest unanswered questions involve long-term performance.
Genesis has not provided detailed commercial pricing or independently verified reliability results for Eno across extended customer deployments. Gervet acknowledged the challenge when discussing the future of robotics. "The challenge is making sure these robots can operate reliably and safely in the real world, not just perform impressive demonstrations in controlled environments." Those are exactly the questions businesses will need answered before trusting robots with more responsibility.
You probably won't see an Eno robot rolling into your workplace tomorrow. However, this technology offers an early look at how physical jobs could change over the next several years. If you work in manufacturing or a laboratory, robots like Eno could eventually handle tasks that require constant repetition. That could reduce physically demanding work while changing the skills employers expect from their teams.
For employees, the bigger question is how companies will introduce these machines. Will robots work alongside existing teams, or will businesses eventually use them to reduce staffing? Genesis sees opportunities to make workplaces more productive, but the long-term impact on jobs remains uncertain.
For people outside those industries, the longer-term possibilities include robots that help with household chores or assist in healthcare settings. Those applications remain further away and will require additional safety testing.
HYUNDAI TO SEND 25,000 ATLAS ROBOTS TO THE US
There's something fascinating about the idea of teaching robots to do our jobs simply by putting on a pair of electronic gloves. But I can't help wondering what happens when those robots become capable of performing the same work without us. That's a conversation I think we need to start having now, before this technology becomes commonplace. The $500 million investment shows how much confidence major tech investors have in Genesis AI. 
The company has ambitious plans to bring Eno into workplaces, and we're getting closer to seeing how robots like these could change the way businesses operate. Genesis says people participating in its training program voluntarily opt in, which is important. But I think there's still a bigger conversation to have about what happens after these robots learn the job. If companies eventually use them to take over certain responsibilities, employees deserve to understand how that could affect their future.
Would you be comfortable wearing special gloves that teach a robot how to do your job if that same robot could eventually replace you? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan customer data leaked
articles.excerpt: JPMorgan Chase says hackers accessed marketing data at third-party vendors as an extortion group leaks records tied to Visa and…
articles.fullText:
You trust your bank to protect your money. But how much do you know about the outside companies that also handle your personal information? That's a question worth asking after a ransomware group leaked customer data linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase.
On Nov. 19, 2026, The Wall Street Journal reported that hackers had leaked information allegedly linked to thousands of customers of the three financial companies. The reported exposure involved third-party service providers that work with financial companies. Now, customers are left wondering what information hackers obtained and whether they need to take action.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.
A SCAMMER HAS YOUR NAME, PHONE NUMBER AND ADDRESS; WHAT CAN THEY ACTUALLY DO?
Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
A cyber extortion group known as n0n claimed to have stolen information associated with the three financial companies. According to Reuters, the group posted claims on Nov. 16 about obtaining cardholder engagement records. These allegedly included extensive marketing activity associated with tens of thousands of email addresses. The group also posted claims involving Visa and Mastercard that same day.
The reported cyberattack involved outside service providers that handle information for financial institutions. Some of the records appear connected to customer marketing activities and cardholder benefit programs. However, several important questions remain unanswered. The companies have not publicly identified all the affected vendors, and investigators have yet to establish whether one compromised provider was responsible for all three reported exposures.
JPMorgan Chase confirmed that third-party service providers were targeted in a cyberattack. In a statement to CyberGuy, a JPMorgan Chase spokesperson said, "Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses."
The bank says its services remain operational. It also plans to contact affected customers where appropriate and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring. Addressing the transaction processing delays that affected multiple banks earlier this week, the spokesperson added, "There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week."
According to Reuters, leaked records appeared to contain more than 16,000 JPMorgan Chase customer email addresses and 124 bank employee email addresses. Some entries also included phone numbers and postal codes. Reuters could not independently verify the authenticity of the records.
Mastercard also acknowledged an incident involving an outside provider. However, the company says the exposed information was limited to email addresses belonging to a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program. In a statement to CyberGuy, Mastercard said the incident involved non-payment information.
"There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards," Mastercard said.
The company also confirmed that the exposure has been contained. Its teams are working with the affected provider to support cardholders as needed. Mastercard has not publicly identified the benefit program involved or disclosed an exact number of affected customers. The company also has not indicated that payment card numbers were exposed.
Visa has responded to CyberGuy about the reported cybersecurity incident involving a third-party service provider in the Asia-Pacific region. The company says its own systems and payment information were unaffected.
In a statement, the company said, "Visa is aware of these claims. They are associated with an incident involving a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific. Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected. This is unrelated to any of the system disruptions across different industries this past week."
However, Visa has not identified the service provider or disclosed how many customers may have been affected. The company also has not specified what non-payment information, if any, was exposed.
So far, the companies' statements point primarily to customer information held by outside service providers. Mastercard says its payment network remains secure, while Visa says payment card numbers were unaffected. JPMorgan Chase has identified potentially exposed marketing data. There has been no verified indication that customer banking passwords were stolen or that hackers accessed funds through this incident.
However, stolen contact information can still create problems. Criminals may use names or email addresses to make phishing messages appear more convincing. You could receive an email claiming your bank detected suspicious activity related to the recent cyberattack. The message might direct you to a fake website designed to steal your login information. We've covered how convincing these scams can be in our article about fake bank security alerts that trick customers into sharing personal information.
9 WARNING SIGNS OF IDENTITY THEFT YOU SHOULD NEVER IGNORE
You do not need to assume your account has been compromised. However, there are several practical steps I recommend taking to reduce your exposure to follow-up scams.
Be cautious of unexpected emails or text messages claiming your Visa, Mastercard or JPMorgan Chase account needs immediate attention. Scammers may reference a real cyberattack to make their messages more convincing. They could also claim that your card will be suspended unless you verify your information. Don't click links or open attachments in suspicious messages. 
Instead, open your bank's official app or type its website address directly into your browser. You can also call the number printed on the back of your card. Using strong antivirus software can provide additional protection by helping detect malicious links and downloads before they cause damage. Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com
A scammer may call pretending to be from your bank's fraud department. The caller might already know your name or email address and claim that a recent breach put your account at risk. The scammer may then ask you to read back a one-time verification code sent to your phone. 
That code could allow someone to access your account or approve an unauthorized transaction. Never share a verification code with someone who contacts you unexpectedly. Also, never transfer money to another account because a caller claims it will keep your funds safe. Legitimate bank representatives will not ask you to move your money to a supposedly safe account.
Enable transaction notifications through your bank or credit card app. These alerts can help you spot unfamiliar purchases without waiting for your monthly statement. Check your recent activity and report anything suspicious immediately. Even though the companies have not reported a compromise of their payment networks, monitoring your accounts remains a useful security habit.
Make sure your banking and primary email accounts use unique passwords. If you have reused passwords across accounts, replace them with strong alternatives. A password manager can help you generate and store them securely. Turn on multifactor authentication wherever available. If your bank supports passkeys or security keys, consider using them. 
An authenticator app is generally a stronger option than SMS codes, although it can still be vulnerable to certain phishing attacks. There is currently no verified evidence that passwords were exposed in this incident. These precautions can help protect your accounts against separate attacks. For more details, see our guide to whether bank text codes are enough to protect you.
JPMorgan Chase says it will contact affected customers where appropriate and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring. If you receive a breach notification, confirm that it came from your financial institution before clicking an enrollment link or sharing personal information. Credit monitoring can help you identify suspicious changes to your credit reports. However, it cannot stop someone from sending phishing emails or impersonating your bank. You should also be suspicious of anyone demanding payment to activate complimentary protection offered after a breach.
A credit freeze makes it harder for criminals to open new credit accounts in your name. You can place one for free through Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. You must contact each credit bureau separately. A freeze does not affect your credit score, and you can temporarily lift it when you need to apply for credit. If only your name and email address were exposed, a freeze may not be necessary because of this incident alone. However, it can provide broader protection, especially if a breach involves more sensitive identifiers such as a Social Security number.
An exposed email address becomes more useful to scammers when they can connect it with other personal details found online. Consider removing unnecessary information from public profiles and checking what data broker websites have collected about you. A personal data removal service can also help request the removal of information from participating people-search sites. These services cannot erase information already stolen in a cyberattack. 
However, reducing the amount of personal information publicly available may make it harder for criminals to build convincing profiles for targeted scams. You should also use your phone's spam filtering features and reputable antivirus software to help block suspicious messages or malicious downloads. Get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web: Cyberguy.com
If you clicked a suspicious banking link or shared personal information, take action quickly. What you do next depends on what happened.
You can also report suspected fraud through ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
I've always believed that protecting your financial information requires knowing who has access to it. This latest incident shows how complicated that has become. You can do everything right with your bank account, yet an outside company handling your personal information could still experience a cyberattack. Most of us have little say in which vendors our financial institutions use, and we rarely know how much information those companies collect. 
I appreciate that Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase provided statements about the incident. It's reassuring that payment services remain operational, but I'd like to see more transparency about the outside providers involved and exactly what customer information they were holding. Until we have those answers, I would pay close attention to unexpected messages claiming to be from a financial institution. If someone contacts you about a problem with your account, verify it yourself before taking action.
If your bank shares your personal information with outside companies, shouldn't you have a right to know exactly who has it? And would a data leak like this make you reconsider which financial institutions you trust? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com
